providers.description: Kakao Entertainment Corp. is the South Korean entertainment subsidiary of Kakao Corp., formed from the 2021 merger of Kakao Page and Kakao M. It operates three business lines — Story (Kakao Page and Kakao Webtoon serialized webtoon and web-novel platforms, plus the overseas Tapas and Radish properties), Music (the Melon streaming service and the StarShip, IST, EDAM and Antenna labels), and Media (film, drama and artist management). Its public machine-readable API surface is agent-native rather than REST: Melon publishes a first-party remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server at https://mcp.melon.com/mcp, in beta, exposing 18 anonymously-introspectable tools for music search, official Melon charts, artist and album detail, genre browsing, personalized DJ Mallang recommendations, listening history and playlist/playback URL generation. Access is authenticated with OAuth 2.0 against the Melon Alliance Auth v3 platform, which publishes RFC 8414 authorization server metadata and an RFC 7591 dynamic client registration endpoint. Kakao Entertainment publishes no OpenAPI, no REST developer portal, and no SDKs; the corporate site and the Melon consumer properties carry no developer program. Kakao Corp's general developer platform at developers.kakao.com belongs to the parent company and is profiled separately as `kakao`.

providers.name: SoundHound
providers.description: SoundHound AI is a voice AI and audio intelligence platform offering the Houndify conversational voice assistant API and a music fingerprint identification API. Developers can build voice-enabled applications using HTTP and WebSocket endpoints that accept audio or text queries and return structured JSON, powered by SoundHound's proprietary Speech-to-Meaning and Deep Meaning Understanding technologies.

providers.name: Curalate
providers.description: Curalate provides a visual commerce platform that enables brands and retailers to harness user‑generated content, shoppable photos, and influencer marketing to drive sales. After being acquired by Bazaarvoice, Curalate’s technology integrates with Bazaarvoice’s suite to deliver social commerce solutions, allowing shoppers to purchase directly from images and videos across web and mobile experiences. The platform offers analytics, content moderation, and campaign tools for marketers seeking authentic, visual-driven engagement.

providers.name: Melty
providers.description: Melty is a French digital media brand for youth culture — news and entertainment coverage of series, cinema, television, celebrity, gaming and lifestyle aimed at a 15-34 audience. Founded in 2008 in Paris and operated by EEPLE SAS, Melty was a Serena Capital portfolio company before Reworld Media acquired 100% of the business in a distressed M&A process completed in 2021-2022; melty.fr is now published by EEPLE within Groupe Reworld Media and monetised through advertising and native content rather than software licensing. Melty publishes no developer program, no public API product and no machine-readable API contract. Its only public developer surface is the meltygroup GitHub organisation, which carries the identity servers Kisee and Pasee — MIT-licensed, self-hosted Python HTTP API servers written in-house and released to PyPI, last published in 2021.

providers.name: Boonful
providers.description: Boonful is a publishing platform that enables creators to build, sell, and manage digital products such as books, courses, videos, podcasts, newsletters, and apps. It offers tools for product creation, audience discovery, payment processing via Stripe, and automated marketing features. The service emphasizes a no‑code approach, AI‑assisted content generation, and integrated scheduling across social channels, aiming to help creators monetize their work without technical barriers.

providers.name: Bandmixr
providers.description: Bandmixr is an AI mixing and mastering service for producers, artists and bands. Upload your stems and get a finished, streaming‑ready song in minutes. The platform offers automated mixing, genre‑aware EQ, compression, mastering presets, and tools like Mix Analyzer, Stem Separator, and Rehearsal Cutter. Pricing starts free with paid plans up to $19 per month, providing flexible options for creators.

providers.name: Ecamm
providers.description: Ecamm provides powerful live streaming and video production software for macOS, enabling creators to stream, record, and present with professional features such as multi-camera support, scene composition, green screen effects, and integration with platforms like Stream Deck. Their flagship product, Ecamm Live, offers a user-friendly interface for live broadcasting, podcasting, and video creation, targeting both individual creators and businesses seeking high-quality video content.

providers.name: StoryCut
providers.description: StoryCut provides an AI-powered platform that automatically creates short, viral‑ready videos for TikTok, Reels, Shorts and other social channels. Users upload long‑form video content and the service extracts key moments, adds dynamic captions, auto‑reframes, and applies transitions, all within seconds. The platform offers multiple caption styles, AI‑generated B‑Roll, and tools for branding, targeting creators, businesses and marketers looking to boost engagement across short‑form video platforms.

providers.name: U.S. Agency for Global Media
providers.description: The U.S. Agency for Global Media (USAGM) is an independent federal agency that oversees a network of international media organizations aimed at providing news and information to audiences around the world in support of freedom and democracy. These media outlets include Voice of America (VOA), Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty (RFE/RL), Radio Free Asia (RFA), Office of Cuba Broadcasting (OCB), Middle East Broadcasting Networks (MBN), and the Open Technology Fund (OTF). Together these entities operate in over 64 languages and reach approximately 427 million people weekly, producing more than 3,000 hours of original programming per week in regions where access to a free press is limited.

providers.name: Botika
providers.description: Botika is an AI fashion-photography platform that helps online clothing and e-commerce brands replace traditional model photoshoots with generative AI. It turns flat-lay, mannequin, and basic on-model product photos into studio-quality images featuring fully AI-generated fashion models, poses, and on-brand backgrounds. Founded by Eran Dagan and Yarin Didi Meir and backed by an $8M seed round with participation from Seedcamp, Botika ships a web console, a native Shopify app, and an iOS app, cutting photoshoot costs by up to 90% and speeding time-to-market roughly 3x. A public API is on the company roadmap but is not yet released, so this profile currently captures company identity and public web properties rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: CrowdMade
providers.description: CrowdMade partners with online creators from YouTube, Instagram, Snapchat and beyond to design, produce, warehouse, and ship official merchandise their fans are proud to wear. The public storefront at crowdmade.com runs on Shopify and, as of 2026, exposes a machine- and agent-facing commerce surface: a published Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) MCP shopping endpoint, Shopify Customer Accounts OpenID Connect / OAuth discovery documents, an llms.txt, and an agents.md describing how AI shopping agents can search the catalog, build a cart, and complete a buyer-approved checkout. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and profiled into the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Eastman Kodak
providers.description: Eastman Kodak Company is a global commercial printing and imaging company that provides hardware, software, consumables, and services to customers in the print, packaging, publishing, manufacturing, and entertainment industries. Kodak does not currently publish a public developer program or API portfolio.

providers.name: Microsoft Sway
providers.description: Microsoft Sway is a presentation and storytelling application that enables creating interactive, web-based content. It integrates with Microsoft 365 for sharing and embedding interactive presentations, newsletters, and reports across an organization.

providers.name: Ziff Davis Enterprise
providers.description: Ziff Davis (Nasdaq: ZD) is a vertically focused digital media and internet company whose portfolio includes leading brands across technology, entertainment, shopping, health, cybersecurity, and marketing technology. Its brands include PCMag, Mashable, IGN, Lifehacker, RetailMeNot, Spiceworks, Everyday Health, IPVanish, Ookla (Speedtest), FullContact, and iContact, among others. The company operates a portfolio of advertising, subscription, and performance-marketing businesses rather than a single first-party public API product. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced as an Insight Partners portfolio lead; a public web crawl of the corporate site found an active investor-relations, newsroom, brands, privacy, and terms surface but no developer portal, API reference, or published API specification at the corporate (ziffdavis.com) level. A second enrichment pass on 2026-08-13 ran full contract discovery against www.ziffdavis.com — OpenAPI, Swagger, GraphQL, MCP, llms.txt and every /.well-known/ path returned 404, and the WordPress REST root returned 401 — confirming the absence, while surfacing three real corporate programs: a Bugcrowd-hosted Responsible Vulnerability Disclosure Program, a published data-protection compliance program (Data Privacy Framework self-certification for 32 named group entities, GDPR DPAs, CCPA request metrics, EU DSA statement, NIST SP 800-88 vendor security exhibit), and five first-party PHP packages in the ziffdavis Packagist namespace — none of which is an API client library. Ziff Davis brands with their own API surfaces are profiled as separate entries.

providers.name: Condé Nast
providers.description: Condé Nast is a global media company owned by Advance Publications that produces editorial content across more than two dozen iconic brands — Vogue, GQ, The New Yorker, Wired, Vanity Fair, Bon Appétit, Architectural Digest, Pitchfork, Allure, Glamour, Self, Teen Vogue, Condé Nast Traveler, Epicurious, Tatler, House & Garden, The World of Interiors, Ars Technica, Vogue Business, La Cucina Italiana and Johansens. Public content surfaces are not a developer API but a federated set of brand-level RSS feeds, schema.org NewsArticle JSON-LD on every article, monthly XML sitemaps, syndicated video on YouTube and OTT, and a private editorial CMS (internally known as Copilot) that powers all sites.

providers.name: Next Big Idea Club
providers.description: Next Big Idea Club is a nonfiction book subscription club and podcast that curates the most important new nonfiction, chosen by a selection committee of Malcolm Gladwell, Adam Grant, Susan Cain, and Daniel Pink. Members receive curated new nonfiction, an in-app library, courses, and author interviews across the web and native iOS/Android apps. The consumer experience is powered by a first-party WordPress REST API (the members/v1 namespace) secured with OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect via the WP OAuth Server, with Stripe integration for subscription billing. This profile was seeded as a Bloomberg Beta portfolio lead and enriched from the provider's public /wp-json/ discovery and /.well-known/ OAuth surface.

providers.name: UnitedMasters
providers.description: UnitedMasters is an independent music distribution platform founded by Steve Stoute in 2017 and backed by Alphabet, Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), and Apple. Artists distribute music to 150+ streaming services while keeping full ownership of their master recordings, with real-time royalty payouts, Blueprint AI artist development tools, analytics, and brand and sync licensing partnerships with the NBA, ESPN, TikTok, and other major brands. UnitedMasters does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: 1Social
providers.description: 1Social enables publishing to major social networks directly from AI chat interfaces like ChatGPT and Claude. One message to your AI agent is sent to Instagram, TikTok, YouTube Shorts, LinkedIn, X, Bluesky, Threads and Facebook, with each caption automatically trimmed to fit. No dashboard, no copy‑paste, and scheduling is handled server‑side. The service respects your tokens, never stores them, and provides engagement metrics per network.

providers.name: Breakr
providers.description: Breakr provides an operating system for creator ecosystems, offering tools for campaign management, creator discovery, CRM, payments, escrow, analytics, and AI assistance. The platform enables brands, agencies, and creators to run campaigns, manage finances, and automate workflows, with a focus on secure escrow‑protected payments and AI‑driven insights. It aims to streamline the creator economy by integrating product, payment, and relationship layers into a single ledger.

providers.name: Captura
providers.description: Captura provides an all‑in‑one photography suite for studios and businesses, offering workflow management, yearbook creation, AI‑enhanced image editing, print lab services, and more. Their platform connects every step of the photography process, helping over 500 businesses streamline operations, increase revenue, and deliver professional results efficiently.

providers.name: VaynerMedia
providers.description: VaynerMedia is an integrated strategy, creative, and media agency founded by Gary Vaynerchuk, positioning itself as "The Modern Agency of Record" with social media at the center of its practice. Headquartered in New York with roughly 2,000 employees across offices in Los Angeles, Chattanooga, Chicago, Miami, Toronto, Amsterdam, London, Mexico City, Sydney, Mumbai, Tokyo, Kuala Lumpur, Singapore, and Bangkok, the agency serves clients including Bose, Coach, Diageo, Duracell, Indeed, Jimmy John's, Meta, Mondelez, NatWest, PepsiCo, Tinder, and Wingstop. VaynerMedia is the flagship brand of holding company VaynerX, whose portfolio also includes Gallery Media Group, ChukMedia, Tamara Group, Eva Nosidam Productions, VaynerSpeakers, Tingley Lane, and the Marketing for the Now podcast. VaynerMedia is a services agency, not an API or platform company — it does not publish a developer API, SDK, or public technology product, and its public GitHub presence (github.com/vaynermedia and github.com/vaynerx) consists primarily of forked open source libraries and internal build tooling rather than maintained API products. The one machine-readable surface VaynerMedia does serve is its own website: vaynermedia.com runs on self-hosted WordPress at WP Engine and leaves the WordPress REST API open for anonymous reads at vaynermedia.com/wp-json/, with 365 registered routes covering posts, pages, media, taxonomies and the agency's own case_study custom post type. The site also serves a Yoast-generated llms.txt. Neither is a developer product — they are the content surface of a marketing site — but both are real, public and callable, and they are what an agent researching the agency can actually read.

providers.name: Audora
providers.description: Audora provides distribution and promotion services for independent artists, part of Metalmedia Group in Gothenburg. Founded in 2025, Audora offers music upload, ISRC management, royalty tracking, and marketing tools, ensuring artists retain ownership of their ISRCs. The platform supports streaming, digital storefronts, and provides analytics for audience growth.

providers.name: Soundful
providers.description: Soundful provides AI-generated music for brands, creators, and enterprises. Their platform offers scalable, royalty‑free tracks created with ethically trained AI, enabling users to quickly generate custom soundtracks for marketing, video, podcasts, and more. Soundful’s service includes a free tier for hobbyists, paid plans for teams, and enterprise licensing, with features like unlimited track generation, style libraries, and direct download options. The company emphasizes copyright‑safe music, brand‑centric sonic identity, and collaborative tools for producers.

providers.name: DatePhotos AI
providers.description: DatePhotos AI provides AI‑generated dating profile photos for platforms like Tinder, Bumble and Hinge. The service uses advanced generative models to create natural‑looking, high‑quality images that help users improve their first impression and increase match rates. It offers a web dashboard, mobile apps, and integrations, with features such as multiple style generations, realness scoring, and privacy controls. The company emphasizes data protection and user consent, and its platform is available globally.

providers.name: Metacritic
providers.description: Metacritic is a review aggregator that collects critic and user scores for games, movies, TV shows, and music, computing a weighted Metascore for each title. The Metacritic API (provided via Fabric Origin / IVA / Gracenote) gives programmatic access to Metascores, user scores, individual critic reviews, publication details, and entertainment rankings for movies and television. Unofficial community-built wrappers also expose game, movie, and TV data from Metacritic's public backend.

providers.name: Phyllo
providers.description: Phyllo provides APIs that give developers access to public and consented social data across 25+ platforms, enabling influencer discovery, brand safety vetting, social listening, background verification, and financial services such as income assessment and visa checks. Their platform consolidates multiple social media sources into a single API, offering tools for creator tools, identity verification, content publishing, and AI-driven insights, aimed at influencer marketing, PR agencies, and financial institutions.

providers.name: BuzzSearch
providers.description: BuzzSearch provides AI‑powered tools to discover ad angles on Reddit and TikTok, tracking brand visibility across ChatGPT, Gemini, and Google AI Overviews. It monitors rankings, sentiment, and citations in real time, helping marketers improve their outreach and measure impact across major social platforms.

providers.name: Liveu
providers.description: LiveU is a provider of cloud-based, IP-bonded live video contribution, production, and distribution technology for broadcasters, sports, news, public safety, and enterprise. Its portfolio spans field encoders (the LU-series and the Q Era LU900Q), the LiveU Central cloud management platform, LiveU Studio and Nexus production tools, the LiveU Matrix distribution grid, DataBridge and LU-LINK connectivity, and the LiveU Solo streaming line. LiveU pioneered bonded-cellular transmission that aggregates multiple LTE/5G, Wi-Fi, and satellite links into a single reliable, low-latency video feed. This profile was surfaced as a venture-capital portfolio company and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline; LiveU publishes marketing, support, and training surfaces but no public developer portal, OpenAPI, or open API documentation was found - the LiveU Central API is available to customers behind authentication.

providers.name: Maloja
providers.description: Maloja is an open-source, self-hosted music scrobble database that lets users collect and analyze their listening habits. It provides charts, artist association insights, and customizable images without relying on external music services. Users can run it via Docker or Podman, configure API keys for Last.fm or Spotify, and integrate with existing scrobble clients through a standard-compliant API. The project emphasizes privacy, data ownership, and simplicity, offering manual scrobbling and proxy capabilities.

providers.name: Hackernoon
providers.description: HackerNoon is an independent technology publishing platform and community CMS, founded in 2016 by David Smooke and headquartered in Edwards, Colorado. It operates a free, open library of more than 150,000 practitioner-authored, human-edited technology stories from 35,000+ contributing engineers, covering AI, software engineering, Web3, cybersecurity, startups and science, and serves roughly 3-4 million monthly readers. The company builds and open-sources the publishing software behind the site — the Chowa collaborative editor, the Pixel Icon Library, the HackerNoon pixel font and the Editing Protocol — and monetises through business blogging credits, targeted ads, newsletters and AI content licensing. HackerNoon publishes no public API: probed on 2026-08-22, it serves no OpenAPI, GraphQL, MCP or A2A surface. Its machine-readable surface is a content and AI-access one — an llms.txt, a per-crawler robots.txt policy, RSS feeds and sitemaps — with a "live content feed API" advertised in llms.txt as coming in Q3 2026 and not yet shipped.

providers.name: Native Instruments
providers.description: Native Instruments creates software and hardware for music production, DJing, and audio engineering. Their portfolio includes the Komplete suite, Maschine, Traktor, and a range of virtual instruments and effects, serving musicians, producers, and sound designers worldwide.

providers.name: Postcron
providers.description: Postcron is a social media scheduling and publishing tool that lets marketers, agencies, and small businesses plan, schedule, and automatically publish content across Instagram, Facebook, X (Twitter), LinkedIn, Pinterest, and TikTok from a single dashboard. It supports bulk uploading up to 1,000 posts from Excel or Google Docs, multi-account and team management, automatic image watermarking, a browser extension, and mobile apps for iOS and Android. Originally a Y Combinator / 500 Global-backed startup, Postcron is a consumer- and SMB-facing publishing product; it exposes an internal application API used by its own clients but does not publish a documented public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or a developer portal.

providers.name: usesignal-dev
providers.description: useSignal offers a suite of free, browser‑based tools that require no registration. Users can download video or audio from URLs, record screen or voice, compress and merge PDF files, generate QR codes, and format or beautify JSON data. All tools run client‑side, ensuring privacy and quick results, and are accessible via a clean web interface at usesignal.dev.

providers.name: Bookbub
providers.description: BookBub is a book-discovery and ebook-deals platform that connects a membership of over 10 million power readers with limited-time discounted ebooks, new releases, and preorders across major retailers (Kindle, Apple Books, Barnes & Noble, Kobo, Google Play) in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia. For readers it curates personalized daily deal alerts and recommendations; for authors and publishers it operates a partner side offering Featured Deals promotions, BookBub Ads (a self-serve display advertising platform), preorder and new-release alerts, author profiles, and free marketing tools, all managed through the Partner Dashboard. BookBub is backed by Bloomberg Beta. No public developer API is currently published; partner tooling is delivered through the web dashboard rather than a documented API surface.

providers.name: Scopio
providers.description: Scopio (Scopio LLC) is a New York-based global visual-content marketplace and creative-talent platform, founded in 2017 and backed by 500 Global. It connects businesses with a network of 25,000+ vetted photographers and visual artists across 172 countries and a library of more than three million authentic, diverse stock images that can be licensed under standard, extended, and editorial licenses. Brands including Disney, Microsoft, and Meta use Scopio to hire creative talent and source unique imagery, with AI used to sort, tag, title, and feature contributed work. Scopio operates as a consumer- and business-facing web and mobile marketplace (Shopify-hosted storefront plus iOS/Android artist apps); it does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Gannett
providers.description: Gannett Co., Inc. is a diversified media and digital marketing solutions company and the publisher of USA TODAY and a network of more than 200 local daily newspapers across the United States. It now presents its corporate identity as USA TODAY Co. — www.gannett.com 301-redirects its corporate pages to www.usatodayco.com, and investors.gannett.com resolves to investors.usatodayco.com. Through the USA TODAY Network and LocaliQ, its digital marketing services arm for small and medium-sized businesses, Gannett delivers news, audience and advertising technology. Gannett publishes no developer portal, no API reference and no machine-readable API contract: developer.gannett.com and developer.usatoday.com both redirect to consumer sites, and no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL, MCP or A2A surface is served on any of its hosts. What it does publish machine-readably is a publisher-side control surface — an RFC 9116 security.txt, a Global Privacy Control signal, an llms.txt on localiq.com, and a 958-line robots.txt that denies the major AI crawlers site-wide while re-allowing a commercial subset of shopping, money and sponsor-content paths.

providers.name: Literati
providers.description: Literati is an Austin, Texas based children's book company founded by Jessica Ewing that operates three connected consumer and school businesses: personalized monthly Book Clubs for Kids that ship five curated books matched to a child's reading level and interests starting at $11.95 per month, Clubs for Classrooms for teachers, and a school book fair business (in-person and online) run through the OpenBook coordinator dashboard at openbook.literati.com and the year-round Literati Store, which returns a share of proceeds to participating schools. The company draws on 150+ publishers, combines expert curation with data science to personalize book selection, and reports more than one million books donated to Title I schools and underserved communities since 2019. Literati publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs; its public technical surface is limited to consumer and school-facing web applications, iOS and Android apps, and an RFC 9116 security.txt vulnerability-reporting contact.

providers.name: Media Chain
providers.description: Mediachain (Mediachain Labs) was a decentralized universal media library and attribution protocol built on IPFS and blockchain technology, designed to let creators and applications collaborate on open metadata about creative works and track the provenance and ownership of online images and other media. Founded in 2016 with seed funding from Andreessen Horowitz and Union Square Ventures, the company was acqui-hired by Spotify in April 2017 to help build fair, blockchain-based royalty attribution for rightsholders. The company is now defunct and its primary domain (mediachain.io) is a parked page, but its open-source protocol, design documentation, Protocol Buffer definitions, and first-party client libraries (the `aleph`/`mcclient` JavaScript client on npm and the `mediachain-client` Python reader on PyPI) remain public under the github.com/mediachain organization. This profile was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and enriched from its surviving open-source surface.

providers.name: Scott Foresman
providers.description: Scott Foresman was a leading elementary educational publisher for PreK through Grade 6 across all subject areas. Founded in 1896, the company became part of Pearson PLC in 1996. In 2019, Pearson spun off its U.S.-based K-12 courseware business, which was rebranded as Savvas Learning Company in 2020. Scott Foresman's iconic educational content — including the "Dick and Jane" reading series and basal reading programs — now lives under the Savvas Learning brand. No public developer API is currently available.

providers.name: Soundboks
providers.description: Soundboks is a Danish consumer-electronics company that designs and manufactures loud, durable, battery-powered Bluetooth party speakers (Soundboks 4, Soundboks Mix) plus companion products such as Lightboks party lights. Products are sold direct-to-consumer through a Shopify-powered storefront and controlled with a companion iOS/Android app that supports wireless playback and multi-speaker pairing (TeamUp). Soundboks does not publish a first-party developer API or SDK; its only programmatic surface is the Shopify Customer Account API (OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect) exposed on its own store domain via the standard Shopify discovery documents, which is what this enrichment pass captured.

providers.name: Sudowrite
providers.description: Sudowrite is an AI writing platform built specifically for fiction and creative writers, used by 300,000+ authors from debut novelists to bestselling professionals. Its fiction-trained Muse AI model, alongside Story Bible (AI-powered character, worldbuilding, plot, and style memory), First Draft chapter drafting, and tools like Write, Rewrite, Describe, Expand, Brainstorm, and Canvas, helps writers draft, revise, and develop stories faster without sacrificing their voice. Sudowrite also offers a 1,000+ plugin marketplace, multi-model support (Sudowrite Muse, Claude, GPT, Gemini), and web plus iOS/Android apps. Named "a salvation" by The New Yorker and featured in The New York Times, The Verge, Time, and Wired. Sudowrite publishes no public developer API; the surface here is its consumer product, docs, and support properties.

providers.name: Ableton
providers.description: Ableton is a Berlin‑based company that creates software, hardware, and learning platforms for music creation and performance. Founded in 1999, Ableton develops the flagship DAW Live, as well as instruments like Push, Move, and Note, and offers extensive educational resources, community support, and a global user base of musicians, producers, and educators.

providers.name: Horizon Media
providers.description: Horizon Media is the largest independent media agency in the United States, founded in 1989 by Bill Koenigsberg and headquartered at 75 Varick Street in New York with offices in Los Angeles and Toronto. The agency employs roughly 2,300+ people, is ranked the third largest US media agency by COMvergence, and manages an estimated $8.7 billion in billings. Horizon operates a portfolio of specialty units (Horizon Next for performance, Blue Hour Studios for social/creator, Night Market for retail media, Scout Sports for sponsorship via Horizon Sports & Experiences, and the WHY Group for cultural insights) and runs a proprietary data and AI stack anchored by the Blu platform. In 2025 Horizon formed Horizon Global, a 50/50 US joint venture with Havas positioned at roughly $20 billion in combined billings, merging Blu with Havas Converged into a shared platform branded BluConverged, and is also building Horizon OS (Open Sphere) as an orchestration layer over the programmatic ad-tech stack. In June 2026 Horizon launched an agentic integration layer around Blu — a set of Blu audience APIs, MCP endpoints and agent-based integration points that ad-tech, media-owner and martech partners can build on — but that surface is partner-gated: Horizon publishes no developer portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, no SDKs in any public registry, and its GitHub organization has zero public repositories. The only route to the API is the corporate contact form. All platforms documented here are proprietary systems reachable through a commercial partnership rather than open developer APIs.

providers.name: Audiobookshelf
providers.description: Audiobookshelf provides a self‑hosted audiobook and podcast server that lets users organize, stream, and share their personal media collections. It offers a web UI, mobile apps, and integrations for popular platforms, supporting features like library management, playback controls, and metadata fetching from online sources.

providers.name: Avid
providers.description: Avid provides media creation and management solutions empowering audio, video, and broadcast professionals. Their platform includes MediaCentral, Content Core, and AI‑powered workflow tools used by millions of creators worldwide. Avid’s products support news, film, TV, music, and live events, earning multiple Emmy Awards and serving customers in over 60 countries.

providers.name: Backerkit
providers.description: BackerKit is a crowdfunding and pledge-management platform for professional creators. It began as backer-survey and data-management software that helps creators who funded projects on Kickstarter and Indiegogo collect shipping addresses, sell add-ons and pre-orders, charge cards, and manage backer data for reward fulfillment. It has since grown into a full crowdfunding platform of its own, powering campaigns end to end and, in 2024, roughly one in every four dollars raised on Kickstarter. BackerKit is a Y Combinator company. It exposes integration API keys (API key, secret, and Store GUID) so creators can connect fulfillment services such as ShipStation, but it does not publish a public, self-serve developer API, OpenAPI definition, or SDKs; developer access is account-scoped and configured inside the BackerKit dashboard.

providers.name: gpodder.net
providers.description: gpodder.net is a free, open-source podcast syncing service that lets users discover, subscribe to, and track podcasts across devices. It provides a web interface and API for managing podcast subscriptions, fetching episode metadata, and sharing lists. The platform is community‑driven, offers public directories, and supports integration with third‑party podcast apps.

providers.name: Aiguang
providers.description: Aiguang (爱逛) is a Hangzhou, China live-streaming and short-video commerce platform built on the WeChat ecosystem. Consumers enter live rooms through the Aiguang WeChat mini-program and the Aiguang mobile app to take part in limited-time discounts, group buys and live-stream giveaways, while merchants and MCN hosts run their broadcasts from the Aiguang seller app and a PC live-broadcast console carrying interaction, marketing, promotion and analytics tooling. The platform is wired into the Youzan (有赞) CPS product pool so viewers can resell what they watch. Per its own user agreement and privacy statement (effective 2025-01-17) the platform is operated by 杭州杨杨得翼文化有限公司 (Hangzhou Yangyang Deyi Culture Co., Ltd.). Aiguang publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract; its merchant, supplier and MCN surfaces are reached through account logins and a merchant community forum.

providers.name: Detail
providers.description: Detail is a video creation and editing app for iOS and macOS built by Detail Technologies B.V., a Point Nine portfolio company. It combines multi-camera recording, AI-powered auto-editing (silence removal, zoom cuts, captions, titles, and music), live multi-platform streaming to YouTube, Twitch, Instagram, and LinkedIn, a built-in teleprompter, green-screen background removal, and automatic captions, aimed at creators, podcasters, and streamers producing polished video quickly. Detail won the 2025 App Store Award for iPad App of the Year and was a 2026 Apple Design Award finalist. It is a consumer application and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: 4DReplay
providers.description: 4DReplay is a media technology company that builds multi-camera, time-slice ("bullet-time") video capture and replay systems for live sports, entertainment and events. Arrays of roughly 50 to 120 synchronized cameras — locked to within 1/10,000 of a second — are processed in real time to produce any-angle replay highlights within seconds of a play and deliver them to broadcast, mobile and OTT audiences. The product line spans 4DReplay (premium broadcast instant replay), 4DReplay+ / 4DLive (5G-based interactive multi-view live streaming with speed, angle and tracking overlays), and 4Dist, a browser-based interactive OTT platform that adds automated AI motion and swing analysis for academies, coaches and players. Founded in 2012 by Hongsu Jung and headquartered in San Mateo, California, with offices in Seoul and Tokyo, the company has worked with ESPN, NBC, CBS, FOX Sports, the NBA, MLB, NHL, the PGA Championship and the Olympics. As of August 2026 4DReplay publishes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable API contract; its surfaces are broadcast integrations and the consumer/operator 4Dist web and mobile apps.

providers.name: Amazon Music
providers.description: Amazon Music is a streaming service offering on-demand music, playlists, and podcasts. It integrates with Amazon devices and provides a catalog of millions of songs, personalized stations, and offline listening. The service is part of Amazon’s ecosystem, available via web, mobile apps, and Alexa-enabled devices, and supports subscription tiers for ad‑free listening and high‑fidelity audio.

providers.name: Legendary Entertainment
providers.description: Legendary Entertainment is a Burbank, California media company that owns, produces and distributes content to worldwide audiences across three divisions: Legendary Pictures (film), Legendary Television and Digital Media, and Legendary Comics. Its productions have grossed more than $20 billion worldwide at the box office, spanning franchises such as Dune, Godzilla and Kong, A Minecraft Movie, Street Fighter, Enola Holmes and Monarch: Legacy of Monsters, with an explicit focus on the fandom demographic. Legendary runs no public developer program and publishes no documented API. It does, however, expose a live, publicly readable WordPress REST API on legendary.com that serves its news posts and its film, television, comics, trailer and digital catalogs as JSON — captured here as a platform-exposed content API rather than a supported product.

providers.name: Ellipsus
providers.description: Ellipsus is a collaborative writing platform built for creative and fiction writers, combining a modern text editor with granular, Git-style version control so authors can draft, branch, share, and merge work together across devices. Founded in 2022 and operated by a small distributed team across Berlin (Germany), Madrid (Spain), and Szczecin (Poland), the product threads collaboration through every stage of writing — organizing drafts, discussing feedback, tracking changes, and preserving public version history — with a writers-first, artist-ownership, anti-AI-generated-content stance. Ellipsus offers a free tier and a paid Plus license, and is backed by Speedinvest. It is added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Universe
providers.description: Universe is a no-code website builder that lets anyone design and publish a custom website from a phone, tablet, or computer, using a drag-and-drop GRID block system with built-in commerce, mail tools, analytics, and SEO. A 2023 Apple Design Award winner with more than one million sites built, Universe is a Y Combinator W18 company backed by GV and General Catalyst. Universe is a consumer creation platform and publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: ablefy
providers.description: ablefy (formerly elopage) is a German all-in-one sales and monetization platform for coaches, creators, trainers, consultants, and online educators. It provides conversion-optimized checkout with 12+ payment methods (PayPal, Klarna, SEPA, cards, Apple/Google Pay) across multiple currencies, an integrated LMS for online courses, memberships and subscriptions, community and live events, e-ticketing, automated invoicing with international tax/OSS compliance, and an optional reseller (merchant-of-record) model. Sellers can automate workflows through the ablefy API, webhooks, and access-token authentication, plus a Zapier integration and email-marketing connectors. The platform reports 80,000+ sellers, 6M+ customers serviced, and over EUR 2 billion in processed transactions across 13+ years of operation.

providers.name: Rapchat
providers.description: Rapchat is a mobile-first music creation platform for artists, rappers, singers, and producers, founded in 2014. Creators use the Rapchat iOS and Android apps to find professionally-produced beats from top producers, record studio-quality vocals with effects and audio filters, write lyrics, join music challenges, collaborate, and share finished songs with a creator community. The platform reports 15M+ creators, 100M+ tracks, and over one billion plays, and offers free web-based artist tools (rap name generator, lyric generator, rhyme finder, BPM mood guide) alongside Free, Premium, and Pro subscription tiers. Rapchat is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this profile the company exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; its /api endpoint is an internal application backend (HTTP 403).

providers.name: The Business of Fashion
providers.description: The Business of Fashion (BoF) is an authoritative digital media and intelligence company founded by Imran Amed in 2007, serving the global fashion and luxury industry. It publishes news, analysis, case studies and industry data, and operates subscription products including BoF Professional membership, BoF Insights research reports, events and online courses. Backed by Index Ventures. BoF publishes no public developer API; this profile captures the company's public web, subscription and legal surface plus a domain-security probe.

providers.name: KatalistAI
providers.description: Katalist is an AI-powered storyboarding and video platform that turns scripts and ideas into visual stories with consistent characters and scenes. Founded in 2023, it converts scripts (CSV, Word, PowerPoint) into storyboards in one click, keeps characters consistent across shots, lets creators customize framing, angles, poses and scenes, and includes a video studio that layers voiceover, music and sound effects. It targets filmmakers, directors, advertisers, content creators, animators and educators looking to move from concept to visualized story faster. Backed by 500 Global, Katalist is a consumer/creative generative-AI SaaS accessed through its web application; it does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, or developer documentation surface.

providers.name: Arcalune Music
providers.description: Arcalune Music is a Japanese‑origin online music library offering original compositions, fan‑arranged game tracks, and royalty‑free background music and sound effects. All tracks are available for free streaming and download, suitable for use in videos, live streams, and game projects. The site provides high‑quality MP3 files under Creative Commons licensing, with multilingual navigation (Japanese, English, Spanish, Portuguese, Hindi, Indonesian, French).

providers.name: Buzzfy
providers.description: Buzzfy is an Instagram growth platform that re‑edits creators’ best reels, adding new openings, subtitles, backgrounds or reply stickers, then posts them as trial reels to reach new audiences. It offers analytics and comment‑to‑DM features, helping creators expand their reach without needing a large follower base.

providers.name: creativeLIVE
providers.description: creativeLIVE (CreativeLive) is an online learning platform offering more than 2,300 on-demand courses and live interactive classes taught by working professionals across photography, video and filmmaking, graphic and web design, business and entrepreneurship, arts and crafts, audio and music production, and AI and technology. Learners access practical, skill-based instruction through a subscription, with certificates of completion available. Surfaced as a portfolio company of GV and added to the API Evangelist network; creativeLIVE exposes no public developer API, but does publish a machine-readable llms.txt course index for AI agents.

providers.name: Audiodraft
providers.description: Audiodraft is a Helsinki-founded global audio branding and custom music production company that helps brands design, create, and manage their sonic identity across advertising, video, games, and campaigns. Its service is organized around three offerings — ANALYZE (data-driven audio strategy and brand-attribute analysis), CREATE (custom music, sound design, and voice-over production), and MANAGE (brand-fit validation and sound testing) — drawing on a crowdsourced community of thousands of composers and sound designers across 100+ countries. Audiodraft has worked with brands and agencies including Nokia, Red Bull Media House, Finnair, Fortum, and TBWA. It is a creative audio-branding services provider and does not currently publish a public API or developer program; this profile was surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and enriched with its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Blockpartyapp
providers.description: Block Party is a consumer privacy tool — a browser extension (Chrome, Firefox, and Edge) that helps people deep-clean and secure their social media presence. It scans connected accounts for privacy and security exposures, then automates bulk cleanup across Facebook, X/Twitter, Instagram, Reddit, and LinkedIn: deleting old posts, likes, and comments, untagging photos, removing connections, stripping location data, and tightening privacy settings. Founded by Tracy Chou, Block Party (also branded Privacy Party) is a consumer-facing application and does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Dead Brands, LLC
providers.description: Dead Brands, LLC revives dead brands and offers ERP consulting for small businesses, specializing in SAP Business One and Odoo solutions. They provide AI and automation services, and host the Shark Bite Biz podcast, delivering real talk and results for entrepreneurs seeking growth and technology integration.

providers.name: OpenSponsorship
providers.description: OpenSponsorship is a two-sided sports sponsorship and influencer marketing marketplace that connects brands with a network of more than 25,000 professional athletes, teams, sports creators, and health and wellness influencers across 150+ sports. Brands pay a monthly subscription to search the roster, post campaigns, submit proposals, manage contracts, and track ROI, while athletes and their agents join for free with OpenSponsorship taking a commission on secured deals. The platform layers AI-based matching, social-content search, campaign management, and reporting on top of a managed service that handles matching, outreach, contracts, and reporting. OpenSponsorship exposes no public developer API at this time; this profile captures its public identity and web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: RedCircle
providers.description: RedCircle is a podcast advertising, hosting, and monetization platform founded in 2018 that turns podcast host-read endorsements into measurable results for brands and creators. For podcasters it provides podcast hosting, RSS distribution to directories, dynamic ad insertion, a cross-promotions marketplace, instant payouts, automated transcript and video generation, and audience analytics. For brands it operates a fully managed host-read ad platform that pairs proprietary data with authentic creator voices to run and measure campaigns at scale. RedCircle also documents OpenRAP, its remote ad-pipeline / VAST configuration for dynamic ad insertion. The platform is offered as SaaS tiers (Growth, Pro, and Enterprise) rather than as a public developer API; there is no published developer portal, OpenAPI, or SDK.

providers.name: Libre.fm
providers.description: Libre.fm is an open source music community that lets users track their listening habits across various music players and services. Since 2009, it has recorded hundreds of millions of listens from over 390,000 users, offering public profiles, community charts, and the ability to run a self‑hosted instance. The service integrates with many clients via scrobbling and provides APIs for developers to access user listening data and music metadata.

providers.name: TechRepublic
providers.description: TechRepublic is a leading IT and enterprise technology media site that provides IT professionals with news, analysis, tips, tutorials, best practices, and research on business technology. Covering topics including cloud computing, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, enterprise software, hardware, and data management, TechRepublic serves technology decision-makers and practitioners across industries. The platform exposes its content programmatically via WordPress REST API endpoints and standard RSS/Atom feeds.

providers.name: Bynor
providers.description: Bynor provides an AI‑powered operating system for social media, enabling users to create, publish, analyze, and grow content across platforms. The platform unifies conversations, data, and automation in a single place, helping brands and creators streamline their social workflows and gain insights.

providers.name: Firstory
providers.description: Firstory is a podcast hosting and monetization platform for creators, holding the leading share of the Mandarin-language podcast market and a growing presence across the Asia-Pacific region with over 14,000 shows. Creators upload an episode once and distribute it to Apple Podcasts, Spotify, KKBOX, YouTube, Amazon Music, Pocket Casts, and more than ten other players, then use AI Studio to auto-generate transcripts, summaries, highlights, and newsletter drafts. Firstory layers on second-by-second analytics, dynamic ad insertion, membership subscriptions, listener donations, cross-promotion, a personal website builder, the Flink universal link, and embeddable players. It does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures the company's public surface and infrastructure signals.

providers.name: ReadSpeaker
providers.description: ReadSpeaker provides text-to-speech (TTS) cloud and embedded solutions used to add voice to websites, mobile apps, e-learning, transportation systems, and more. The speechCloud API converts text into high-quality audio in multiple languages and voices that can be returned in formats such as MP3 for use within applications.

providers.name: Thematic
providers.description: Thematic is a copyright-free music licensing platform that connects independent content creators with emerging artists. Creators get a permanent, no-cost license to use tracks in their videos in exchange for including a promotional link in the description, which activates YouTube Content ID whitelisting and prevents copyright claims across YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, and podcasts. Premium ($9.99/mo) and Pro ($24.99/mo) plans unlock the full catalog, podcast licensing, and unlimited downloads. Co-founded with YouTube pioneer Michelle Phan, Thematic serves 1M+ creators and 10,000+ independent artists across 220+ countries. Thematic runs a consumer web and mobile app and does not currently publish a public developer API. Backed by 500 Global and Lux Capital.

providers.name: Wattpad
providers.description: Wattpad is a Toronto-based social storytelling platform where a global community of more than 90 million writers and readers create, share, and read serialized original fiction across every genre. Founded in 2006 and acquired by Naver (WEBTOON) in 2021, Wattpad extends its stories into publishing, film, and TV through Wattpad WEBTOON Studios. Wattpad formerly operated a public developer API (developer.wattpad.com), but public access was discontinued around April 2018 and the API is now internal-only, so this profile captures the company's web properties and operational surface rather than an active API program.

providers.name: 123RF
providers.description: 123RF is a global stock content platform offering millions of royalty‑free photos, vectors, videos, audio and AI‑enhanced creative assets. It provides a developer API for integrating searchable media, image enhancement tools, and white‑label solutions into websites and applications, serving creators, marketers and businesses worldwide.

providers.name: Aicut
providers.description: Aicut provides an AI-powered video generation platform enabling creators to produce faceless YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram videos automatically. Leveraging advanced text‑to‑video models, it offers voiceover, captions, and auto‑scheduling features, targeting marketers and content creators seeking scalable video content. The service includes a free tier and paid plans with higher resolution outputs and brand customization.

providers.name: Buy Me a Coffee
providers.description: Buy Me a Coffee is a creator-support platform that lets fans tip creators ("buy a coffee"), subscribe to recurring memberships, and buy extras from a creator's shop. Its developer API is a read-only REST interface (base https://developers.buymeacoffee.com/api/v1) authenticated with a personal access Bearer token created self-serve in the Developer Dashboard. The API exposes a creator's own one-time supporters, memberships/subscriptions, and extra purchases, and the platform also delivers server-push webhooks for donation, membership, and shop events. Buy Me a Coffee charges a flat 5% platform fee on transactions with no monthly fee.

providers.name: Home From College
providers.description: Home From College (H\FC) is an AI-powered growth platform that connects college students with paid work from consumer brands. Students earn money and build professional experience through microGIGs (quick paid tasks such as app installs, surveys, product feedback, and social sharing with instant payment) and GIGs (larger, ongoing opportunities including content creation, brand-ambassador roles, product testing, and internships), while brands reach and activate Gen Z talent for marketing campaigns. Backed by GV, Home From College runs a two-sided marketplace across a student mobile app and a brand-facing web platform. No public developer program, API documentation, or SDKs were found during enrichment.

providers.name: Smore
providers.description: Smore is a newsletter and flyer builder purpose-built for educators, schools, and districts, letting teachers and administrators create accessible, mobile-friendly digital newsletters from customizable templates to keep families and staff informed. The product emphasizes WCAG AA accessibility, translation for multilingual families, and engagement analytics on opens and clicks. Smore is now part of SchoolStatus, the family-engagement platform. It was surfaced as a Techstars portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Smore publishes no public developer program, API, developer portal, or OpenAPI surface — this profile captures its identity, public web properties, and probed domain security posture only.

providers.name: Stability Audio
providers.description: Stable Audio (by Stability AI) is a generative audio model for music and sound-effect generation. The Stability Developer Platform exposes Stable Audio 2.5 endpoints alongside image, video, and 3D generation. Pricing is credit-based at 1 credit = $0.01; Stable Audio 2.5 generations are reported at $0.20 per generation regardless of duration.

providers.name: ReDEF
providers.description: REDEF is a media curation and newsletter company founded and led by Jason Hirschhorn (CEO + Chief Curator) that "DJs the internet" — surfacing daily remixes of the stories, people, and ideas that matter across Media, Fashion, Music, Sports, and Tech. Readers follow curated Mixes, Sets, Originals, Charts, and email Newsletters ("interest remixes for curious minds"), and can build and share their own mixes. ReDEF was surfaced as a portfolio company of bloomberg-beta and added to the API Evangelist network; enrichment found a public consumer content website (redef.com) but no public developer program, API, documentation, or machine-readable surface.

providers.name: Aimusicgen
providers.description: Aimusicgen provides a free AI-powered music generation service that transforms text descriptions, lyrics, or ideas into fully produced songs with vocals or instrumentals. Users can select styles, customize arrangements, and download the generated tracks. The platform offers tools such as AI Song Cover, Lyrics Generator, and AI Music Maker, catering to creators, marketers, and developers seeking quick audio content. Aimusicgen operates as a SaaS solution with a free tier and paid plans for higher credit usage.

providers.name: Tencent Music Entertainment Group
providers.description: Tencent Music Entertainment Group (TME) is a leading Chinese online music entertainment platform offering streaming services, digital music distribution, and live concert experiences across brands such as QQ Music, Kugou, Kuwo, and JOOX. It provides a comprehensive ecosystem for artists, listeners, and partners, integrating social features, AI-driven recommendations, and extensive licensing across domestic and international markets. TME is publicly listed and actively expands its audio content through acquisitions and strategic partnerships.

providers.name: Scribd
providers.description: Scribd Inc. is an American digital-content media company founded in 2007 by Trip Adler, Jared Friedman and Tikhon Bernstam and headquartered in San Francisco, California. It operates four consumer platforms: Scribd (a document-sharing library), Everand (a subscription service for ebooks, audiobooks, magazines, podcasts and sheet music, formerly the flagship Scribd subscription), SlideShare (presentation hosting) and Fable (a social reading app). Scribd was an early Y Combinator company. Its historical public "Platform" API for uploading, converting and displaying documents is now legacy — the official Ruby client (scribd/rscribd) was archived in 2019, Scribd no longer accepts new API accounts, and the SlideShare developer portal has been retired — so this profile documents the company's identity and the remaining first-party developer artifacts rather than a live API surface.

providers.name: Publish.fun
providers.description: Publish.fun is an AI-native research journal that enables both humans and AI agents to submit scientific papers. Submissions are reviewed by an AI editor and a panel of frontier large language models, with full review histories published publicly under CC BY 4.0. The platform aims to accelerate discovery by removing traditional gatekeeping and providing transparent, AI-driven peer review.

providers.name: TNL Mediagene
providers.description: TNL Mediagene is a next-generation digital and technology media group serving millennial and Gen Z audiences across Asia. Formed from the 2023 merger of Taiwan's The News Lens and Japan's Mediagene, the group operates more than twenty media brands spanning news, business, technology, lifestyle, and sports — including The News Lens, INSIDE, Cool3c, Gizmodo Japan, Business Insider Japan, Lifehacker Japan, Roomie, and licensed titles such as Digiday Japan and Glossy Japan. Beyond publishing, the company runs advertising and marketing technology (the Ad2iction DSP), an AI-driven customer data and audience analytics platform, e-commerce properties, and market-research services. It is a portfolio company of 500 Global and is listed on Nasdaq as TNMG. The group publishes no developer portal, no OpenAPI, and no SDK. Its one public, machine-readable integration surface is the Ad2iction header-bidding adapter shipped inside Prebid.js — a first-party-maintained open-source module that posts bid requests to https://ads.ad2iction.com/html/prebid/, documented on the Prebid.org bidder registry rather than on a TNL Mediagene developer site.

providers.name: BBC
providers.description: The British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) is the United Kingdom’s public service broadcaster, providing news, television, radio, and online content worldwide. It operates a vast digital platform, offers a range of APIs for developers, and maintains extensive documentation for its services, including news feeds, media assets, and data services. The BBC is a trusted source of information and cultural programming, serving millions of users across the globe.

providers.name: DZone
providers.description: DZone is one of the world's largest online communities and a leading publisher of knowledge resources for software engineering professionals. Founded in 1997 with roots in Javalobby, DZone reaches millions of developers each month with articles, tutorials, research guides, and Refcards covering topics including cloud architecture, Java, JavaScript, microservices, containers, data, DevOps, AI, and more.

providers.name: Promolta
providers.description: Promolta is a self-service video advertising platform that promotes YouTube and other videos across a network of blogs, websites, mobile apps, and social networks to grow views, subscribers, and engagement. Advertisers fund campaigns and target audiences, while publishers in the Promolta network earn by distributing sponsored video content. Promolta is a portfolio company of 500 Global. Campaigns start at a $10 minimum budget, go live within 24 hours, and can be optimized for views, YouTube likes, YouTube subscribers, or mobile app installs, with targeting by age, gender, location, and keyword. As of the 2026-08-12 enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI/GraphQL contract, developer portal, or webhook surface — this profile captures its public web, legal, blog, and domain-security footprint.

providers.name: Wave AI
providers.description: Wave AI (WaveAI) is a Sunnyvale, California AI music company founded in 2017 by David Loker, Dr. Maya Ackerman, and Chris Cassion, building foundational generative AI models for music and songwriting. Its flagship product LyricStudio is an AI-powered lyric-writing assistant used by millions of artists and creators to generate genre- and topic-aware lyrical suggestions, rhymes, and full songs, and MelodyStudio adds generative vocal-melody and chord generation. The company is backed by 500 Global, Horizon 3 Venture Capital, Kilowatt Capital, and angel investors. Wave AI ships consumer web applications rather than a public developer API; this profile captures its company identity and public web properties. Added to the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio lead and enriched with a domain-security probe and verified public link properties.

providers.name: Fab.com
providers.description: Fab.com is a digital content marketplace operated by Epic Games, where creators buy and sell 3D models, materials, environments, VFX, audio, and game-ready assets. Launched in October 2024, Fab consolidated four of Epic's prior storefronts — the Unreal Engine Marketplace, the Sketchfab Store, Quixel, and the ArtStation Marketplace — into a single catalog with unified licensing, and integrates into Unreal Engine, UEFN, and the Epic Games Launcher. The fabcom entry was originally added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio lead for the earlier, unrelated Fab.com flash-sale design-commerce company (2011–2015), which wound down before the domain passed to Epic Games; see x-identity-note. Fab publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification as of this pass — the surface captured here is its documentation, support, and security-disclosure posture.

providers.name: Venue
providers.description: Venue is an all-in-one internal communications platform that makes it easy for teams to host, organize, and share all hands, webinars, AMAs, and fireside chats. It combines HD live streaming, recording, automatic transcription and summarization, branded Q&A, engagement tracking, and Channels for centralizing events and videos. Aimed at internal comms and employer-brand teams at companies like Shopify, PwC, Wealthsimple, and Yelp, Venue is a Toronto-based, Accel- and Y Combinator-backed productivity company. As of this enrichment pass Venue publishes no public developer API, SDK, or API documentation surface — this profile captures its identity, website properties, and domain security posture.

providers.name: Dreamforge
providers.description: DreamForge.ai is an AI-powered game creation platform for building, iterating on, and publishing 2D and stylized 3D games directly in the browser. Creators use AI to generate gameplay systems, game-ready art and textures, animation, and playable web builds, then share public play pages under dreamforge.ai/play. The platform pairs a creator-facing web studio (including an Asset Studio) with a consumer application distributed on Steam, iOS, and Android. Founded in 2025 and based in Miami, Florida, DreamForge is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z). DreamForge supports stylized 3D world generation, textures, voxels, and billboarding workflows; native 3D model generation is not currently provided. No public developer API, SDK, or developer portal is published at this time.

providers.name: Lala
providers.description: Lala (meetlala.io) is an AI content platform for educators that turns recordings of online classes into publishable social media content. Instructors either host lessons natively on Lala's own video-call product or upload an existing recording by file or link, and Lala automatically curates short-form Reels in Instagram and TikTok aspect ratios, assembles packaged courses, and returns a transcription and summary after each class. It is sold in three tiers -- Free, Pro and Enterprise -- metered on upload minutes, video-call participants and Reels generated per class, and is aimed at tutors, music instructors, teacherpreneurs, schools and universities. Lala is a 500 Global portfolio company that came out of the 500 Georgia program. As of July 2026 Lala publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs or machine-readable API description.

providers.name: The Cirqle
providers.description: The Cirqle provides an AI‑powered influencer marketing platform that connects brands with creators to run performance‑driven campaigns. Its end‑to‑end solution includes creator discovery, AI‑generated briefs, automated contracts, rights management, and detailed ROAS forecasting. By integrating with major ad and e‑commerce networks, The Cirqle enables brands to turn organic creator content into scalable advertising, offering real‑time reporting, affiliate tracking, and a marketplace for creator‑driven ads. The platform aims to maximize ROI for advertisers while simplifying workflow for creators.

providers.name: 24Symbols
providers.description: 24Symbols is a digital reading subscription service, often described as a "Spotify for books," giving readers unlimited access to a catalog of more than 500,000 e-books across Spanish, English, German, Italian, Portuguese, and French for a flat monthly fee. Founded in Madrid and backed by Seedcamp, the platform lets subscribers read on smartphones, tablets, e-readers, and the web, build personal bookshelves, track reading progress, and follow other readers and authors through its social reading community. Alongside its consumer premium plan, 24Symbols offers B2B "reading space" solutions that let hotels, telecoms, media outlets, educational institutions, and loyalty or employee programs license library access for their audiences. The company operates as a consumer- and business-facing subscription product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or partner integration surface; this profile captures its verifiable identity and public web properties.

providers.name: Braid Social
providers.description: Braid Social, Inc. is a venture-backed startup that has run two products under the Braid name. It launched as a creator-economy, direct-to-fan engagement platform — founded by former Facebook product designer Matthew Cahill and software engineer Chris Piro — letting creators build customizable landing pages that consolidated their work across the web (blog posts, videos, podcasts, and commerce links), collect fan phone numbers, and reach followers directly through SMS, push notifications, and mailing lists, with link tracking and cross-platform analytics. It raised a $6.8M seed round in August 2023 led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) with Initialized Capital. The original domain braid.ai is now a domain-for-sale listing at atom.com and braid.social no longer resolves. The same legal entity now ships "Braid Teams" at trybraid.io (mirrored at braidsocial.com) — an AI-powered employee-engagement copilot that runs inside Slack, automating icebreakers, games, polls, events, reminders, leaderboards, and engagement reporting for distributed teams, on a free / $5-per-user Premium / contact-us Enterprise plan. Braid Teams is a Slack-app product with no public developer program: no developer portal, no documentation, no OpenAPI, no SDKs, and no GitHub organization. The only machine surface is the private application backend at core.trybraid.io, which answers {"status":"ok"} at its root and 404s every spec, docs and /.well-known/ path. The homepage states the product is "Currently not accepting new users" and the Slack install endpoint returns HTTP 500.

providers.name: Replica Studios
providers.description: Replica Studios (operated by Replica Media Pty Ltd) built AI voice, text-to-speech (TTS) and speech-to-speech (STS) technology for creators, game developers, and software teams. Its platform offered an AI Voice Library of 40+ expressive voices, Voice Lab for blending up to five voices into a custom character, and Voice Director for generating voice overs and dialogue. Developers integrated these capabilities through the Replica API v2 (OpenAPI 3.0.0) — a REST API supporting text-to-speech, speech-to-speech, and voice-listing operations, authenticated with API keys or Bearer JWTs minted at the /v2/auth endpoint. Replica Studios was a Techstars portfolio company. The company ceased operations on 2025-06-30; the marketing site now shows a farewell page and the api.replicastudios.com host no longer resolves, so this profile is a historical/discovery record captured from public documentation.

providers.name: AbleSky
providers.description: AbleSky, Inc. (能力天空) is an online-education SaaS company incorporated in 2007 in Mountain View, California, operating in China through its wholly owned subsidiary 能力天空科技（北京）有限公司 in Beijing. Its platform lets a school, training institution or instructor stand up a branded online school — website, Android and iOS apps, WeChat micro-school and official account — with course hosting, live classes, exams, educational-administration workflow, course distribution and learner payment collection, marketed as roughly 3,000 features to training organisations across more than 2,000 Chinese cities. It also sells an independent deployment onto a customer's own cloud or hardware. It publishes NO public API: contract discovery on 2026-09-06 found no OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL SDL, WSDL, gRPC service, MCP server, agent card, SDK or developer portal on any AbleSky host. The one machine-readable document it does publish is a valid, auto-discoverable OpenSearch 1.1 course-search descriptor.

providers.name: Melodics
providers.description: Melodics is a New Zealand-based interactive music-learning application that teaches drums, MIDI keyboards, and pad controllers (finger drumming) through gamified, real-time lessons. It connects to electronic instruments and MIDI controllers to give immediate feedback on timing and accuracy, offering guided learning paths, song tutorials, and structured daily practice for beginner through advanced players across desktop and mobile. Melodics is a consumer edtech product and a portfolio company of 500 Global; it publishes no public developer API surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: ChannelMeter
providers.description: ChannelMeter is a creator management and payments platform for multi-channel networks, agencies, and brands. Founded in 2012 and headquartered in San Francisco, it provides an all-in-one suite for creator discovery, onboarding, contract management, analytics, and automated global payouts. Its Creator Pay product moves money to creators across 21+ currencies and 50+ countries, and Creator Cash offers cash advances to creators. ChannelMeter reports having processed over $1B in payments to more than one million creators, working with Stripe and Fifth Third Bank for financial services. The company is backed by 500 Global.

providers.name: Equipboard
providers.description: Equipboard is a community-sourced music-gear discovery platform where musicians, producers, and DJs find the equipment behind the music. Members browse the gear their favorite artists play — guitars, effects pedals, synthesizers, DAWs, plug-ins, microphones, drum machines, and keyboards — build and share their own rigs and gear lists, read and write reviews, and follow buy-links to retailers. Equipboard is built by musicians for musicians and monetizes primarily through affiliate relationships (including the Amazon Associates Program). Recent product work adds album- and track-level gear attribution. The company is backed by 500 Global. Equipboard does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network and enriched from Equipboard's public web surface.

providers.name: Fortell
providers.description: Fortell develops clinically proven AI hearing aids that provide superior speech clarity in noisy environments. The company leverages advanced AI algorithms and scientific research to enhance hearing experiences for users, offering personalized solutions and a modern approach to auditory health.

providers.name: CD Baby
providers.description: CD Baby is an independent music distribution and publishing administration service for songwriters, performers, and independent record labels. Founded in 1998 and now part of Downtown Music Holdings under Virgin Music Group, CD Baby services over 50 million music assets from creators in hundreds of countries across six continents. The platform distributes music to 150+ digital service providers including Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube, Pandora, Tidal, TikTok, Amazon, Shazam, and Deezer, and is a flagship member of YouTube's Preferred Distributor Program plus a preferred partner with Apple and Spotify. Services include digital distribution, physical CD and vinyl manufacturing, publishing administration, cover song licensing, sync licensing through CDB Boost, YouTube and social monetization, performing rights organization (ASCAP, BMI, SOCAN) registration assistance, and promotion tools via SymphonyOS, HearNow, Show.co, Managed Ads, Groover, Laylo, and Internet Radio Airplay. Pricing is a one-time fee ($9.99 single, $14.99 album) with artists retaining over 90% of earnings. CD Baby has paid out more than $1 billion to artists. CD Baby has no public developer API, SDK, or open-source release; all distribution and reporting workflows are exposed only through the artist member portal at members.cdbaby.com.

providers.name: dwell
providers.description: Dwell is a digital publication and lifestyle brand focused on modern home design, architecture, and interior inspiration, published by Ziff Davis. It offers curated home tours, architectural features, renovation and before/after projects, design photography, real estate listings, shopping guides, and design news, plus a Dwell+ subscription for ad-free access and subscriber exclusives, a shop for furniture and decor, and a "Find a Pro" professional directory. Dwell was surfaced as a portfolio-adjacent lead in the API Evangelist network; the public dwell.com property is a consumer media site with no developer API, SDK, or developer portal, so no API artifacts are captured for it.

providers.name: GigFinesse
providers.description: GigFinesse is a live-entertainment talent booking platform that connects hospitality venues — hotels, restaurants, bars, and clubs — with musicians, DJs, and performing artists. Venues discover and book vetted talent and manage contracts, insurance, scheduling, and payments through a centralized dashboard, while artists gain access to consistent, recurring gig opportunities. Clients include premium hospitality brands such as St. Regis, The Ritz-Carlton, Fairmont Hotels, and Hard Rock Hotel. GigFinesse is backed by Bessemer Venture Partners. No public developer API is published as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Intro
providers.description: Intro is a consumer marketplace, founded in 2020 by Raad Mobrem and headquartered in Los Angeles, that connects people with vetted, in-demand experts for one-on-one advice over scheduled video calls. Experts span career and business, interior design and home decor, style and beauty, health and wellness, fitness and nutrition, astrology, and more, with per-session pricing set by each expert. Intro also lets creators and professionals monetize their audience by publishing a bookable profile. The company raised a $10M seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) with participation from Seven Seven Six. Intro operates as a consumer web and mobile product; it does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or a developer portal.

providers.name: Memberful
providers.description: Memberful is a membership and subscription platform (owned by Patreon) that lets independent publishers, educators, and creators sell memberships, subscriptions, digital downloads, podcasts, and courses on their own site while Memberful handles checkout, recurring billing (via Stripe), and member management. Its public developer surface is a GraphQL API served per account at https://ACCOUNT.memberful.com/api/graphql, authenticated with an API key (bearer token) or OAuth 2.0 access token, covering Members, Subscriptions, Plans/Passes, Coupons, and Orders through queries and mutations. Memberful also provides OAuth 2.0 single sign-on for apps and HMAC-signed webhooks for member, subscription, plan, order, and download events.

providers.name: Merchbar
providers.description: Merchbar, Inc. is the official merchandise retailer for top musicians, selling vinyl records, CDs, t-shirts, hoodies, posters, and other band merchandise across thousands of artist storefronts at merchbar.com. It runs a consumer shopping experience alongside a "Merchbar for Artists" program and official merchandise integrations with YouTube and Spotify. Merchbar is a portfolio company of Bullpen Capital. As of this enrichment pass Merchbar publishes no public API, developer program, SDKs, or technical documentation — no developer/api/docs subdomain resolves and there is no /.well-known/security.txt — so this profile captures only its public web presence and probed domain-security posture.

providers.name: Publishizer
providers.description: Publishizer is a book crowdfunding platform and literary agency that connects authors with readers and publishers. Authors create book proposals and run pre-order campaigns; readers pre-order copies to signal demand; and publishers use data such as pre-order volume and proposal quality to discover and acquire promising manuscripts. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes a consumer web platform and blog but no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Reedsy
providers.description: Reedsy is a marketplace and toolset for authors and publishers, connecting writers with a curated network of more than 3,700 vetted publishing professionals including editors, book designers, marketers, ghostwriters, web designers, and translators.
