Beyond the marketplace, Reedsy offers Reedsy Studio (a free writing and book-formatting application), Reedsy Learning (courses and events), Reedsy Discovery (book reviews), and Reedsy Prompts (weekly writing prompts). It supports authors across the full self-publishing journey from manuscript development through market launch. Reedsy is backed by Seedcamp and publishes no public developer API today.

providers.name: Smiler
providers.description: Smiler is an Amsterdam-based on-the-spot photography marketplace that connects travelers and consumers with a network of professional freelance photographers at popular tourist hotspots and leisure locations worldwide. Founded in 2020, Smiler lets people book fast, affordable photoshoots in advance across 100+ destinations, with photos delivered within 48 hours and free cancellation up to 24 hours before the shoot. The company also operates the Smiler Photographer Suite, an all-in-one tool for photographers to build portfolio websites, manage bookings, deliver mobile-friendly client galleries, and handle payments. Smiler is trusted by tens of thousands of photographers across 50+ countries and is backed by Speedinvest, Mosaic Ventures, Dutch Founders Fund, and PROfounders.

providers.name: TREBEL Music
providers.description: TREBEL Music (operated by M&M Media, Inc.) is an advertising-sponsored, legally licensed music download and streaming service that lets people download and listen to music offline at no cost. Founded in 2014 by Gary Mekikian, Corey Jones and Luis Soto Durazo and headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut with offices in Mexico City, Jakarta, Bogota, Los Angeles and Miami, TREBEL licenses catalog from Universal Music Group, Sony Music Entertainment, Warner Music Group and independent labels, and monetizes through digital advertising, branded experiences, virtual goods and a TREBEL Max tier rather than a conventional paid subscription. TREBEL is a consumer mobile product distributed through the Apple App Store, Google Play and Huawei AppGallery; it publishes no public developer program, API reference, SDK or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Universal Music Group
providers.description: Universal Music Group N.V. (UMG) is the world's largest music company, headquartered in Hilversum, Netherlands with operational headquarters in Santa Monica, California. Spun off from Vivendi and listed on Euronext Amsterdam (ticker: UMG) on September 21, 2021 at a EUR 54 billion valuation, UMG operates Recorded Music, Music Publishing (Universal Music Publishing Group / UMPG), and Merchandising (Bravado), plus film and television production (PolyGram Entertainment) and the artist services and catalog arm Universal Music Enterprises. The company is led by Chairman and CEO Sir Lucian Grainge. Major label families include Republic Corps (Republic, Island, Def Jam), Interscope Capitol Labels Group (Interscope, Geffen, A&M, Capitol, Blue Note, Motown), Virgin Music Group, Verve Label Group (Verve, Decca, Deutsche Grammophon, Impulse!, Philips), UMG Nashville (MCA Nashville, Mercury Nashville, EMI Records Nashville, Capitol Records Nashville), Universal Music Latin Entertainment, and Universal Music UK. Catalog scale exceeds 3 million recordings and 4 million compositions. Ownership is split among Bolloré / Vivendi (~28%), Tencent Music (~11%), Pershing Square (~10%), and the public float. UMG operates no public developer portal: catalog and metadata reach developers only indirectly through downstream DSPs (Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube, Amazon Music) and through partner / aggregator programs (7digital exposed UMG catalog under a partner API; that integration is the only third-party developer-facing surface that has ever been openly documented). Royalty and publishing portals (UMG Royalty Portal, UMPG Window) exist for songwriters and rights holders behind authentication, not as APIs. AI is the active integration vector in 2025-2026: UMG has announced licensed generative-music partnerships with Udio, Splice, KLAY Vision, SoundLabs, ProRata, BandLab, YouTube, TikTok, Meta, and KDDI, and has filed 15+ AI patents with Liquidax Capital across collaboration, rights management, music & health, and AI threat protection. These integrations operate through bilateral commercial agreements, not a self-serve developer program. The official Universal-Music-Group GitHub organization (created May 15, 2024) has 0 public repositories.

providers.name: AcoustID
providers.description: AcoustID is an open-source audio fingerprinting service providing a REST API for identifying music tracks by audio fingerprint and linking results to MusicBrainz metadata records. Built on the Chromaprint library, it offers a crowdsourced fingerprint database free for non-commercial use, with commercial plans available through AcoustID OÜ.

providers.name: Makrwatch
providers.description: Makrwatch is a creator representation and sponsorship management platform that sits between independent content creators and brands. It sources and filters brand-deal opportunities, negotiates terms and rates, protects creator IP and creative freedom, and handles the administrative work of briefs, timelines, revisions, invoicing, and payment tracking so creators can focus on producing content. Founded out of Y Combinator (W15) and based in New York City, the platform reports $27M+ distributed to creators across 34,000+ sponsorships for 7,400+ creators operating in 118 countries. The company was founded in 2013 as themidgame and still operates its GitHub organization under that name. Makrwatch does not publish a public developer API or documentation surface at this time: there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, SDK, MCP server or agent card anywhere on its public surface, and its two AWS API Gateway hosts (api.makrwatch.com and platform.makrwatch.com) are private backends for its own Creators and Brands applications, answering every unauthenticated request with HTTP 403.

providers.name: Skillshare
providers.description: Skillshare is a New York City–based online learning community for creators, founded in 2010 by Michael Karnjanaprakorn and Malcolm Ong. The platform hosts thousands of on-demand video classes across creative disciplines — illustration, design, photography, animation, lettering, film, productivity, writing, and business — taught by working creators and industry professionals. Skillshare operates on a paid subscription model (Premium membership) that grants members unlimited access to the class catalog, project-based learning, and a discussion community where students submit class projects for feedback. The company has a teacher revenue-share program in which class creators are paid based on watch time and student enrollments, and runs Skillshare for Teams as a B2B offering for organizations to give employees access to the catalog. Skillshare does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, partner API, or SDK. The platform's programmatic surface is limited to internal web/mobile clients and an affiliate/marketing referral program; there is no documented developer portal, public webhook system, or third-party integration API for the Skillshare catalog, enrollments, watch-time, or teacher-payout data.

providers.name: Teespring
providers.description: Teespring is a creator-commerce and print-on-demand platform, founded in 2011, that lets creators design, launch, and sell custom apparel and merchandise with no upfront cost or inventory, handling production, payment, and fulfillment on the creator's behalf. Backed by a16z, the company rebranded to "Spring" in 2021 and now operates as Amaze Commerce (part of Amaze Holdings): its consumer storefront lives at spri.ng while the creator/merchant SaaS platform runs at amazecommerce.com and amaze.co. As of this enrichment pass the company exposes no public developer API, developer portal, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, /.well-known discovery surface, or llms.txt; this profile therefore captures verified company identity and published site properties only.

providers.name: Soundtrap
providers.description: Soundtrap is an online music creation platform that lets users create, record, and collaborate on music projects directly in the browser. It offers a digital audio workstation with virtual instruments, loops, and effects, supporting both individual creators and educators. Users can share their tracks, collaborate in real-time, and access a library of royalty‑free sounds, making music production accessible without installing software.

providers.name: 1World Online
providers.description: 1World Online is an audience-engagement and interactive-advertising company, operating since 2012, that serves media publishers, advertisers and travel brands. Its platform embeds Interactive Media Units — polls, quizzes, trivia, debates and surveys — into publisher pages in 30+ languages, turns the resulting engagement into interactive ad inventory and first-party audience insight, and rewards participants through a points-based loyalty program and Web3 collectables (TravelVerse). The company also operates a technology center offering custom development and integration services. Its platform backend is live at app-wleu.1worldonline.com and serves the publisher portal, widget frontend and loyalty applications, but 1World Online publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable contract today, and the historic public Swagger UI host api.1worldonline.com no longer resolves.

providers.name: Affinity Technology (The Lobby)
providers.description: Affinity Technology, Inc. operates The Lobby (fromthelobby.com; app at tryaffinity.com), an invite-only creator-marketing marketplace connecting direct-to-consumer brands with content creators for product seeding, paid partnerships and user-generated content. Brands stock a Creator Closet that vetted creators request from, and the platform handles standardized one-click partnership offers, contracts, Shopify-driven fulfilment and shipment tracking, deliverable reminders, a content library and social-listening reporting. The company began as Affinity, an AI personalized-fashion recommendation service for brands and retailers (San Francisco, backed by 8VC, EquityZen ticker AFFI) and pivoted the same entity and domain to the creator-marketing product. It publishes NO developer program: no portal, no API reference, no OpenAPI/GraphQL/MCP surface, no api.* host, no public code org. Its only advertised integration is a Shopify connection configured inside the authenticated brand dashboard.

providers.name: Baton Media
providers.description: Baton is a music collaboration and IP-management platform for unreleased music, built by Baton Media Inc. (New York, Techstars '23). It gives musicians, producers, managers, and talent scouts tools to securely upload, organize, version, and share unreleased tracks, beat packs, and sample libraries across iOS and web. A proprietary media player shows creators exactly who is listening to their material, while collaboration spaces (private, invite-only, or public), an in-app audio studio (looping, pitch shifting, EQ, effects, sample pairing), and a creator-to-fan marketplace support discovery, placement opportunities, and monetization. Baton is building collaboration protocols to track IP rights and automate crediting and compensation across the creator economy. As of this enrichment the company publishes a consumer product (iOS app + web) with no public API, developer portal, or documentation.

providers.name: Bindery
providers.description: Bindery (Bindery Books) is a community-driven, influencer-led book publishing platform and marketplace founded by Matt Kaye and Meg Harvey. It pairs established book "tastemakers" — social-media book reviewers and BookTok / Bookstagram creators — with emerging authors, letting each tastemaker run their own micro-imprint (Ezeekat Press, Boundless Press, Skies Press, and others), acquire titles, weigh in on creative decisions, and promote them to their communities in exchange for a share of net earnings. Often described as "Patreon meets publishing," Bindery combines traditional trade distribution and marketing with paid membership communities, a bookshop, exclusive reviews and author interviews, and iOS and Android apps. The company is backed by Bloomberg Beta.

providers.name: BuzzFeed
providers.description: BuzzFeed Inc. is a digital media company founded in 2006 and headquartered in New York City, best known for its viral entertainment, quizzes, pop-culture coverage, and commerce content. The company operates a portfolio of brands including the flagship BuzzFeed site, the news operation HuffPost, and the food brand Tasty, and produces video, podcasts, and shoppable content across web and social platforms. BuzzFeed is a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: BZFD) and monetizes through advertising, brand partnerships, and commerce. It does not publish a general-purpose public developer API program; its public machine-readable surface consists of content syndication (RSS feeds), an advertising/partnerships business, and a security.txt vulnerability-disclosure program via HackerOne. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from an a16z portfolio lead and enriched with the provider's real public surface.

providers.name: DubClub
providers.description: DubClub is an all-in-one platform to create and join sports betting communities. It is a marketplace connecting sports betting content creators known as cappers or handicappers with subscribers who want timely, reliable betting picks and analysis. Creators monetize their expertise by selling picks and predictions through paid subscriptions, while subscribers receive content directly via notifications and messaging rather than scattered across social media and Discord. DubClub has facilitated tens of millions in payments for creators and delivered hundreds of millions of messages containing informational sports betting content. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital; DubClub publishes a consumer web product and does not expose a public developer API program at this time.

providers.name: Groover
providers.description: Groover is a music promotion platform that connects independent artists and their representatives with a network of more than 3,000 vetted music-industry professionals — playlist curators, bloggers, journalists, radio stations, record labels, and managers. Artists submit a track and spend credits ("Grooviz", roughly €2 each) to reach individual curators, and Groover guarantees personalized feedback within seven days or refunds the credit. Founded in Paris in 2018, the company also operates Temple by Groover, a fanbase-growth toolset. Groover runs a consumer web application on a credit-based, pay-per-submission model and publishes no public developer API.

providers.name: Kickstarter
providers.description: Kickstarter is a public-benefit crowdfunding platform where creators launch funding campaigns for creative projects — film, music, art, design, games, technology, publishing, and more — and backers pledge money to help bring them to life on an all-or-nothing funding model. Founded in 2009 and headquartered in Brooklyn, New York, it has channeled billions of dollars in pledges to hundreds of thousands of successfully funded projects. Kickstarter does not currently operate a public developer API program or developer portal; its GraphQL and REST endpoints power its own web and mobile clients and are not documented for third-party integration. The company does maintain an active open-source GitHub organization (including its iOS and Android app source), a help center, and a company blog. This API Evangelist profile tracks Kickstarter's public developer, security, and platform surface for discovery and enrichment.

providers.name: Novel Effect
providers.description: Novel Effect is a Techstars-backed interactive read-aloud technology company whose voice-recognition platform listens as a person reads a children's picture book aloud and plays perfectly synchronized music, sound effects, and character voices in response, turning any book into an immersive shared experience. Delivered through iOS, Android, and web apps, Novel Effect is used by families, teachers, and libraries to make reading aloud more engaging for young children. Novel Effect is a consumer and education (EdTech) product and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: Sol
providers.description: Sol Reader is a wearable e-reader — marketed as the world's first wearable e-reader — built by Sol and backed by Initialized Capital. The device is a lightweight (104g) headset with dual 1.3" 271ppi side-lit E Ink displays, adjustable diopter optics and IPD, a handheld remote, and 25+ hours of battery for a distraction-free reading experience. It reads a connected Kindle library and DRM-free EPUB uploads, offers the Sol Store with over one million titles, plus AI question-answering and an AutoPilot speed-reading mode. Sol is a consumer hardware company; it publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Songfinch
providers.description: Songfinch is a Chicago-based direct-to-consumer music gifting platform that pairs customers with a curated community of independent professional singer-songwriters to produce one-of-a-kind personalized songs. A buyer picks an artist by genre, mood and tempo, submits the story and details behind the occasion through a guided song builder, and the artist writes, records and delivers an original recording to a shareable song page, with add-on products spanning lyric prints, vinyl, CDs, sheet music, QR plaques, streaming release and rights upgrades. Songfinch operates a two-sided marketplace — a consumer storefront plus an artist application and artist admin — and has paid out tens of millions of dollars to independent artists. It publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or machine-readable contract; api.songfinch.com is a private first-party application backend for its own storefront.

providers.name: Take-Two Interactive Software
providers.description: Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. (NASDAQ: TTWO) is a US interactive-entertainment holding company headquartered in New York City that develops and publishes video games through its labels Rockstar Games, 2K, Zynga and Ghost Story Games. It is a Fortune 1000 corporation. Take-Two operates real API infrastructure — api.take2games.com and the T2GP (Take-Two Game Platform) API at api.t2gp.take2games.com, the backend behind its launcher and account system — but it runs no public developer program: no developer portal, no published reference, no machine-readable contract, no SDKs, and no plans or rate limits. Its developer-surface hosts (docs.take2games.com, dev.take2games.com) redirect every request to a FusionAuth SSO login.

providers.name: Twisty
providers.description: Twisty, operated by Bright Live Inc. (dba Twisty) of Santa Monica, California, is an AI character creation platform that lets creators generate lifelike AI characters and produce personalized, expressive video messages as an alternative to generic talking-head videos. The product ships as a web app plus iOS and Android apps with a free tier and a paid monthly plan, and is backed by Norwest Venture Partners. Twisty does not currently publish a public API, developer documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Autoblogging.ai
providers.description: Autoblogging.ai is an AI-powered article writing and autoblogging platform that researches top-ranking content, generates SEO-optimized blog posts in bulk, fact-checks them, and auto‑publishes to WordPress and other platforms. Founded in 2022 by Vaibhav Sharda, it serves over 40,000 content creators across 38 languages, offering features like keyword research, AI‑generated images, and brand visibility tracking.

providers.name: Egab
providers.description: Egab is a journalism platform founded in late 2020 and headquartered in Cairo, Egypt, that connects local journalists across the Global South — the Middle East, Africa, and beyond (60+ countries) — with international media outlets. It specializes in solutions journalism, offering journalists mentoring, editorial support, skills development, and fair compensation from pitch to publication, while giving newsrooms cost-efficient access to authentic, exclusive stories and diverse local contributors without flying in reporters.

providers.name: Luel
providers.description: Luel is a two-sided marketplace and multi-modal data lab for AI training data, connecting companies that need high-quality, rights-cleared datasets with verified contributors who supply and license on-demand video, audio, and image data. Contributors can earn money by submitting media from their own devices (for example, footage from their camera roll) or by completing requested data tasks, while buyers purchase premium, curated, rights-cleared multimodal datasets from the Luel catalog. Positioned as "the frontier of data," Luel powers the foundations of machine perception through a proprietary, continuous data engine. The company is backed by Y Combinator, General Catalyst, and Lightspeed Venture Partners. Luel does not currently publish a public API, SDK, or developer documentation surface.

providers.name: Palette 2
providers.description: Palette 2, operating as Palette, is a multimodal content creation platform that lets users generate, edit, and storyboard media across formats such as text, images, video, and audio. The service provides a unified canvas for marketing, education, entertainment, and brand storytelling, leveraging AI-driven tools to accelerate production and ensure consistency across audiences.

providers.name: Passes
providers.description: Passes is a creator monetization and accelerator platform founded in 2022 by Lucy Guo and headquartered in Los Angeles. Creators use Passes to build direct, paid relationships with their audiences through subscriptions, paid DMs, livestreams, one-on-one video calls, merchandise, automated message sequences, and instant payouts, while keeping 90% of what they earn. Backed by Bond Capital and Multicoin Capital, the company rebranded in 2026 as a creator accelerator. Passes does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile captures its real public web surface — llms.txt, security.txt, mobile deep-link association files, and domain-security posture — harvested by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Quuu
providers.description: Quuu provides an AI‑powered social media automation platform that creates, schedules, and publishes posts across X (Twitter), LinkedIn, Facebook, and Bluesky. The service learns a brand’s voice from existing content, generates AI‑crafted captions and images, and offers a dashboard for review and control. It targets creators, agencies, small teams, and businesses seeking consistent online presence without hiring a social media manager. Pricing is per connected profile with a free trial and no credit‑card required.

providers.name: Anker Innovations
providers.description: Anker Innovations is a global consumer-electronics company headquartered in Shenzhen, China, known for its Anker charging and power products, Soundcore audio, eufy smart-home and security devices, Nebula projectors, and Anker SOLIX portable power and solar storage. Through the Anker Open Platform (developer.anker.com) the company exposes a developer surface that lets partners integrate and control Anker devices from their own applications via API and SDK, gated behind an Open Platform login. This profile was surfaced as a portfolio company of IDG Capital and is being enriched with the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Jays
providers.description: JAYS is a Swedish consumer audio brand founded in 2006 by Jens and Johan, headquartered in Sweden and owned by the Northbaze Group AB. It designs and sells wireless and wired headphones, true-wireless earbuds, Bluetooth and multiroom speakers, and audio accessories, sold direct-to-consumer through a Shopify storefront at jaysheadphones.com. JAYS publishes no first-party developer API; its only machine-accessible surface is the Shopify-provided agent-commerce layer: a Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) merchant profile with a hosted MCP shopping endpoint, Customer Account OpenID Connect / OAuth discovery documents, and an llms.txt. This profile was surfaced as a Creandum portfolio/commitment lead and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline.

providers.name: Allcams
providers.description: Allcams is an adult live cam aggregator that indexes streams from multiple adult cam platforms, providing a unified searchable directory without hosting any content itself. The site offers age‑verification compliance, affiliate disclosures, and earns commission via referral links. It maintains legal compliance with U.S. 2257 record‑keeping, GDPR and CCPA, and provides a developer MCP server for AI agents. Allcams aims to keep listings honest by removing dead or duplicate entries and supporting multiple languages.

providers.name: Karat.io
providers.description: Karat (trykarat.com) is a fintech platform providing integrated business banking and financial tools built for entrepreneurs, content creators, agencies, and small businesses managing irregular income. Its product suite spans FDIC-insured business checking accounts with high APY, the Karat Card and Karat Max charge/credit cards with rewards and no annual fees, mass and international contractor payments, AI-powered bookkeeping with automatic transaction categorization, invoicing, and multi-entity team management. Surfaced as a portfolio company of ggv-capital and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; as of this pass Karat publishes a consumer web and mobile app but no public developer program, API documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: Memorick
providers.description: Memorick is a 500 Global-backed company operating a live web application at memorick.com. Based on its observable application surface, it is a destination photography booking platform connecting customers with photographers across destinations, handling packages, orders, reviews, coupons, and messaging. The product is built on Laravel (Inertia.js single-page front end) and exposes an OAuth2 authorization server via Laravel Passport (authorize/token/clients/scopes plus personal access tokens), Sanctum first-party session auth, and optional two-factor authentication. It publishes no public API documentation, OpenAPI definition, SDKs, or developer portal at this time; the /api/* routes back the first-party application and are authentication-gated. This profile was enriched from live probing of the public surface.

providers.name: Spinitron
providers.description: Spinitron provides a web-based music playlist management platform for radio stations and music businesses. It offers tools for scheduling, charting, and audience engagement, supporting both community and commercial broadcasters. The service includes features such as automated playlists, detailed analytics, and integration with various streaming services, helping stations curate and manage their music content efficiently.

providers.name: Changelog
providers.description: Changelog is a media company and podcast network for developers covering open source and software development. Founded by Adam Stacoviak and Jerod Santo, Changelog produces world-class developer podcasts including The Changelog, which features deep technical interviews and conversations with the people and teams driving open source software forward. Changelog also publishes a weekly developer news newsletter and operates an open source platform (changelog.com) built with Elixir and Phoenix.

providers.name: Hashtag Paid
providers.description: Hashtag Paid Inc., which trades as #paid, is a Toronto-headquartered creator marketing platform that connects brands and agencies with social media creators. The product is a marketplace and campaign workspace: brands brief a campaign, are matched to vetted creators, review and approve content, license and amplify that content as paid social advertising across Meta, TikTok, YouTube, Snapchat and Pinterest, then measure results and pay creators automatically. #paid is a badged TikTok Marketing Partner and consumes the social platforms' advertising APIs on its customers' behalf. It runs as an end-user SaaS product with brand and creator web applications; as of this profile it publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable contract.

providers.name: Instaread
providers.description: Instaread is a media and audio technology company with two products. Its consumer app delivers ~15-minute audio and text summaries of bestselling books across business, self-help, history, health, politics, and fiction on mobile, tablet, and desktop. Its publisher product, Instaread Player, is a free embeddable audio widget that uses AI text-to-speech (including custom voice cloning) to convert website articles, blogs, and newsletters into natural-sounding audio, monetized for publishers through programmatic audio advertising. The Player is used by 200+ brands, ships ADA/WCAG accessibility support, an analytics dashboard, podcast distribution, and a WordPress plugin, and works on Squarespace, Wix, Webflow, and custom sites via a single embed code. Instaread does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Pratilipi
providers.description: Pratilipi is India's largest digital storytelling platform, democratizing story creation and consumption across languages, formats, and boundaries. Built by Nasadiya Technologies Private Limited and headquartered in Bangalore, it lets more than 300,000 self-published writers reach roughly 25 million monthly readers across twelve Indian languages (Hindi, Gujarati, Marathi, Bengali, English, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Punjabi, Urdu, and Odia). The ecosystem spans Pratilipi Literature, Pratilipi FM (audio books, podcasts, and folk songs), Pratilipi Comics (the largest Hindi online comic platform), Westland Publications, and IVM Podcasts, carrying a story "from someone's draft to someone's screen." Pratilipi does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures the company's identity, web properties, and domain-security posture for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: 9GAG
providers.description: 9GAG is a Hong Kong-based global entertainment platform founded in 2008 with the mission to "make the world happier." It is one of the largest meme and user-generated humor communities on the internet, distributing funny images, GIFs, and videos across its website and iOS/Android apps to an audience of 150-200 million people and billions of monthly video views. 9GAG operates consumer-facing products (the 9GAG feed, 9GAG Pro subscription, and related community features) rather than a public developer API program; it was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a venture-backed company (500 Global, Y Combinator, Freestyle Capital, True Ventures, First Round Capital, Greycroft) and has been enriched with its real public web, policy, and security surfaces. No official public API or developer portal is published as of this enrichment; the community libraries that exist are unofficial and reverse-engineered.

providers.name: Cameo
providers.description: Cameo is a consumer marketplace for personalized video messages from celebrities, athletes, musicians, comedians, and creators. Fans book a custom shout-out by sending a short script with personal details, and the talent records and delivers a bespoke video, typically within seven days, for occasions like birthdays, milestones, and celebrations. Cameo also runs Cameo for Business for branded talent content, sells gift cards, and offers a Red Carpet Rewards loyalty program. Cameo does not publish a public developer API or OpenAPI; this profile tracks the company's public web, help, and security surface.

providers.name: Chain of Thought
providers.description: Chain of Thought is a podcast exploring AI infrastructure, featuring hosts and guests from leading tech companies. It discusses evolving AI tools, platforms, and research, providing insights for builders and enthusiasts. The show covers topics like hardware, software, and industry trends, aiming to inform and inspire the AI community.

providers.name: Icon Source
providers.description: Icon Source is a Denver, Colorado marketplace that connects brands, marketing agencies and universities with professional and college athletes for endorsement, appearance, speaking and social-media deals, including Name, Image and Likeness (NIL) engagements. Founded in 2018 by Chase Garrett, the platform lets brands search and filter verified athletes by location, interest, rate, audience size and demographics, build and send contracts, and pay athletes in-platform, charging a 10% transaction fee on each deal that is signed and closed. A companion product, Icon Suite (launched March 2022), gives universities NIL disclosure and compliance tooling. Icon Source is delivered strictly as an end-user product — a web application at prod.iconsource.app plus iOS and Android apps — and publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal or machine-readable contract of any kind.

providers.name: Audioknihy.cz
providers.description: audioknihy-cz is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: mcp-registry) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: ReverbNation
providers.description: ReverbNation is a music platform that helps artists grow their careers by offering distribution, promotion tools, publishing, and opportunities to connect with industry professionals. Musicians can release music to major streaming services, access marketing resources, and explore revenue options through cash advances and sync licensing. The service provides a suite of tools for audience building, fan engagement, and career development, supporting both emerging and established artists worldwide.

providers.name: STORI AI
providers.description: STORI AI is a San Francisco-based AI content-marketing platform that helps brands define their identity — archetype, tone, tagline, and colors — and turn that identity into on-brand social posts, graphics, images, videos, and go-to-market marketing materials. The product generates personalized branded content, schedules and publishes it across digital platforms, and offers analytics, content storage, and multi-brand, multi-language, team-collaboration tiers. A Product Hunt Golden Kitty Award recipient, STORI AI is a web SaaS application for marketers and brand teams; it exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: TourHero
providers.description: TourHero is a social travel platform and end-to-end group trip operations partner that lets creators, coaches, and community leaders host fully customized group trips in 50+ countries, with itinerary design, vetted local operators, payments, and on-the-ground logistics handled by TourHero. Travelers can browse and book public trips on its Explore page, and hosts plan for free while TourHero earns commission from local suppliers. Backed by 500 Global and Lightspeed Venture Partners, it is a consumer platform with no publicly documented developer API surface at this time, though it publishes an llms.txt profile for AI agents.

providers.name: Qsic
providers.description: Qsic (styled QSIC) is an Australian-founded, AI-driven in-store audio and retail media platform, headquartered in Melbourne with a North American office in Dallas, Texas. The platform blends curated music, targeted audio advertising and store-level intelligence, deploying either over a retailer's existing speaker infrastructure or over premium smart speakers, and adapting playback to ambient conditions, dayparts and shopper behaviour. Qsic sells three connected products — In-Store Audio, Ads and Intelligence — and positions the combination as a way to turn physical stores into measurable retail media networks with store-level performance reporting and demand-side platform integration. Publicly reported deployments include 7-Eleven ("Gulp Radio"), Dollar General, Coles Liquor and Mecca. Qsic runs a live JSON API host at api.getqsic.com and a Vanta-hosted trust center, but publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable specification as of this profile.

providers.name: Copify
providers.description: Copify is a digital marketing agency that provides services such as paid media, SEO, web design, social media marketing, content creation, and e‑commerce marketing to businesses across various industries. It offers consulting and campaign management to help clients increase conversions, grow revenue, and manage ad spend.

providers.name: Discz
providers.description: Discz is a consumer mobile application that blends music discovery with social chat, styled as a modern, MySpace-inspired music community. Users discover songs, build music profiles, and chat with others around shared taste in music. The iOS app is developed by Discz, a Y Combinator-backed startup and a portfolio company of DCM Ventures. Discz publishes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal; its surface is the consumer iOS app distributed through the Apple App Store.

providers.name: SmartShoot
providers.description: SmartShoot is a San Francisco-based (founded 2012) photography and video production platform that connects enterprises and marketing teams with a managed network of more than 200,000 professional photographers and videographers to produce custom, on-brand photo and video content at scale. The web-based platform coordinates shoot booking, project collaboration, editing, and cloud-based delivery across many locations, serving e-commerce, real estate, and multi-location brands such as Google, YouTube, Uber, Expedia, and Yelp. SmartShoot is a B2B managed-service marketplace with no publicly documented developer API, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI specification, SDK, MCP server, or developer portal as of this enrichment pass; it was surfaced as a portfolio company of Uncork Capital.

providers.name: Svbtle
providers.description: Svbtle is a minimalist publishing and blogging platform designed to work the way your brain does, pairing a distraction-free Markdown editor with a simple dashboard for organizing drafts, developing ideas, and publishing to a clean reading experience. Created by Dustin Curtis and operated by Neutral Corporation, Svbtle emphasizes longevity through its "Forever Promise" that published writing remains permanently accessible online. Svbtle is a subscription-based writer's network rather than a developer platform: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public API, developer portal, OpenAPI definition, OAuth authorization server, or .well-known metadata, and each blog is exposed only as a human-readable site with an RSS feed.

providers.name: The Atavist
providers.description: The Atavist is a pioneering digital longform-storytelling brand founded in 2009 by Evan Ratliff, Jefferson Rabb, and Nicholas Thompson. It comprises The Atavist Magazine, which publishes one immersive work of narrative nonfiction each month and has earned National Magazine Award and Emmy recognition, and the Atavist multimedia publishing platform for building rich, media-driven stories. Automattic (the company behind WordPress.com) acquired both the magazine and the platform in 2018; the platform's storytelling features were folded into WordPress.com and the magazine now runs on Newspack by Automattic. The Atavist exposes no public developer API or documented developer program — it is a reader-facing publication at magazine.atavist.com.

providers.name: alphin
providers.description: alphin is a Berlin-based marketing platform for local small businesses, giving restaurants, cafes, salons, and similar SMBs an all-in-one app to manage and automate their online presence. Its product suite spans review collection (alphin Reviews), Instagram and social management (alphin Socials), professional photography (alphin Photos), local influencer marketing (alphin Local Influencers), targeted Instagram advertising (alphin Local Ads), and multi-platform profile management across Google, TripAdvisor, and Yelp (alphin Portals), consolidated into one dashboard with daily reporting and analytics. Founded in 2016 (as Freachly GmbH), alphin serves 1,000+ local businesses across Germany, Austria, the UK, and Israel, and is backed by HV Capital, Partech, Scale Capital, and Wille Finance. alphin publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs; the product is delivered through its web and mobile Business App.

providers.name: Cirrus Logic
providers.description: Cirrus Logic designs and manufactures high-performance analog and mixed-signal semiconductors for audio, voice, and IoT applications. The company provides audio codecs, amplifiers, and digital signal processors used in consumer electronics, automotive, and industrial devices. Its solutions enable high-fidelity sound, efficient power management, and advanced connectivity across a wide range of products worldwide.

providers.name: Spotter
providers.description: Spotter is a creator-economy platform that invests in YouTube creators through capital, catalog licensing, and brand partnerships, and connects brands with top long-form YouTube creators for marketing and content opportunities. Its Spotter Studio product provides AI-assisted tooling that helps creators plan, ideate, and optimize their content and titles. The company reports more than $1 billion invested in creators and over 43 billion monthly views across a network that includes creators such as MrBeast, Critical Role, and Sam and Colby. Spotter is backed by SoftBank Vision Fund. Spotter publishes no public developer API: contract discovery on 2026-08-13 found no OpenAPI, GraphQL SDL, AsyncAPI, MCP server or A2A agent card on any Spotter host, and the Spotter Studio application backends return 503 to anonymous callers. Spotter Studio is a consumer of the YouTube Data and Analytics APIs via Google OAuth, not a provider of one.

providers.name: roli
providers.description: ROLI (Luminary ROLI Ltd.) is a British music-technology company known for expressive electronic instruments — the Seaboard, LUMI Keys keyboards, and the modular BLOCKS system — together with companion software such as ROLI Dashboard, ROLI Connect, Equator, and ROLI Learn. Its instruments pioneer MPE (MIDI Polyphonic Expression) for per-note pitch, timbre, and dynamics control. For developers, ROLI publishes first-party SDKs under the github.com/weareroli organization — the C++ BLOCKS-SDK and roli_blocks_basics for building applications that talk to BLOCKS hardware, and the archived mpejs library for MPE MIDI in the browser. ROLI is backed by Balderton Capital and Index Ventures. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio lead and enriched with real developer, SDK, and domain-security artifacts.

providers.name: Solve Data
providers.description: Solve Data provides a marketing automation platform that simplifies content creation, message personalization, and campaign management. It removes complexity by offering reusable content blocks, intelligent frequency management, and real‑time analytics, helping brands deliver targeted messages without manual effort. The solution includes audience segmentation, decision engine, and audit trails, and is trusted by enterprises for scalable, data‑driven communications.

providers.name: AMC Global Media
providers.description: AMC Global Media Inc. (NASDAQ: AMCX), known as AMC Networks until its 2026 rebrand, is a global entertainment company that owns and operates AMC, BBC America, IFC, SundanceTV and We TV, the AMC+, Acorn TV, Shudder, Sundance Now, HIDIVE and ALLBLK streaming services, AMC Studios, IFC Films and AMC Networks International. It distributes 33 FAST channels across 22 platforms and sells advertising through its Audience+ audience data platform and AMCN Outcomes measurement product. The company publishes no public developer program and no machine-readable API contract: affiliate distribution runs through a login-gated partner portal, advertising is booked through sales, and broadcast delivery is contracted through its Broadcasting & Technology group. The legacy domain www.amcnetworks.com now redirects to www.amcglobalmedia.com.

providers.name: Pixyalbum
providers.description: Pixyalbum is a Mexican consumer photo-printing service that turns digital photos from a mobile device into physical printed products delivered across Mexico. Its catalog includes Fotolibros (soft- and hard-cover photo books of 40-100 pages), Imanes (packs of square photo magnets), and Pixycuadros (photographic prints with optional framing). Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. Pixyalbum is a direct-to-consumer product with no public API, developer portal, or documentation at the time of enrichment; this profile captures its public identity and web properties.

providers.name: DistroKid
providers.description: DistroKid is a Brooklyn, New York based digital music distribution service founded in 2013 by Philip Kaplan that lets independent musicians and labels upload an unlimited number of songs and albums to Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon Music, YouTube Music, TikTok, Instagram, Pandora, Tidal, Deezer, and dozens of other streaming and download stores for a flat annual subscription fee while keeping 100% of their royalties. By 2020 the platform was distributing roughly a third of all new music released worldwide and serving more than two million artists; Spotify and Insight Partners both hold equity stakes following a 2021 valuation around $1.3B. Around the core distribution product DistroKid has built out a suite of artist services including Teams for automated royalty splits, cover-song mechanical licensing, YouTube Content ID monetization, DistroVid music-video distribution, Upstream label matching, Mixea AI mastering, and DistroKid Direct for fan merchandising and pre-orders. The company has historically operated without a public developer API — integrations with stores, DSPs, rights organizations, and partners are handled through private B2B arrangements, and the only public web endpoints exposed under distrokid.com/api are unauthenticated pre-save widgets used to drive Spotify follow/save campaigns. DistroKid is actively hiring API engineers to scale partner and AI-facing integrations, suggesting a more formal developer surface may emerge, but as of 2026 there is no published OpenAPI specification, SDK, CLI, sandbox, or developer portal. Third-party reverse-engineered wrappers such as the unofficial Golang `distrogo` library exist but are not endorsed.

providers.name: Lapse
providers.description: Lapse is a London-founded consumer photo company (Lapse Ltd) whose iOS app turns an iPhone into a disposable camera - a one-tap Lock Screen shutter, a film "developing" delay, and a friends-only photo journal built on a "Friends not followers" thesis of no ads, no data sales, and no public follower counts. The app is invite and friends-gated Early Access, free to use, iOS only, and screens uploads with AI moderation; contacts are hashed and encrypted on device. Lapse is backed by Greylock, GV and Speedinvest. It publishes no public API, developer portal, SDKs or documentation as of the July 2026 enrichment pass, so this profile captures company identity, the published policy and support surface, and probed security posture rather than an API surface.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: HYPERZ AI
providers.description: HYPERZ AI is a generative-AI company focused on professional photography and headshot generation, offering both consumer (B2C) and enterprise (B2B) products. Its consumer tool, Business Photo AI (businessphoto.ai), turns selfies into professional headshots with customizable poses, outfits, and backgrounds. Its enterprise product, HYPERTURE (hyperture.ai), delivers consistent, studio-grade headshots for teams with brand-consistency controls, member approval workflows, and C2PA provenance verification. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of the venture firm qiming and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass it publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation, or /.well-known discovery surface — the products are end-user applications rather than a developer platform.

providers.name: Airblack
providers.description: Airblack (Airblack Technologies Private Limited) is a Gurugram, India-based edtech company that runs an outcome-focused skilling academy for creators and micro-entrepreneurs, delivering live online makeup, beauty and culinary courses with professional certification through its website and Android/iOS app, plus a sister app, Zudo. Founded by Videt Jaiswal and backed by Info Edge Ventures and Elevation Capital (USD 5.2M Series A, 2021), it reports a community of 45,000+ students. Airblack is a consumer learning product, not a platform: it publishes no developer program, no public API documentation and no machine-readable API contract, and the backend its web app calls (service.ablck.com) is a private application service that answers every probed path with a JSON 404.

providers.name: Humans Anonymous
providers.description: Humans Anonymous is a consumer mobile application offering anonymous audio spaces for mental health and peer support, built on the premise that "being a human is hard" and no one should face it alone. Distributed as an iOS app, it lets people join anonymous, real-time audio rooms to talk and listen around mental wellbeing. Surfaced as a portfolio company of General Catalyst and added to the API Evangelist network; the company publishes a consumer product website (humansanon.com) with privacy and terms pages but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Kuli
providers.description: Kuli is an AI agent for influencer marketing, built for consumer brands. It runs the full creator marketing lifecycle end to end — discovery, vetting, outreach, and reporting — so a small marketing team ships like a much larger one. Unlike platforms that filter creators on metadata such as follower counts and engagement rates, Kuli's agent watches actual creator videos frame by frame across TikTok and Instagram, assessing brand safety, content style, audience signals, and brand fit, then drafts personalized outreach in the brand's own voice and reports campaign ROI on a schedule. Founded in 2025 and headquartered in Levallois-Perret, Paris, Kuli is a Y Combinator company. As of this profile Kuli publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs — its only machine-readable surface is an llms.txt.

providers.name: LANDR
providers.description: LANDR is a creative platform for musicians offering AI‑powered mastering, distribution, sample libraries, plugins, and collaborative tools. It provides a suite of services including LANDR Studio, mastering plugins, a marketplace for samples and plugins, online courses, and tools for music creators to release and monetize their work worldwide.

providers.name: Prologue
providers.description: Prologue (Prologue AI) is a multimodal creative operating system that lets teams create, edit, and organize AI-generated images, video, audio, and text in a single workspace. Powered by "Prologue Intent" and a best-in-class catalog of third-party generative models, it targets professional creative workflows for agencies and brands ("crafted, not generated"). It was surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network as a stub for enrichment. As of this pass no public developer API, documentation, or SDK surface was discoverable — the product site is a consumer/pro web application behind bot protection.

providers.name: Noodle
providers.description: Noodle is a Brazilian fintech building financial infrastructure for the creator economy. It provides automated payouts to creators, influencers, and vendors; FastPay early access to future earnings; noodleOS, a unified platform for campaigns, creator data, payments, and asset tracking; global payouts powered by Ebanx; foreign-exchange settlement; and credit and capital products underwritten in part on a creator's social presence. Backed by QED Investors, Noodle serves media companies, agencies, and platforms that pay content creators. The company references API-based integrations but publishes no public developer portal or API documentation.

providers.name: Open Podcast API
providers.description: The Open Podcast API is an initiative aiming to provide a feature-complete synchronization API specification for podcast (web) apps and user-focused servers. The specification covers synchronization of subscriptions, listening progress, favorites, queues, and device state across compliant clients and self-hosted servers, with the goal of giving listeners portable control of their podcast data.

providers.name: Tone
providers.description: Tone is a full-stack royalty management platform for music rights owners — independent labels, distributors, and royalty teams. It centralizes royalty accounting, income tracking, and contract management, then pays artists directly through integrated global payouts. The platform processes large royalty periods quickly, provides near-real-time sales intelligence with timeline views and customizable charts, models deal structures with a contract simulator (reserves, deductions, escalations), automatically associates costs with the applicable royalty periods, and gives artists transparent dashboards into their earnings. In-app artist payouts are powered by Airwallex for secure multi-currency international payments, letting labels pay artists and partners worldwide without juggling separate banking tools. Tone is backed by QED Investors. This profile was added to the API Evangelist network from a VC-portfolio lead; Tone is a SaaS application and does not currently publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal.

providers.name: Artbook Society
providers.description: Artbook Society is an international platform for art publishing, offering a permanent festival of art and photography books, limited editions and prints directly from independent publishers and self‑published artists worldwide. It connects artists, publishers, and collectors, fostering a global community of art enthusiasts.

providers.name: Bmat
providers.description: BMAT Music Innovators provides a music operating system that aggregates and processes usage data across the music industry. Founded in Barcelona in 2006, BMAT offers solutions for DSP processing, VOD processing, UGC tracking, reporting, and rights management, enabling faster, data‑driven decisions for artists, labels, broadcasters, and AI companies. The platform connects every usage source, from radio to streaming, to deliver comprehensive analytics and revenue insights.

providers.name: Booko
providers.description: Booko is an Australian book, eBook, audiobook, DVD, music and collectibles price-comparison service operating since 2007. It aggregates new and used prices across many online retailers and regions, calculates shipping, and converts international prices to the shopper's local currency to surface the cheapest place to buy a title. Booko also offers shopping lists with bundled shipping calculations, barcode scanning, reading lists, price alerts and notifications. It is a consumer-facing comparison site rather than a retailer or a public API provider, earning referral fees from partner shops (including Amazon Associates) when shoppers buy through its links. Booko is a solo developer-run product surfaced through the API Evangelist network as a Y Combinator portfolio company.

providers.name: B612
providers.description: B612 is a consumer selfie and beauty camera application for iOS and Android, published globally by SNOW Corporation and operated in mainland China as B612咔叽 (B612 Kaji) by Yiruike Information Technology (Beijing) Co., Ltd. The app combines a real-time beauty camera, AR stickers and scene effects, user-created and creator-published filters, and photo and video editing tools, and has been distributed through the Apple App Store and Google Play since 2014. B612 is a mobile end-user product rather than an API provider: as of this enrichment pass the company publishes no developer portal, no public API documentation, no SDKs, and no machine-readable API artifacts on any of its web properties.

providers.name: Xperi
providers.description: Xperi Inc. (NYSE: XPER) is an entertainment technology company whose licensed technologies power audio, video, and media discovery experiences across connected cars, consumer electronics, pay-TV, and streaming media platforms. Its brands include DTS immersive audio, HD Radio digital broadcast radio, IMAX Enhanced certification, and the TiVo video platform. Xperi ships its technologies to automakers, device makers, and video providers through commercial licensing and integration programs rather than a public developer API; no public developer portal or API documentation was found, though its TiVo engineering organization maintains an open-source presence on GitHub.

providers.name: All City Network
providers.description: ALLCITY Network (All City Network) is a sports media and podcasting company built on the tagline "Sports Over Everything." It operates a set of city-based sports networks — DNVR (Denver), PHNX (Phoenix), CHGO (Chicago), PHLY (Philadelphia), and DLLS (Dallas) — that produce team-focused podcasts, video shows, and written coverage of local professional and collegiate sports, alongside network-wide shows and NBA/NFL programming. The company reaches fans through audio and video podcasts, memberships, and a merchandise store. It is a Bullpen Capital portfolio company and is not an API provider; it publishes no developer portal, documentation, or API, so the API-specific artifacts of the enrichment pipeline are not applicable.

providers.name: Audible
providers.description: Audible is an Amazon-owned online audiobook, podcast, and spoken-word entertainment service. It sells and streams audiobooks, Audible Originals, and podcasts through membership plans and a la carte purchases, delivered via web, iOS, Android, Alexa, and Kindle apps. Audible does not operate a public developer program or documented API — its catalog, library, and playback endpoints are a private internal API consumed by its own first-party apps. Community projects (the mkb79/Audible Python library, audible-cli, and omarroth/audible.cr) reverse-engineer that internal API; none are first-party or officially supported. This profile catalogs Audible's public web, help, and legal surface plus the unofficial client ecosystem.

providers.name: AudioMuse-AI
providers.description: AudioMuse-AI is an open‑source, self‑hosted music analysis platform that uses sonic fingerprinting and AI to rediscover forgotten songs, generate intelligent playlists, and visualize music libraries. It integrates with popular self‑hosted media servers such as Navidrome, Jellyfin, LMS, Lyrion, Emby, and Plex, offering features like multi‑server support, clustering, instant playlist generation, music map visualizations, lyric and text search, and audio‑recording based song identification, all without relying on external metadata services.

providers.name: Awa Studios
providers.description: AWA Studios (Artists, Writers & Artisans, Inc.) is a New York-based independent multimedia entertainment company founded in 2018 by comics-industry veterans, including former Marvel editor-in-chief Axel Alonso and former Marvel president Bill Jemas, with media executive Jon Miller as board chairman. AWA publishes original comic books and graphic novels across action, crime, horror, science fiction, and fantasy genres, built around a creator-owned business model that offers favorable terms to writers and artists. The company operates the "Upshot" imprint and a shared "Resistance Universe," runs a direct-to-consumer shop for print and digital titles, and develops film and television adaptations of its properties. AWA received seed-stage funding from Lightspeed Venture Partners in 2018. It is a media and entertainment company and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: BeReal
providers.description: BeReal is a French social media application that encourages authentic, unfiltered daily sharing through a two-minute random notification window in which users capture a moment using both the front and rear cameras simultaneously. Positioned as an alternative to curated, algorithmic social media, it emphasizes genuine connection over performance and explicitly excludes AI-generated content from the platform. Founded in France and acquired by mobile publisher Voodoo, BeReal operates a consumer mobile product with a help center and an advertising business, but publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or SDKs. This API Evangelist profile was surfaced via a16z and Accel portfolio data and enriched with the provider's real public web properties and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Blue Wire
providers.description: Blue Wire is a podcast network and monetization platform built for independent sports content creators, positioning itself as "The Monetization Engine for Sports Creators." The company provides sales, marketing, distribution, and operational support so creators can focus on producing content while Blue Wire handles ad sales and sponsorship coordination across a network of 200+ shows and 500+ creators reaching hundreds of millions of listeners. Backed by 500 Global. Blue Wire operates as a media and advertising business and does not publish a public developer API; this profile captures its company identity and domain-security posture within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Castbox
providers.description: Castbox is a free cross-platform podcast and audio content platform that lets listeners discover, stream, download, and manage millions of podcasts, audiobooks, and radio shows across Apple iOS, Android, Amazon Alexa, Google Home, CarPlay, Android Auto, and the web. Alongside its consumer listening apps, Castbox offers a "For Podcasters" suite for creators to host, distribute, and monetize their shows. Surfaced as a portfolio company of Qiming Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network, Castbox is a consumer audio company that publishes no public developer API portal; this profile captures its public identity, legal, and support surface.

providers.name: Jellysmack
providers.description: Jellysmack is a content amplification and creator-growth platform that helps digital creators expand their audiences and earnings across multiple social platforms (YouTube, Facebook, Snapchat, TikTok, Instagram) using AI-driven optimization, first-party data, and multi-platform distribution expertise. Its offerings span the Creator Program (audience growth and monetization for 500+ creator partners), Jellysmack Originals (owned beauty, sports, gaming, and entertainment channels), media licensing, and brand partnerships. The company reports 10B+ monthly video views and 125M+ monthly U.S. unique viewers. It is a consumer/creator-facing media technology company and does not publish a public developer API; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network for company/portfolio intelligence.

providers.name: Kale
providers.description: Kale (operated by Palette Technologies, Inc., dba Kale) is a creator-rewards and user-generated-content marketplace that connects social-media content creators with brands. Creators join brand challenges and tournaments, post authentic sponsored content about products they use, and earn cash, merchandise, and perks; brands source authentic UGC and micro-influencer marketing at scale. The platform is delivered through the getkale.com and kalecard.com web apps and native iOS/Android apps, with a merchant network spanning consumer brands such as Chili's, Planet Fitness, Urban Outfitters, DoorDash, Southwest, and Starbucks. Kale is backed by Forerunner Ventures. No public developer/API surface is published; this profile captures the company's public identity and security posture.

providers.name: Marshall
providers.description: Marshall is a Swedish-British consumer audio brand, part of Marshall Group AB, known for its iconic guitar amplifiers and a modern line of Bluetooth speakers, wireless headphones, and earbuds. Built on more than 60 years of live-music heritage, Marshall sells direct-to-consumer through marshall.com across amps, home and portable speakers, and personal audio. It was added to the API Evangelist network as a consumer portfolio company of HongShan. Marshall publishes no public developer API, developer portal, or API documentation at this time; this profile captures its public web identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: MeetMe
providers.description: MeetMe is a consumer social-discovery and chat platform that helps people find and connect with new people nearby who share their interests, through profiles, feeds, live streaming, and real-time messaging on web and mobile. Operated by The Meet Group as part of the ParshipMeet Group, MeetMe grew out of the myYearbook social network and today runs as a location-aware social networking and dating-adjacent app. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and Norwest Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass MeetMe publishes no public developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI, or SDKs — this profile captures its identity, legal surface, and live domain-security posture only.

providers.name: Momox
providers.description: momox SE (formerly Momox AG / Momox GmbH) is a Berlin-based re-commerce company founded by Christian Wegner in 2004 — the name stands for "Moderner Medien Online Express-Ankauf" (Modern Media Online Express Purchase). Through momox.de it buys used books, CDs, DVDs/Blu-rays and games from private sellers at fixed prices in Germany, Austria, France, Belgium and the UK, reselling them via its Medimops shop and third-party marketplaces. Its momox fashion arm (formerly ubup.com, momoxfashion.com) does the same for second-hand clothing, shoes and accessories. momox runs large logistics centres in Berlin, Leipzig and Neuenhagen bei Berlin and has handled more than 350 million articles since founding. momox is a consumer-facing re-commerce operation; it publishes no official public developer program, API portal, or SDKs. The only machine surface is an internal, undocumented mobile-app pricing endpoint (api.momox.de / api.momox.fr) that is not offered as a first-party API.

providers.name: Tactile Games
providers.description: Tactile Games is a Danish mobile game studio headquartered in Copenhagen, founded in 2014, that builds and publishes casual free-to-play puzzle titles for iOS and Android. Its portfolio includes Lily's Garden, Penny & Flo, Makeover Match, the Cookie Cats series (Cookie Cats, Cookie Cats Pop, Cookie Cats Blast), and the Simon's Cat games. Tactile is a portfolio company of Index Ventures. It is a consumer game publisher rather than an API producer: it exposes no public developer API, SDK, or developer portal, so this profile captures the company identity, public web properties, and domain-security posture surfaced by the enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: TheSkimm
providers.description: TheSkimm is a digital media company founded in 2012 that curates news, lifestyle, money, career, and wellness content for a primarily female audience, delivered through email newsletters (the flagship Daily Skimm, plus Well Played, Skimm Well + Good, and Skimm Shopping), a mobile app, podcasts, and shopping guides. It is now part of Everyday Health, Inc., a Ziff Davis company. TheSkimm operates as a consumer media and audience business rather than an API provider: it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or machine-readable API specifications. This API Evangelist profile was seeded as a portfolio lead of GV (Google Ventures) and enriched with the company's public identity, link properties, and domain-security posture.

providers.name: TuneCore
providers.description: TuneCore is a Brooklyn, New York based independent music distribution and publishing administration company founded in 2006 (as YourTunes, Inc., rebranded TuneCore in 2008) and acquired by French music company Believe in 2015. TuneCore lets self-releasing artists and labels deliver recorded music to 150+ digital stores and streaming services — Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon Music, YouTube Music, TikTok, Tidal, Deezer, Beatport, and others — while retaining 100% of their rights and master ownership, in exchange for a flat annual distribution fee starting at $24.99/year for unlimited releases. TuneCore Publishing Administration registers compositions with performance rights organizations, mechanical rights societies, and digital service providers worldwide to collect songwriter royalties, sync, and neighboring rights income. Additional services include the TuneCore Accelerator artist development program, TuneCore Social (monetization on TikTok, Reels, and Shorts), TuneCore Direct Advance (royalty-backed capital, powered by RoyFi), mastering, and Splits for collaborator revenue sharing. TuneCore operates across 5 continents with local teams in 15+ countries through Believe's global network. There is no current public TuneCore developer API, SDK, or partner portal — an earlier white-label REST/XML "TuneCore Direct" partner API existed circa 2008-2012 (with a community Ruby gem `tunecore_direct`) but is no longer actively documented or promoted. TuneCore's public-facing surface is the artist web app at web.tunecore.com and the support/help center; any current B2B integrations run through Believe's enterprise partnerships.

providers.name: Duetti
providers.description: Duetti is a New York-headquartered music finance and catalog services company founded in 2022 by Lior Tibon and Christopher Nolte that buys music rights directly from independent artists, songwriters and creators. Artists earning at least $2,000 a year from tracks at least six months old can sell masters, publishing shares or a percentage of their royalties for an upfront cash payment — no debt, interest or recoupment — while keeping whatever they do not sell. Alongside the catalog purchases Duetti provides distribution, royalty tracking and claiming, playlisting across a network of owned Spotify playlists, sync placement, paid advertising, influencer and UGC campaigns, and a commissioned remix program. The company has raised more than $435 million, works with 1,100+ music creators, and publishes the Music Economics Report and the Billboard Music Finance Index. Duetti operates artist-facing web applications (DUO onboarding, statements vault, sync portal) but publishes no public developer API, SDK, or machine-readable API contract as of this profile.

providers.name: Endel
providers.description: Endel is a wellness technology company that generates personalized, adaptive soundscapes to help people focus, relax, sleep, and stay active. Its patented technology creates endless real-time audio that responds to inputs such as time of day, weather, circadian rhythm, heart rate, and location, delivered across iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, web, Apple Watch, Apple TV, Amazon Fire TV, and Alexa. Endel is a consumer application; as of this profile it does not publish a public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface, so this repo captures its identity and public web properties rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Merlin
providers.description: Merlin is a global digital music licensing organization that represents independent music companies, providing them access to licensing deals, tools, and data insights. It operates a membership platform called Wizard, offers technology solutions, and publishes reports and industry insights to support its members in navigating the digital music ecosystem.

providers.name: Songlink / Odesli
providers.description: Get all the services on which a song is available

providers.name: SpotHopper
providers.description: SpotHopper is a Milwaukee, Wisconsin based restaurant marketing and web technology company, founded in 2015, selling an all-in-one, AI-assisted platform to independent restaurants and multi-location restaurant groups. The platform bundles restaurant website design and hosting (customer sites are served from the spotapps.co domain), SEO and Google Business Profile syncing, menu / specials / event publishing, automated social posting to Facebook and Instagram, email and SMS campaigns, review generation and reputation management, and link-outs to reservation and ordering partners such as OpenTable, Yelp and UberEats. The company markets itself as powering more than 20,000 restaurants. As of the 2026-08-29 enrichment probe SpotHopper publishes no developer portal, no API reference, and no machine-readable API contract on any host it controls.

providers.name: ASCAP
providers.description: The American Society of Composers, Authors and Publishers (ASCAP) is a not‑for‑profit performance‑rights organization representing over 1.1 million songwriters, composers and music publishers. It licenses public performances of music, collects royalties, and distributes them to creators. ASCAP also advocates for creators’ rights, offers educational resources, and provides tools such as a repertory search, licensing portals, and support services for members and music users.

providers.name: BandSaaS
providers.description: BandSaaS is an all‑in‑one artist platform that lets musicians license their music to AI companies on a per‑use basis, register tracks by ISRC, and maintain a provable audit trail of who accessed their work. It also provides direct‑to‑fan tools such as music sales, merch, ticketing, fan subscriptions, crowdfunding, and integrates with Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube, Instagram, TikTok, and SoundCloud. The platform charges a 1.5% fee and offers custom domain support with automatic SSL.

providers.name: PLOS
providers.description: These examples use the search API to search the PLOS corpus of scientific articles. These examples are not intended to be a full explanation on the use of Solr. A full Solr query language explanation can be found here and a tutorial here. The construction of PLOS search queries deviates from the standard Solr query URL by using search instead of select when making request to the end point. The primary endpoint is http://api.plos.org/search and supports parameters such as q, fl, wt, start, and rows for querying the PLOS Solr index.

providers.name: Lidarr
providers.description: Lidarr is an open-source music collection manager that automates the downloading, organization, and tagging of music files. It monitors your favorite artists and releases, integrates with download clients, and ensures metadata is correctly applied, providing a convenient way to keep your music library up to date.

providers.name: QQ Music
providers.description: QQ Music (QQ音乐) is a leading Chinese online music streaming service operated by Tencent. It offers a massive catalog of high‑quality, lossless tracks, personalized playlists, and social sharing features. Users can stream, download, and enjoy curated recommendations across web and mobile platforms, making it a central hub for music entertainment in China.

providers.name: Vivendi
providers.description: Vivendi is a Paris-based content, media and entertainment group (Vivendi SE) that holds a portfolio of listed and unlisted assets: Gameloft (wholly owned video-game publisher), V Collection (luxury media), and minority stakes in Universal Music Group, Banijay, Lagardère, MediaForEurope, Prisma Media and Prisa. Its website is a corporate, investor and press site; the group publishes no public API, SDK or developer program of its own.

providers.name: Audiomob
providers.description: Audiomob is an in-game and in-app audio advertising platform that lets mobile game and app publishers monetize their titles with non-interruptive, skippable and rewarded audio ads while advertisers reach engaged gaming audiences at scale. Publishers integrate through the Audiomob Unity plugin or native iOS and Android SDKs (plus a community React Native adapter), add their games to the Audiomob developer dashboard, and configure ad units, an Ad Availability API, and server-to-server webhooks for reward and event tracking. The platform is Open Measurement (IAB Tech Lab) compliant, supports consent management via OneTrust and Sourcepoint, exposes Impression Level Revenue Data (ILRD), and integrates with mediation partners such as AdMob and LevelPlay (MAX) and mobile measurement partners including Adjust, Singular and Tenjin. The current SDK line is SDK 10. Audiomob is backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners.

providers.name: Everyday Health
providers.description: Everyday Health is a consumer health media brand founded in 2002 and the flagship property of Everyday Health Group, a division of Ziff Davis (NASDAQ: ZD). The group operates a portfolio of consumer, pregnancy-and-parenting and healthcare-professional brands — Everyday Health, BabyCenter, What to Expect, MedPage Today, Castle Connolly, Diabetes Daily, DailyOM, Lose It!, Migraine Again, theSkimm, HealthCentral and Emma's Diary — and sells pharma commercialization, digital health and wellness, and provider solutions to life sciences companies, hospitals, health systems and clinicians. It is a publisher and advertising business, not an API platform: there is no developer portal, no public API documentation, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, no SDKs and no hosted MCP or agent surface on any Everyday Health host. This API Evangelist profile captures what the company does publish programmatically — a sitemap index, one public RSS/Media RSS content feed, an auth-gated AWS API Gateway host at api.everydayhealth.com, and an unusually explicit robots.txt that blocks 107 named AI and agent crawlers site-wide while carving out two commercial product-review URLs.

providers.name: MyARC Fitness
providers.description: MyARC (operated by Vert Analytics Limited) is an all-in-one platform that lets fitness creators and coaches scale their business without writing code. Coaches use MyARC to launch a branded mobile app, automate AI-personalized workout and meal plans for thousands of members at once, run challenges and 1-on-1 coaching, build community, and earn recurring subscription revenue. The consumer-facing MyARC Fitness app ships on iOS and Android with progress tracking and accountability features. As of this profile MyARC exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface — it is a creator-facing SaaS and mobile product, not an API provider. Offices in London, New York, Melbourne, and India.

providers.name: favorited
providers.description: Favorited is a mobile-first live streaming platform that helps content creators run interactive, real-time shows with their audiences. The app centers on participatory formats — games, giveaways, and community interactions — so that viewers feel like they are playing together with a creator rather than passively watching a broadcast, alongside monetization tools for creators.
