Favorited ships as consumer iOS and Android apps and, as of this profile, publishes no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment and monitoring.

providers.name: Mixhalo
providers.description: Mixhalo is an AI-enabled digital audio platform for live events that streams broadcast-quality speaker audio, real-time language interpretation, transcription, and summaries directly to attendees' smartphones, eliminating the need for silent-session headsets or dedicated receiver hardware. Its flagship product, Mixhalo Live, delivers low-latency multilingual audio into event apps, and it has partnered with Eventbase to offer an SDK for embedding the experience in client event applications. Mixhalo is now part of DeepL, extending DeepL's multilingual communication capabilities to in-person events. The company is backed by Cowboy Ventures. This profile currently exposes no public developer portal or API surface.

providers.name: Royal
providers.description: Royal is a music-and-crypto company backed by a16z and Paradigm that originally let fans buy tokenized shares of songs (Limited Digital Assets, or LDAs) so they could earn streaming royalties alongside the artists they support. As of mid-2026 the public site at royal.io states the company is "reinventing itself" and is between products, keeping only its legal pages and LDA support live; it publishes no developer portal, documentation, OpenAPI, SDKs, or public API surface at this time. This profile tracks Royal as an API Evangelist network company and will be enriched further if and when a public API or developer program appears.

providers.name: Sound.xyz
providers.description: Sound.xyz was a web3 music platform and suite of on-chain tools that let artists release music as digital collectibles and host listening parties for new releases, building direct economic relationships with their communities. The consumer platform went offline on 2026-01-16 (with a successor project, Vault.fm), but Sound.xyz's first-party developer surface remains publicly published: the open-source Sound protocol (a permissionless Solidity smart-contract framework for music collectibles) and the official @soundxyz npm SDK ecosystem (@soundxyz/sdk, sdk-viem, legacy-sdk) for on-chain development, alongside GraphQL and caching infrastructure libraries. Added to the API Evangelist network as an a16z portfolio company; this profile now reflects the enrichment pipeline's findings.

providers.name: SoundExchange
providers.description: SoundExchange is a non‑profit collective rights organization that collects and distributes digital performance royalties on behalf of sound recording owners and performers. It ensures that artists, record labels, and rights holders receive fair compensation when their music is streamed, broadcast, or otherwise publicly performed across digital platforms. By operating a transparent and efficient royalty distribution system, SoundExchange supports the sustainability of the music ecosystem and promotes the value of creative works in the modern digital landscape.

providers.name: Vioo
providers.description: Vioo is a Mexican professional visual-content platform that connects businesses with a national network of 1,500+ certified photographers and creators across Mexico, delivering photography, videography, drone footage, 3D renders, and Matterport virtual tours. It serves real estate, gastronomy, e-commerce, hospitality, events, and portrait use cases with AI-assisted editing and 48-hour delivery, and offers scheduling either through a personalized form or automatically via an integration API. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and added to the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Kardome Technology
providers.description: Kardome develops Voice AI technology that lets voice-integrated products hear and understand speech with human-level accuracy in complex, real-world acoustic environments. Its two core technologies are Spatial Hearing AI, which understands the acoustic scene to localize sound sources and attribute speech to the correct speaker, and Cognition AI, which adds contextual awareness so devices understand what people mean in the moment. Kardome targets automotive in-car voice UI and smart-home voice interaction in noisy environments. The company is a Techstars portfolio company, tracked in the API Evangelist network; it licenses embedded voice technology to device makers rather than publishing a public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface at this time.

providers.name: Panoramax
providers.description: Panoramax is a French open‑source initiative that federates local authorities, OpenStreetMap contributors, and the French National Geographic Institute (IGN) to create immersive, geocommunicated base views of territories. It provides tools and APIs for photo‑mapping, enabling communities to capture, share, and integrate high‑resolution panoramic imagery into geographic information systems, supporting open data and collaborative mapping projects.

providers.name: Splash
providers.description: Splash is an AI music-creation platform building games and tools for a new generation of creators. Developed by the team formerly known as Popgun AI, it has built proprietary generative-audio technology and high-quality music datasets since 2017, powering features such as Text-to-Singing, Text-to-Rap, and Generative Text-to-Music. Splash's consumer products include the Splash beat-maker app for iOS and Android, SPLASH on Roblox, the WeMix collaborative music experience, and KAIMIX. The company is backed by Khosla Ventures, Techstars, the Alexa Fund, Bitkraft, King River Capital, and Mawson. Splash publishes no public developer API or documentation surface at this time; this profile captures its public web identity in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Lanch
providers.description: LANCH GmbH is a Berlin-based food-tech startup that builds creator-led virtual restaurant brands for the delivery market. Founded by Nono Konopka and Jonas Meynert and headquartered at Schoenhauser Allee 180 in Berlin, LANCH develops food brands together with German influencers, musicians and athletes, then scales them through franchise partners and ghost-kitchen partners operating out of existing restaurant kitchens. Its two flagship brands are Loco Chicken (halal-certified wings, filets, burgers and chicken-and-waffle creations) and Happy Slice (hand-pulled pinsa-dough pizza, dips and cookies), both distributed through delivery marketplaces including Wolt, Lieferando and Uber Eats. The company is backed by HV Capital and Felix Capital alongside founders of FlixBus, Gorillas, Flaschenpost, Glovo, Foodspring, Foodora, Honest Food and Finleap. LANCH publishes a marketing and partner-recruitment website only; as of this enrichment pass it exposes no public developer portal, API documentation, machine-readable API specification or SDK surface.

providers.name: Podchaser
providers.description: Podchaser provides one of the most comprehensive podcast databases, exposed through a GraphQL API designed to drive podcast discovery for listeners, podcasters, brands, and platform partners. The API surface is GraphQL-only and is therefore not represented as an OpenAPI specification in this index.

providers.name: Ad Radar
providers.description: Ad Radar provides a tool to discover winning Facebook ads quickly. It tracks Meta ads for hundreds of brands, estimates spend, flags scaling ads, and breaks down creative hooks. Users can explore ad performance, filter by niche, and integrate with Claude via an MCP server for AI‑assisted research.

providers.name: Artifact
providers.description: Artifact is a consumer service that captures and preserves family stories through professional, guided interviews. The company conducts remote 30-minute interviews with a family member and edits each one into a studio-quality ~20-minute audio episode, hosted on a private webpage where relatives can add photos and share the recording. Episodes are priced per interview, positioning the product as a way to record a loved one's life story and memories. Backed by GV (Google Ventures) in the consumer sector. As of 2026 the company announced it is winding down: new Artifacts are no longer sold, and previously purchased interviews may be scheduled through October 31. The service exposes no public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface.

providers.name: Likeable Local
providers.description: Likeable Local is a social media marketing company that now operates publicly as Storytellit — likeablelocal.com and www.likeablelocal.com both redirect to storytellit.com, while the product application at app.likeablelocal.com and app.storytellit.com still identifies itself as "Likeable Local" in its web app manifest. Storytellit sells social media management as a white-label service to digital agencies — strategy, custom content creation and publishing, paid social advertising, lead capture, and monthly performance reporting for the agency's clients, across verticals including dental, medical, legal, real estate, insurance, finance, eCommerce, and local business. The company is based in Portland, Maine, and was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio company. As of this enrichment pass Likeable Local / Storytellit publishes no public API, no developer portal, no API documentation, and no machine-readable specification; the public web surface is a four-page marketing site plus a private, login-gated React application. A production API does exist but is an internal application backend rather than a developer product — api.storytellit.com and api.likeablelocal.com both resolve to the same Amazon load balancer and run Express over FeathersJS, and every service path, including a GraphQL endpoint, rejects anonymous callers with HTTP 401 while serving no specification and no documentation of any kind.

providers.name: PRS for Music
providers.description: PRS for Music is the UK’s leading performing rights organisation representing songwriters, composers and music publishers. It collects royalties on behalf of its members when music is used across broadcast, streaming, live performance and public venues, ensuring creators are fairly compensated. The organisation also provides licensing solutions for businesses and supports a wide range of music-related services and initiatives.

providers.name: Verso Corporation
providers.description: Verso Corporation (NYSE: VRS) was a North American producer of coated papers including coated groundwood, coated freesheet, and specialty products used in magazines, catalogs, commercial print, books, and packaging. Headquartered in Miamisburg, Ohio, Verso operated mills in Wisconsin Rapids (Wisconsin), Escanaba (Michigan), Duluth (Minnesota), and historically Luke (Maryland). In March 2022, Swedish pulp and paper group BillerudKorsnäs (now Billerud) completed its acquisition of Verso for $825 million in cash, taking the company private and rebranding it as Billerud Americas Corporation. The Verso standalone brand, ticker, and corporate web presence have been retired; ongoing North American operations, paper grades, and customer relationships now sit inside Billerud's global business.

providers.name: Beatport
providers.description: Beatport is the leading online music store and streaming platform for electronic dance music DJs and producers, founded in 2004 and headquartered in Denver, Colorado. Beatport sells high-quality downloads (lossless WAV, AIFF, and FLAC, plus AAC) of tracks, releases, and DJ tools across more than 150 electronic genres, and operates a subscription streaming tier — Beatport Streaming — that delivers catalog tracks directly into supported DJ applications and hardware including Pioneer DJ rekordbox, Serato DJ Pro, Denon DJ Engine DJ, Algoriddim djay, Virtual DJ, Traktor, and others through integration partners. The Beatport Group also operates Beatsource (open- format DJ streaming and download store), DJCity (open-format record pool), Beatport LINK and Beatsource LINK (in-app streaming for DJ software), BeatportAmp (distribution and rights management for labels, formerly Ampsuite), Plugin Boutique (audio software and plugin marketplace), Loopcloud (sample subscription for producers), Label Radar (demo submission), Beatport Live (live events and streaming), Beatportal (editorial and media), and the International Music Summit (IMS) industry conference. The company reports ten million registered users, eighty thousand labels, four hundred thousand artists, and four hundred million USD paid out to rights holders since launch. Beatport operates a v4 REST API at api.beatport.com governed by OAuth 2.0 (authorization-code grant) with an interactive Swagger-UI developer portal at /v4/docs/; access is gated to approved partners through the Beatport Partner Portal, and there is no public client-credentials tier for general developers. The API exposes the Beatport catalog (tracks, releases, artists, labels, genres, sub-genres, charts, playlists, my-beatport collections, holds, and DJ-oriented search filters such as BPM, key, and released-date) and is the same surface that powers the public beatport.com applications and third-party DJ-software integrations. Beatport does not publish a downloadable OpenAPI document, an official SDK, or a CLI; partner integration is brokered case-by-case through the Partner Portal and the business-development team.

providers.name: Flick
providers.description: Flick is an AI filmmaking studio that lets creators direct short films with AI on an infinite, node-based canvas. Rather than a linear prompt-to-clip generator, Flick gives directors a nonlinear workspace to plan, iterate and assemble complete narratives of any length — generating scenes, keeping character faces and styles consistent across shots, controlling shot composition, and editing images by reference. The product is a web app with a free tier (300 credits) and paid plans from $5/month, plus a Creative Partner Program and a Filmmaker Residency for AI filmmakers. Flick was founded by Ray Wang (previously a founding engineer on the Instagram AI team) and award-winning filmmaker Zoey Zhang, and is Y Combinator- and GV-backed. Flick publishes product documentation, a blog and a verbatim llms.txt, but does not currently expose a public developer API, SDKs, webhooks or an MCP server — the /api/ surface is an internal application API that robots.txt explicitly disallows.

providers.name: Splice
providers.description: Splice is a New York-based music creation platform serving producers, songwriters, and audio creators. Its core offerings are Splice Sounds, a catalog of millions of 100% royalty-free samples, one-shots, loops, MIDI patterns, and presets sold through a credit-based subscription; Splice INSTRUMENT, a creator-first virtual instrument with monthly free drops and unlimited premium presets via subscription; and a Rent-to-Own Plugins marketplace offering pay-as-you-go full-license access to 130+ professional VST/AU/AAX plugins from third-party vendors such as Xfer (Serum 2), Arturia (V Collection 11 Pro), Spitfire Audio (Abbey Road Two), and XLN Audio (RC-20). Splice ships a desktop app, a mobile app, the Splice Sounds Plugin (beta) for in-DAW browsing, and native integrations for Ableton Live 12.3+, Studio One Pro 7, Studio Pro 8+, and Pro Tools 2025.6+. The revenue model is consumer subscriptions (Sounds+ $12.99/mo, Creator $19.99/mo with 200 credits, Creator+ $39.99/mo with 500 credits, INSTRUMENT $12.99/mo) plus rent-to-own plugin payments. Splice does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or partner program; its GitHub organization at github.com/splice contains internal tooling, GitHub Actions, audio engineering exercises, and forks rather than externally consumable APIs.

providers.name: 88rising
providers.description: 88rising (stylized 88 with a rising arrow) is an American mass media company and record label founded in 2015 by Sean Miyashiro, headquartered in Los Angeles and New York with a division in Shanghai. It describes itself as a hybrid management, record label, video production and marketing company, and is known for building a global platform for Asian and Asian American artists including Rich Brian, NIKI, Joji and Keith Ape. Beyond recorded music it operates the Head in the Clouds festival franchise and the 88 Night Market live and commerce brand. It is a media and entertainment company rather than a software company: it publishes no developer program, no public API documentation and no machine-readable specifications.

providers.name: Business Insider
providers.description: Business Insider is a global business and financial news media company founded in 2007 and headquartered in New York City, operating as part of Axel Springer. It publishes fast-paced coverage of markets, technology, finance, the economy, retail, media, and careers across its flagship Business Insider brand and verticals such as Markets Insider. The organization was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of the venture firm IVP. It operates consumer news properties and content syndication feeds rather than a public developer API program, so this profile tracks its public web presence and domain security posture rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Mad Realities
providers.description: Mad Realities is a creator-powered entertainment network that produces original episodic shows for internet-native audiences, bridging the gap between culture born online and television-level production by partnering with creators. Its Mad Labs arm is an R&D effort leveraging AI and technology to superpower creatives. Backed by Paradigm, the company operates as a consumer media brand and publishes no public API, SDK, or developer platform at this time.

providers.name: Rexby
providers.description: Rexby is a consumer travel discovery and trip-planning platform where local creators publish interactive travel guides and maps of curated "spots," and travelers browse those guides, build personal itineraries, and follow creator recommendations. The product is delivered as iOS and Android mobile apps plus the rexby.com web experience, with a creator program that lets travel enthusiasts monetize their guides. Backed by Techstars. As of this profile Rexby publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation; this apis.yml captures its identity and a domain-security probe for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Sharechat
providers.description: ShareChat (Mohalla Tech Pvt. Ltd.) is an Indian social media company that operates the regional-language social network ShareChat and the short-video entertainment app Moj. The platform lets users across 15+ Indian languages share posts, images, videos, shayari, quotes, and trending content through personalized feeds. ShareChat monetizes through a self-serve advertising platform (ShareChat Ads) offering campaign management, audience targeting, and brand partnerships across its social and short-video surfaces. Backed by Lightspeed Venture Partners and other investors, the company is one of the largest homegrown social platforms in India. As of this profile, ShareChat exposes consumer apps and a self-serve ad manager but publishes no public developer program, API documentation, or programmatic API surface.

providers.name: Shibuya
providers.description: Shibuya is a platform for curated short films and the independent creators behind them, describing itself as a home where fans help greenlight the future of film and audiences discover original storytelling. Operated by NotShibuya, Inc. and backed by a16z, Shibuya began as a web3 storytelling experiment and has grown into a community-driven curation platform for short-form film, winning a 2025 Primetime Emmy for Outstanding Innovation in Emerging Media Programming. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this enrichment pass Shibuya publishes no public developer program, API, SDK, or documentation surface; this profile captures its real public web properties.

providers.name: Shoobs
providers.description: Shoobs is a UK-based online events discovery and ticketing platform focused on urban culture — Afrobeats, R&B, hip-hop, dancehall, comedy, theatre, festivals, brunches and club nights across London and other British cities. Founded as a Y Combinator-backed startup, Shoobs helps fans find and book tickets to events that match their taste, and lets promoters list and sell tickets for urban and Black-British cultural events. The platform pairs an events listing and discovery site with an integrated editorial blog covering artists, concerts and nightlife. Shoobs is a consumer web product; it does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: NetEase Cloud Music
providers.description: NetEase Cloud Music (网易云音乐) is a leading Chinese music streaming service offering a vast library of songs, playlists, podcasts, and user‑generated content. Users can discover music, create personal playlists, follow artists, and access high‑quality audio via web and mobile apps. The platform provides APIs for searching tracks, retrieving album details, managing user libraries, and streaming content, serving both consumer and developer ecosystems.

providers.name: Calaxy
providers.description: Calaxy is a decentralized social platform that empowers creators, communities, and brands to build and own their own Worlds—standalone social apps. Launched in 2025, it offers tools for audience engagement, content monetization, and cross‑network interoperability, aiming to free the internet one World at a time.

providers.name: DAZN
providers.description: DAZN is a global over-the-top live sports streaming service headquartered in London and owned by Access Industries. Launched in 2015 out of the former Perform Group, it streams boxing, football, MotoGP, UFC and other rights to subscribers across more than 200 countries and territories, and has expanded through the acquisitions of Eleven Group, Foxtel/Kayo Sports and ViewLift, alongside the DAZN Bet and DAZN Media brands. DAZN operates a large Node.js microservice estate on AWS and publishes open source engineering tooling (the Kopytko Roku ecosystem, dazn-lambda-powertools) from its GitHub organization, but it runs no public developer program: there is no developer portal, no API reference, and no machine-readable specification for the consumer platform APIs that power its apps.

providers.name: News Corp
providers.description: News Corp (Nasdaq: NWS, NWSA) is a global, diversified media and information services company focused on creating and distributing authoritative and engaging content across publishing, news media, digital real estate services, and book publishing. Its businesses and brands include Dow Jones (The Wall Street Journal, Barron's, MarketWatch, Investor's Business Daily), the New York Post, News UK (The Times, The Sun), News Corp Australia, HarperCollins, Storyful, REA Group and Realtor.com. No public developer program or API documentation is published on newscorp.com.

providers.name: Dipsea
providers.description: Dipsea is a San Francisco‑based media production company that offers a subscription‑based app delivering audio erotica and immersive storytelling from a female‑gaze perspective. The platform features a library of over 1,000 erotic audio stories across diverse tropes, created by professional writers and narrators, aiming to provide a safe, uncensored space for sexual wellness exploration.

providers.name: Essence Ventures
providers.description: Essence Ventures is an independent, African American-owned media, technology, and commerce company focused on content, community, and commerce for Black women and their communities. Founded by Richelieu Dennis, it acquired Essence Communications (Essence magazine and the Essence Festival of Culture) in 2018, and its portfolio of lifestyle brands has included Afropunk, BeautyCon, and Essence Studios, reaching audiences across print, digital, video, social, and live events. Essence Ventures does not operate a public developer program or API; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a company/portfolio lead awaiting further enrichment.

providers.name: Baller League
providers.description: Baller League is a small-sided (six-a-side) football entertainment league and media format founded in Germany that bills itself as "a new era of football, created for the streets by the streets." Teams are captained by professional footballers, influencers, and streamers, with matches played under a fast-paced ruleset and distributed primarily through live streaming and social video (Twitch, YouTube, TikTok, Instagram) rather than traditional broadcast. The organization has expanded from Germany into the United Kingdom and United States and is running its fourth season. It is a consumer sports-media and entertainment brand; as of this profile it publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer program. Backed by EQT Ventures and tracked in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company.

providers.name: Beaubble
providers.description: Beaubble is a community-driven beauty commerce platform that lets creators launch their own customized, premium beauty brands and products by engaging their audiences. The company runs a direct-to-consumer storefront at beaubble.com featuring creator-led lines from talent such as Teni Panosian, Elsa Hosk, Shanina Shaik, Abbie Herbert, Rudi Berry, and Avrey Ovard, selling items like lip stains, freckle pens, and curated bundles. Backed by 500 Global, Beaubble is a consumer e-commerce brand with no public developer API surface; this profile was created by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline and captures the company's public web presence and domain-security posture.

providers.name: FreshPlanet
providers.description: FreshPlanet Inc. is a New York City based mobile game developer, headquartered at 200 Hudson St, New York, NY 10013, best known for the music trivia franchise SongPop. The studio builds free-to-play mobile entertainment titles for iOS and Android, combining licensed music catalogs, social multiplayer play, and live events. FreshPlanet is a portfolio company of Uncork Capital. As a consumer game studio it does not operate a public developer program or API: it exposes only a marketing site, player support via a Zendesk help center, and standard legal surfaces (Terms of Use and Privacy Policy). This profile captures the studio's real public web and legal footprint for the API Evangelist network; there is no OpenAPI, SDK, or agent surface to enrich because the company publishes none.

providers.name: publifye-com
providers.description: Publifye AS is a Norwegian Bible publishing company based in Oslo, offering over 4,200 Bible editions and a suite of AI‑enhanced tools for Scripture study, publishing, document management, and Norwegian data integration. Their platform provides APIs that enable developers to access biblical texts, leverage AI for content generation, and integrate publishing workflows into applications. Publifye focuses on combining traditional publishing expertise with modern AI capabilities to serve churches, scholars, and developers worldwide.

providers.name: Syncbak
providers.description: Syncbak is a Marion, Iowa media-technology company founded in 2009 by Jack Perry that built the streaming infrastructure local U.S. television broadcasters use to put their over-the-air signals online. Its SimpleSync / MediaMogul platform handles live-stream transcoding, cloud-based rights resolution and geo-location authentication, cloud DVR, device filtering, content management, stream monitoring, clipping, and dynamic ad insertion through its AdSync product, delivering station feeds to OTT destinations including Paramount+, Hulu, fuboTV, Amazon, Roku, Apple TV and the NFL across 200+ U.S. markets. The company rebranded to Zeam Media in May 2024 to match its Zeam consumer hyperlocal streaming app, and syncbak.com now redirects to zeammedia.com. Syncbak publishes no public developer program, API reference, or machine-readable contract; its platform is delivered to broadcasters and station groups under commercial agreement.

providers.name: 이지에이전시
providers.description: 이지에이전시는 홈페이지·시스템 구축부터 브랜딩·마케팅, 운영까지 비즈니스에 필요한 모든 것을 제공하는 종합 솔루션 기업입니다. 고객의 디지털 전환을 지원하며 다양한 웹·앱 개발, 콘텐츠 제작, 마케팅, 브랜딩 서비스를 제공하고 있습니다. 또한 기업 맞춤형 프로젝트 관리와 컨설팅을 통해 효율적인 비즈니스 프로세스를 구현하고, 최신 트렌드와 기술을 활용한 혁신적인 디지털 경험을 제공합니다.

providers.name: CatchaSet
providers.description: CatchaSet is a live‑music discovery platform focused on Austin, helping users find concerts that match their musical tastes. The service aggregates event data, provides personalized recommendations, and offers tools for browsing venues, artists, and upcoming shows. It aims to connect music fans with live experiences through an intuitive web interface and curated listings.

providers.name: ListenBrainz
providers.description: ListenBrainz is an open music listening tracking platform that lets users record, explore, visualise and share the music they listen to. It provides a public API for accessing listening data, user profiles, and music metadata, enabling developers to build applications and services around music listening habits.

providers.name: PearPop
providers.description: Pearpop, Inc. is a Los Angeles-based creator marketing company founded in October 2020 by Cole Mason and Guy Oseary. It began as a two-sided social collaboration marketplace where brands could book social-media creators on demand under a performance-based, pay-per-placement model, and has since grown into a full-service creator marketing partner running campaigns for brands including Netflix, Microsoft, Chipotle, Klarna and Activision. Its current product line is marketed at pearpop.com (brand campaigns, creator representation and events) plus Pearpop.AI at pearpop.ai — described in Pearpop's own terms of service as an AI-powered email platform for content creators and influencers that handles brand-deal inboxes, contract review, rate recommendations and payments. Pearpop publishes no public developer program, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API specification; the only live API namespace, pearpop.ai/api/*, redirects unauthenticated callers to the application sign-in page.

providers.name: Believe
providers.description: Believe is a global artist development company that provides recording, publishing, and distribution services. It works with independent artists, songwriters, record labels, and music publishers to develop careers, protect rights, and collect royalties worldwide. The company operates in more than 50 countries and supports its partners with technology, expertise, and operational support.

providers.name: Dare Drop
providers.description: Dare Drop is a gaming influencer marketing platform that connects game publishers and brands with content creators across Twitch, YouTube, and TikTok. The platform runs reward-driven "Dares" — challenges that incentivize streamers and creators to produce longer, more engaging content around a title, while automating creator targeting, campaign management, and reporting. Dare Drop offers influencer campaigns, ongoing influencer programs, and organic outreach, and has facilitated over 18,000 publisher Dares and distributed more than 30,000 rewards to creator communities. Its customers include game studios and publishers such as EA, Respawn, Raw Fury, Tencent, Obsidian, and Gearbox. Surfaced as an a16z portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network; no public developer API surface has been found to date.

providers.name: Mindset
providers.description: Mindset is a mobile self-care and wellness application by DIVE Studios that pairs audio content from celebrity artists and musicians with expert-led mental health resources. Features include Celebrity Mindsets audio collections, a five-minute Daily Check-In routine, Daily Reflections community sharing, licensed-professional advice, and daily quotes, delivered on iOS and Android with a 50,000+ member Discord community. Mindset operates a private, login-gated mobile backend at api.getmindset.com behind Google OAuth; no public developer API, documentation, SDKs, or well-known discovery surface is published.

providers.name: Supponor
providers.description: Supponor is a virtual advertising technology company for live sports broadcasting, now part of TGI Sport. Its software digitally replaces and inserts in-venue brand placements with real-time overlays, letting broadcasters serve region-targeted advertising across multiple feeds, languages, surfaces, and camera angles. Core products include AIR, an AI-driven virtual advertising platform for live broadcast; HUB, a pre-event suite for fixtures, inventory, playlists, creative and approvals; and Data Room, a post-event analytics platform for reporting, video storage, and performance metrics. Supponor works across any sport and surface with remotely deployable, all-weather technology, and is used by organizations including FC Bayern, the NHL, The FA, Serie A, and La Liga. Added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of Northzone; it publishes a corporate and careers web presence but no public developer API surface.

providers.name: Audacy
providers.description: Audacy, Inc. is a U.S. multi-platform audio and entertainment company that operates the country's second-largest radio group alongside the Audacy streaming app, a major podcast network, and the Amperwave audio ad-tech and distribution platform. Formerly known as Entercom (rebranded to Audacy on March 30, 2021), the company filed prepackaged Chapter 11 bankruptcy on January 7, 2024 and emerged on September 30, 2024 as a privately held company after equitizing approximately $1.6 billion of funded debt and reducing total debt from roughly $1.9 billion to $350 million. The current portfolio spans ~230 radio brands across 47 markets, 200+ million monthly listeners, ~2 billion annual podcast downloads, and the Cadence13, Pineapple Street Studios, Podcorn, and BetMGM Network (formerly BetQL) audio brands. There is no public developer API, no published OpenAPI, and no GitHub organization with public repositories; integration is brokered through ad sales, programmatic marketplaces, and the Amperwave platform.

providers.name: Grade
providers.description: Grade is the API for performance-based payroll, letting companies pay workers, creators, contractors, and AI agents based on results rather than hours worked. Companies push performance signals into Grade via webhooks or direct API calls (task completed, milestone hit, content published, views tracked, invoice processed), and Grade runs them against configurable payout rules — flat fees, tiered commissions, threshold bonuses, or blended structures — handling the math, de-duplication, and approval workflows automatically. Grade tracks every post across platforms, approves and distributes bulk payouts in one click, and handles compliance end to end: KYC verification, tax-form collection, DAC7 reporting, worker classification, and merchant-of-record services. Payouts reach 190+ countries via local bank transfers, PayPal, Wise, Payoneer, Revolut, Airtm, and USDT, with no separate creator account required. Grade (YC W26) is based in San Francisco and has paid out $10M+ to date.

providers.name: Pump.fun
providers.description: Pump.fun is a Solana-based memecoin launchpad and livestreaming platform that lets anyone deploy a token with a bonding-curve market in seconds; tokens that reach a target market cap graduate to PumpSwap, the project's own AMM. The project does not publish a formally documented public REST API - the canonical integration surface is the on-chain Solana programs for token creation, bonding-curve trades, and PumpSwap liquidity, plus the open-source pump-fun-sdk client. Most "Pump.fun APIs" used in the wider ecosystem are third-party indexers (Bitquery, Helius, Jupiter, Tatum) wrapping that on-chain activity.

providers.name: Blavity
providers.description: Blavity Inc. is a Black-owned digital media and technology company founded in 2014 by Morgan DeBaun, operating a portfolio of premium content brands and events for Black millennials and Gen Z around culture, technology, travel, and lifestyle. Its properties include Blavity.com (news and culture), AfroTech (the largest Black tech conference and media brand), Travel Noire (travel), Shadow and Act (film and entertainment), and 21Ninety (women's lifestyle). Blavity Inc. monetizes through advertising, branded content, events, and its Blavity Media Group agency. It is a privately held company backed by investors including 500 Global and GV, and does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, or machine-readable API specifications. This profile tracks Blavity as a company in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Palmstreet
providers.description: Palmstreet is a live shopping marketplace where sellers host interactive live-stream sales and buyers browse more than a million listings across rare plants, handmade goods, vintage items, jewelry, crystals, coins, fashion, beauty, aquatics, reptiles, and designer toys. The platform pairs real-time video commerce with a traditional marketplace, free seller onboarding, and Seller Hub inventory tooling. Backed by Craft Ventures, Palmstreet operates as a consumer mobile app (iOS/Android) and web storefront. No public developer API, documentation portal, or partner API surface is published as of this enrichment pass; this profile captures the company identity and public web properties only.

providers.name: HAAWK
providers.description: HAAWK is a Los Angeles-based music rights management and monetization company that administers digital rights across YouTube, Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok for record labels, music publishers, and independent artists. Its products include HAAWK (full-service YouTube Content ID and Meta Rights Manager administration), Identifyy (self-service UGC rights management for independent creators), Keyframe Audio (a micro sync-licensing catalog of 50,000+ production music tracks), and Diistro (digital music distribution to Apple Music, Spotify, YouTube Music, and TikTok). HAAWK has administered 100B+ video views and manages 1.1M+ music copyrights for 2,000+ rights holders. Backed by 500 Global. No public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Humeo
providers.description: Humeo, INC. is a San Francisco-based applied AI research lab focused on creative intelligence, blending design, social science, and frontier AI research. Its products include VideoClaw, a desktop creative production agent that transforms existing media and automates media creation, and Studio, a web application for producing high-impact short-form video content. Humeo's research spans creative attunement, taste modeling, universal media transformation, world models of attention, and creative efficiency. The company is backed by 500 Global. As of this profile Humeo publishes no public API, developer portal, or documentation; VideoClaw is in private alpha with access granted by request.

providers.name: KK直播 (KK Live)
providers.description: KK直播 (KK Live) is a Chinese mobile-first video livestreaming and social entertainment platform operated by 杭州米络文化传播有限公司 (Hangzhou Melot Culture Communication Co., Ltd.), part of 米络星集团 (Melot Group), headquartered in Hangzhou with offices in Beijing, Changsha, Xi'an, Shenyang, Los Angeles and Mumbai. Founded in 2012 to fill the gap in mobile livestreaming variety shows, the platform pairs talent and performance streaming with interactive social features — virtual gifting, bullet comments (弹幕), multi-person live connections, PK mini-games, karaoke rooms, outdoor streaming and paid companionship. The company reports more than 100,000 independent streamers, over 600 partner talent agencies and 150 million registered users. Melot Group runs three business lines — entertainment livestreaming, online education and video service solutions — under the KK, 棒直播 and 米乐 brands. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners (启明创投), Sequoia China (红杉资本), CMC Capital (华人文化基金) and Shanda Capital (盛大资本). KK Live is a business-to-consumer product: as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API specifications.

providers.name: LyricFind
providers.description: LyricFind provides licensed lyrics and music‑related data services to businesses worldwide. Through its robust API platform, developers can integrate lyric search, display, translation, and licensing capabilities into applications across industries such as streaming, automotive, health & fitness, and retail. The company offers comprehensive data licensing, compliance tools, and analytics to ensure lawful use of copyrighted lyrics, supporting partners from major record labels to independent artists.

providers.name: Glimmer (formerly Storyhunter)
providers.description: Glimmer, formerly known as Storyhunter, is an all-in-one creator management platform and global marketplace connecting brands and media companies with a vetted network of 50,000+ freelance content creators, video producers, and journalists across 170+ countries. Founded in 2012 by Jaron Gilinsky in Brooklyn, New York, and rebranded from Storyhunter to Glimmer in November 2023, the platform organizes creator teams, messaging, project management, online contracts, and global payments in one central dashboard, and offers Glimmer Select as a full-service managed production studio. Clients have included CNN, The New York Times, National Geographic, MSNBC, and Starbucks. The company was backed in part by 500 Global and is surfaced here as an API Evangelist network company profile; it does not publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Yousician
providers.description: Yousician is a fun, interactive music learning platform that helps users of all ages learn guitar, piano, ukulele, bass, and singing through a gamified experience with thousands of popular songs, personalized lessons, real-time feedback, and progress tracking, making music education engaging and accessible.

providers.name: bith.tv
providers.description: Bith.ai (bith.tv) is an all-in-one, AI-powered video editing and content creation platform for creators, letting users record, edit, resize, caption, and publish short-form video reformatted for the major social platforms from a single browser-based dashboard. Founded in 2019 and headquartered in Amman, Jordan, the company is backed by 500 Global, BeyondCapital, Propeller, and Oasis500. Bith does not currently expose a public developer API, SDKs, or documentation surface; this profile was added to the API Evangelist network as a 500 Global portfolio lead and enriched with what the company publicly publishes (website, marketing tool pages, pricing, sign-up, and probed domain security posture).

providers.name: برندوان
providers.description: برندوان یک شرکت مشاوره‌ای در زمینه برندینگ، تولید محتوا و تحول دیجیتال است که از سال ۱۳۹۶ فعالیت می‌کند. این شرکت به کسب‌وکارها کمک می‌کند تا هویت برند خود را بسازند، محتوای دقیق تولید کنند و برای تحول دیجیتال آماده شوند.

providers.name: saifs-ai
providers.description: Saifs AI provides a suite of professional AI tools for content creation, enabling users to generate videos, images, text, and audio effortlessly. The platform offers AI video generation, text-to-video, AI sound effect generation, and image-to-video capabilities, targeting creators, marketers, and businesses seeking automated multimedia production.

providers.name: The MLC
providers.description: The Mechanical Licensing Collective (MLC) is a U.S. statutory organization that administers mechanical licensing and royalty distribution for music creators. It provides a centralized database of musical works, facilitates licensing for digital music services, and ensures creators receive proper compensation. The MLC offers APIs and data services to support industry participants in accessing catalog information, licensing data, and royalty reports.

providers.name: Yandex Music
providers.description: Yandex Music is a Russian online music streaming service offering a vast catalog of songs, albums, playlists, and podcasts. Users can listen to music on-demand, create personal playlists, and discover new content through personalized recommendations. The platform provides both free ad‑supported and subscription‑based tiers, supporting multiple devices including web, mobile apps, and smart speakers. Yandex Music integrates with Yandex’s broader ecosystem, offering seamless access via Yandex ID and supporting social sharing features.

providers.name: Hudl
providers.description: Hudl is a Lincoln, Nebraska sports performance and analytics technology company founded in 2007. The company started as a video sharing and review platform for high school, college, and professional teams and has grown into a global provider of video capture hardware, performance analysis software, and sports data services. Hudl operates across basketball, baseball, football, ice hockey, rugby, soccer, softball, and volleyball, serving customers from youth clubs through professional leagues. The company's product portfolio spans the core Hudl video platform, Hudl Focus AI-powered capture cameras (Indoor, Outdoor, Flex, Point), Hudl Replay and Hudl Studio for live and tactical analysis, Hudl IQ for American football analytics, Volleymetrics, the Hudl TV livestreaming product, and Hudl Tickets digital ticketing. Through acquisitions Hudl has consolidated several leading performance analysis and football data brands under its umbrella, including Sportscode (performance analysis software), Wyscout (the largest soccer video and stats database), Statsbomb (advanced football analytics), Instat (video and scouting), WIMU and Titan (athlete tracking and wearables), and Signal and ADI. Hudl exposes commercial developer surfaces primarily through Hudl Wyscout (Wyscout Data API, documented as OpenAPI 3.0 at apidocs.wyscout.com, with Database, Stats, Events, and Physical Data packs) and Hudl Statsbomb (the Statsbomb Aggregated API for player-match, player-season, team-match, and team-season data, accessed via the Data Hub, plus the Raw X&Y Tracking Data API and a Wyscout/Statsbomb ID Mapping API). Core Hudl video and Hudl Focus do not publish a public developer API; B2B integrations are sales-mediated. Hudl maintains a public GitHub organization (github.com/hudl) with infrastructure, resilience, and media tooling open source projects (Mjolnir, Fargo, HudlFfmpeg, react-native components), but these are engineering libraries, not product SDKs. Hudl's revenue model is SaaS subscriptions for video, analytics, and data packages, plus camera hardware sales and data licensing.

providers.name: LRCLIB
providers.description: LRCLIB provides a free and open lyrics database accessible via a public API. It offers endpoints to search for songs, retrieve lyrics, and obtain metadata such as artists and albums. The service is unauthenticated, CORS-enabled, and includes generous rate limits for anonymous users, with optional registration for higher limits. Documentation is available in Markdown and plain text formats.

providers.name: Mixcloud
providers.description: Music

providers.name: Remix 3
providers.description: Remix (YC W26, "remix-3" in the Y Combinator directory) is a San Francisco AI startup building a consumer social-media content platform under the tagline "Trends, remixed by you." Users connect their accounts and drop in photos, voice notes, or messages, and Remix uses hundreds of parallel AI agents to auto-generate posts in their style — articles, tweets, carousels, and short-form videos, including riffs on trending formats — without manual prompting. The company was founded in 2025 by Sam Kaplan (Harvard CS; early Brex employee). As of this enrichment pass Remix ships a consumer web/mobile product only and publishes no public developer API, SDK, docs, or webhook surface, so this remains an identity-only profile in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: turntable
providers.description: turntable (Turntable Labs) is a consumer social-music company originally surfaced as a portfolio company of slow-ventures and union-square-ventures. The original Turntable.fm social listening service shut down in 2013 and its domain no longer resolves. The lineage lives on at Turntable Labs, which operates two consumer music products - Hangout (a social music-streaming and group-chat app at hangout.fm / hang.fm) and Turntable (a create-share-and-vibe GenAI music experience). No public API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation are published for any of these products - this is a consumer application, not an API provider. Enrichment probes (DNS, HTTP, site fetch) confirmed no developer surface as of 2026-07-21.

providers.name: ArdaBot, Inc.
providers.description: ArdaBot, Inc. builds a suite of AI‑powered applications that let users translate conversations privately, access AI‑enhanced healthcare records, receive personalized tutoring, manage photography portfolios, converse with historical figures, and integrate AI inference across apps via Arda Gateway. All products focus on privacy, on‑device processing, and seamless cross‑app AI experiences.

providers.name: BallerTV
providers.description: BallerTV (Baller, Inc.) is a Pasadena, California sports media company that live streams and provides on-demand replays and highlights of youth and amateur sports, including basketball, volleyball, soccer, lacrosse, softball, and football, from thousands of tournaments and showcases nationwide. Subscribers range from families following athletes to NCAA and professional scouts using the footage for recruiting and scouting. The platform includes a Game Finder for locating events, purchasable athlete highlight reels, and BTVision, an AI-powered ball-tracking streaming technology that improves the basketball viewing experience. BallerTV is a consumer streaming product delivered through its website and iOS/Android apps; it does not publish a public developer API or SDK program. This profile was surfaced as an index-ventures portfolio company and enriched from public web sources.

providers.name: Pic-Time
providers.description: Pic-Time is an online gallery, proofing, and print-sales delivery platform for professional photographers - client galleries, slideshows, an integrated print store, and studio-management integrations. Pic-Time does not publish a public developer API, API reference, or OpenAPI specification. Automation is limited to a Zapier integration (three triggers - New Gallery Visitor, New Order Placed, Main Client Gallery Invite Sent - and one action, Create New Gallery) plus private, bilaterally-arranged partner integrations (HoneyBook, Studio Ninja, Light Blue, StyleCloud, the Pic-Time Connect WordPress plugin) that are not documented for third-party developers. No API keys, endpoints, or SDKs are published for general developer use.

providers.name: Red Ventures
providers.description: Red Ventures is a privately held digital marketing and media holding company headquartered in Fort Mill, South Carolina, operating a portfolio of high-growth consumer comparison, commerce, education, and content businesses including Bankrate, The Points Guy, Lonely Planet, Allconnect, Sage Home Loans, RV Education, and RV Home Client Services. The company combines proprietary technology, data science, and performance marketing to acquire customers on behalf of its brands and partners. It maintains a public GitHub organization of 77 largely-forked internal engineering repositories and a company blog, but publishes no public developer API program: there is no developer portal, API reference, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI/GraphQL contract, first-party SDK, or served /.well-known/ discovery document on any Red Ventures-controlled host.

providers.name: Belkin WeMo
providers.description: Belkin provides a range of consumer electronics accessories, including chargers, power banks, wireless charging stations, and cable adapters. It also offers protective accessories such as screen protectors and phone cases for devices like iPhone, Samsung, Google, and Nintendo Switch. The product lineup extends to audio devices, computer peripherals, and surge protection equipment for home and office use.

providers.name: Rainmaker Live
providers.description: Rainmaker Live is a platform for live streaming, virtual events, and audience engagement. No public REST APIs or developer documentation have been verified as of the latest research. The platform focuses on event management, live streaming delivery, and interactive audience participation for webinars, conferences, and live productions.

providers.name: tagSpace
providers.description: tagSpace is a Spatial AI platform, part of the tagStorm group, that lets creators and brands publish interactive augmented-reality experiences and spatial content anchored to real-world places. Through its create, explore, and publish surfaces, tagSpace offers a creator-economy platform where makers showcase spatial "tags," and its tagAI layer applies AI to spatial content. It markets to brands and enterprises (B2B) with named partners including RTL, Telekom, Telstra, Warner Music Group and others. The public site is a Framer marketing presence; as of this enrichment pass tagSpace exposes no public developer portal, API documentation, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or well-known API metadata. This profile remains an identity-only company record.

providers.name: Contents.com
providers.description: Contents.com is an enterprise agentic AI content platform that lets organizations create, govern, approve, translate, and orchestrate content operations at scale across brands, markets, and teams. The platform combines AI Writer, AI Art, AI Chat, HTML Editor, Brand Voice, and AI Translation with structured approval chains and full auditability, orchestrating model-agnostic generation across providers including Meta, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Mistral for multilingual campaigns, product descriptions, SEO content, newsletters, and investor communications.

providers.name: Dotterel
providers.description: Dotterel Technologies is an Auckland, New Zealand acoustics and audio-hardware company founded in 2015 out of the Callaghan Innovation C-Prize. It began by solving drone noise, building acoustic shrouds, low-noise propellers, and onboard active audio-recording systems for UAVs used in film, security, and noise mapping. That work led to Konos (now marketed as Konos Digital), an 80-element directional MEMS microphone array with a continuously variable 60-300 degree beam width that streams four channels of AES67 / SMPTE ST 2110 audio over a single Power-over-Ethernet cable, targeting film, broadcast, and live-sports production. The microphone exposes a firmware-updatable on-device HTTP control interface (a web page plus a POST control endpoint for beam steering) rather than a public developer web API. Dotterel is backed by Techstars (Adelaide 2017 cohort) and is tracked here as a hardware company; it publishes no public API specification, SDK, or developer portal.

providers.name: MemeChat
providers.description: MemeChat is an Indian consumer social and creator-economy mobile app from MemeChat Private Limited (Memetech), where users make, share, and compete with memes — including a Face Swap AI feature and a MemeChat keyboard — and earn money when their content goes viral. Marketed as a self-reliant ("Atmanirbhar") Indian app that has crossed five million users, it is backed by 500 Global. This API Evangelist profile is a network stub: MemeChat is a consumer application with no public developer API, SDK, or documentation surface discovered at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Podcastpage
providers.description: Podcastpage.io was a podcast website builder that provided programmatic access for managing podcast websites and content. The product is now operating under the Beamly brand (beamly.com) following a rebrand. As of this entry the service does not publish a public OpenAPI specification or open developer documentation, and integration support is provided through customer support and Help Center articles.

providers.name: 2bytes
providers.description: 2bytes Corporation (투바이트) is a South Korean game services and publishing company founded in 2020 in Seoul, providing game localization, QA testing, player support, content marketing, live operations and global launch support to more than 40 game company partners including Pearl Abyss and Kakao Games. The company also builds and operates an H5 (HTML5) game platform that runs in-app without installation, covering platform construction, global H5 game sourcing, localization and live operations, integrated by partner apps through an SDK. Its service brand is 2bytes Play. As of this profile 2bytes publishes no public developer portal, API reference, or machine-readable API contract; the H5 platform SDK is offered through a business contact channel rather than a self-serve developer program.

providers.name: Scratch Music Group
providers.description: Scratch Music Group, founded in 2002, is a leading provider of DJ bookings, education, and event services. Co‑founded by Jam Master Jay of Run DMC, the company runs the Scratch DJ Academy offering beginner to professional curricula, both online and in‑person at locations in New York and Los Angeles. With over 500,000 students taught, 10,000+ DJ events annually, and a network of 7,600+ DJs, Scratch serves brand clients, retailers, hospitality venues, and corporate events worldwide. Their proprietary event platform powers 100,000+ events, delivering scalable solutions and guaranteed paid gigs for graduates. The company also offers equipment discounts and certification tracks, positioning itself as a comprehensive ecosystem for DJ talent and event management.

providers.name: Skool
providers.description: Skool is an all-in-one community platform that combines discussion communities, online courses, live calls, and gamification in a single product, founded by Sam Ovens and popularized in partnership with Alex Hormozi. As of this review, Skool does NOT publish an official public or partner developer REST API. The only official programmatic surface is a Zapier integration, gated to the paid Pro plan, that exposes a small set of triggers and actions via a per-group API key used solely to link a Skool group to Zapier - it is not a general-purpose developer API. All broader "Skool API" offerings found in the wild (Apify actors, docs.skoolapi.com, reverse-engineered clients, Chrome extensions) are unofficial third-party tools built on Skool's undocumented internal endpoints and are not endorsed or supported by Skool. This catalog entry is an honest gated stub: no public API surface is modeled because none is documented.

providers.name: AmpMe
providers.description: AmpMe is a mobile application that synchronizes music playback across multiple smartphones to create a collective, portable sound system. Users connect friends' phones together so their device speakers play the same track in sync, amplifying the audio for parties and gatherings. The app supports streaming sources such as Spotify, YouTube, SoundCloud, and Deezer, and runs natively on iOS and Android. AmpMe was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; it is a consumer mobile product that does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: BMI
providers.description: Broadcast Music, Inc. (BMI) is the largest performing rights organization in the United States, representing songwriters, composers and music publishers. It collects and distributes royalties for public performances of music, offers licensing services to businesses, and provides resources, advocacy, and career development for music creators. BMI also runs programs like Health Connect, Spark, and AI & Copyright initiatives to support its members.

providers.name: DSP Concepts
providers.description: DSP Concepts provides embedded audio processing software and the Audio Weaver platform, enabling developers to integrate advanced audio algorithms into automotive, consumer, and professional audio products. Their solutions include AI‑enhanced audio processing, customizable DSP blocks, and tools for rapid development and deployment across a range of industries. The company emphasizes modular, scalable designs and offers extensive documentation, training, and support for engineers building audio‑centric applications.

providers.name: Kobalt
providers.description: Kobalt Music Group is an independent music rights management and administrative publishing company founded in 2000 by Willard Ahdritz, operating from New York and London. Unlike traditional publishers it administers copyrights rather than owning them, running Kobalt Music Publishing, a neighbouring rights division, and AMRA, the digital-first collection society it acquired in 2014. Royalty and rights processing runs on KTech, the rights and content management platform built to independently serve both Kobalt Music Publishing and AMRA at the scale of billions of music micro-transactions, with songwriters and rightsholders viewing statements and analytics through the authenticated Kobalt Portal. Kobalt publishes no public developer program: a 2026-07-19 probe found no developer portal, no API documentation, no OpenAPI or AsyncAPI description, and no API discovery documents under /.well-known/. Integration is arranged commercially through Kobalt or KTech rather than through a self-service API.

providers.name: Rebel Girls
providers.description: Rebel Girls is a global media and publishing brand that celebrates inspiring stories about girls and women, empowering young audiences through books, a podcast, a YouTube channel, apparel and accessories, activities, and the Rebel Girls Sport program. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. As of this pass Rebel Girls publishes no developer, API, or well-known discovery surface: rebelgirls.com redirects to www.rebelgirls.com and every standard well-known endpoint returns 404, and there are no developer/api subdomains. This profile captures the company's public identity and a live domain-security posture probe; it carries no API artifacts because there is no public API to describe.

providers.name: SoundBetter
providers.description: SoundBetter is an online marketplace that connects musicians and artists with professional audio talent for hire — mixing and mastering engineers, music producers, singers, songwriters, beat makers, and studio session musicians. Clients post jobs or browse curated professional profiles, audition portfolio tracks, and hire and pay through the platform, which handles escrow, milestones, and delivery. The company also operates a storefront (my.soundbetter.com) and a plugins shop (shop.soundbetter.com / Imagine Plugins). SoundBetter was acquired by Spotify in 2019. As of this enrichment pass, SoundBetter publishes a consumer/creator web marketplace but exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery surface; this profile therefore captures company identity and a live domain-security probe rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: REAPER
providers.description: REAPER is a powerful digital audio workstation (DAW) developed by Cockos. It offers a full‑featured, flexible audio production environment used by professionals and hobbyists alike, supporting recording, editing, mixing, and mastering across Windows, macOS, and Linux. REAPER provides unlimited updates, a customizable interface, extensive plugin support, and a 60‑day evaluation period, all without artificial limitations or DRM.

providers.name: Anghami
providers.description: Anghami is a leading music streaming platform in the Middle East and North Africa, offering a vast library of songs, podcasts, and curated playlists. Users can enjoy personalized recommendations, high‑quality audio, and offline listening across multiple devices. The service provides both free ad‑supported and premium subscription tiers, catering to a diverse audience of music lovers and creators.

providers.name: Drone Racing League
providers.description: The Drone Racing League (DRL) is a New York-based professional drone racing property founded in 2015 by Nicholas Horbaczewski, staging first-person-view (FPV) races in which pilots fly identical, league-built quadcopters - the Racer series - through three-dimensional courses in stadiums, arenas and landmark venues at speeds above 80 mph. DRL designs its own racing drones, timing and telemetry hardware, produces and distributes its race broadcasts across NBC, Sky Sports, ProSiebenSat.1 and streaming platforms, and operates the DRL Simulator, an FPV racing game on Steam, PlayStation and Xbox that feeds the Swatch DRL Tryouts esports pipeline used to recruit professional pilots. The company was acquired by Infinite Reality (now Napster) in April 2024. DRL publishes no public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs or machine-readable API specification, and as of the 2026-08-04 enrichment pass its primary web properties (thedroneracingleague.com, drl.io) were not completing a TLS handshake.

providers.name: Fedica
providers.description: Fedica provides a social media analytics platform that schedules posts across 15 social platforms and delivers deep audience insights, including demographics down to city level, location, bot detection, and engagement analytics. It helps brands understand who their audience is and optimize content strategy with comprehensive metrics and reporting.

providers.name: Kuaidian Reading
providers.description: Kuaidian Reading (快点阅读) is a Chinese mobile reading community operated by Beijing Tiantong Interactive Technology Co., Ltd. (Sky Platanus Interactive, 天桐互动), positioning itself as China's first dialogue-based reading app. Instead of long-form web fiction, the platform publishes chat-style novels rendered as character dialogue, which it argues gives clearer characterization, tighter pacing and stronger reader immersion. Content is user-generated at scale — the company claims over 20,000 new novels uploaded daily — and distributed through a decentralized recommendation algorithm rather than editorial merchandising. Social mechanics include barrage-style inline comments, author tipping, and a co-writing mode that lowers the barrier for first-time writers. Authors work in a separate creation console at editor.kuaidianyuedu.com. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of DCM Ventures. As of this enrichment pass Kuaidian Reading publishes no public API, SDK, developer portal, or /.well-known/ discovery surface; it is a consumer-app company with no developer-facing program.

providers.name: Mediaspectrum
providers.description: Mediaspectrum is a cloud-based SaaS provider of multichannel advertising, content management, and publishing software for media companies and publishers. Founded in 2001 and headquartered in Miami, its platform manages the full advertising lifecycle -- proposal generation, packaging, scheduling, rating, workflow, trafficking, optimization, and billing -- alongside an integrated CRM and the ContentWatch content management system spanning print, web, mobile, video, social, and broadcast channels. The company raised a $35.8M investment from Insight Venture Partners in 2013 and counts Gannett, Dow Jones, and Trinity Mirror among its clients. No public API, developer portal, or SDKs are published as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Cover Art Archive
providers.description: Cover Art Archive provides a free, open database of cover art images for music releases, sourced from the MusicBrainz community. It offers a public API that allows developers to retrieve cover art by release or release-group identifiers, supporting JSON and image formats. The service is community‑maintained, aims to enrich music metadata applications, and operates under an open‑source license.

providers.name: Craon
providers.description: Craon (craon.ai) is an AI-native video editing platform where users edit through natural-language chat instead of a traditional timeline. Creators describe their intent in plain language — "make this more cinematic", "build tension before the reveal", "warm golden-hour grade" — and Craon's AI performs the cuts, color grading, pacing, silence removal, scene detection, subtitle generation, and emotional storytelling automatically. It targets content creators, YouTubers, social and short-form creators, filmmakers, and marketing teams who want professional results without timeline experience or color-theory skills, positioning itself as an AI-native alternative to CapCut, Adobe Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve, iMovie, Filmora, Runway, and Descript. Craon is an early-stage company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. The product is a consumer web application with no public developer API; its only machine-facing surface today is a published /llms.txt for AI discovery.

providers.name: Elevate
providers.description: Elevate K‑12 provides live online teaching solutions for K‑12 schools, offering a catalog of live streaming courses across core, elective, and special education subjects. Districts can subscribe to tiered live teaching services, enabling teachers to deliver real‑time instruction, assessments, and support to students remotely. The platform, recently acquired by Fullmind Learning, serves numerous school districts nationwide, emphasizing flexible, high‑quality virtual classroom experiences.

providers.name: InstaAgent
providers.description: InstaAgent is a Y Combinator-backed AI marketing platform that turns a single campaign brief into hundreds of audience-specific creatives. It generates persona-, trend-, and format-grounded ad variants, distributes them across Meta, TikTok, and niche social accounts built for specific audiences, then tests which personas, hooks, formats, and channels drive performance and scales the winners into the next campaign. The company reports serving 500+ clients across 10+ countries with 10x ad variants and 30%+ ROI improvement. InstaAgent operates a marketing product surface only and does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or developer documentation; this profile captures its public identity and domain-security posture.

providers.name: Promptmage
providers.description: Promptmage provides AI‑powered prompt generation and management tools for creators, developers, and enterprises. Their platform offers a library of curated prompts, a prompt marketplace, and APIs to integrate dynamic prompt creation into applications, enabling users to harness generative AI more effectively across content creation, marketing, and software development workflows.

providers.name: Theta EdgeCloud
providers.description: Theta EdgeCloud is a distributed, hybrid AI and video cloud built on the Theta Network blockchain, offering on-demand GPU compute for AI model training, fine-tuning, inference, video transcoding, and live streaming. EdgeCloud aggregates GPU capacity from data-center hyperscaler partners and a global community of Edge Nodes (consumer and enterprise GPUs) into a single dispatchable compute layer addressable via REST, JSON-RPC, and SDK clients. Core services include EdgeCloud AI Services (on-demand model inference APIs for LLMs, image, audio, and multimodal models such as Llama, Stable Diffusion, FLUX, and Whisper; agentic RAG chatbots; GPU-backed Jupyter notebooks; dedicated GPU pod deployments; and AI training with GPU clusters), EdgeCloud Video Services (the Theta Video API for upload, transcoding, livestream ingestion, DRM, NFT-gated playback, and webhooks), EdgeStore (decentralized object storage), and the EdgeCloud Client (an installable node that earns TFUEL for contributing GPU and bandwidth). Developers authenticate with x-api-key tokens issued from the EdgeCloud dashboard, manage deployments programmatically through api.thetaedgecloud.com and the Node.js SDK @thetalabs/theta-edgecloud, and access on-demand model endpoints (also distributed through RapidAPI). The Theta blockchain layer is EVM-compatible with an Ethereum RPC adaptor, supports TNT-20 tokens and NFTs, and underwrites EdgeCloud's payment, rewards, and staking economy through the THETA governance token and TFUEL gas token. Theta operates as Theta Labs, headquartered in San Jose, California.

providers.name: Art19
providers.description: Art19 (ART19, Inc.) is a podcast hosting, distribution, and monetization platform, and an Amazon company. It provides publishers, networks, and enterprises with a content management system for audio, automated RSS feed generation, dynamic ad insertion and targeting through its WarpFeed feed technology, and an embeddable Web Player. The platform serves podcast delivery, analytics, and advertising workflows at scale. Art19 does not currently publish a public developer API, SDK, or documentation portal; its public presence consists of a marketing site, a contact page, a privacy policy, and a system status page tracking CMS, RSS, WarpFeed, and Web Player availability.

providers.name: Barnes & Noble
providers.description: Barnes & Noble is the largest retail bookseller in the United States and the operator of the Nook digital reading platform. Barnes & Noble does not currently publish a public general-purpose developer portal. Trade and affiliate partners integrate through B&N's affiliate program, the B&N Press self-publishing platform for independent authors, EDI-based wholesale channels with publishers, and the Nook content distribution and reading ecosystem.

providers.name: BarterBanner
providers.description: BarterBanner is a network that helps publishers gain new readers by exchanging article placements across participating sites. The service is free to join and operates on an impression‑based credit system, where sites earn credits for displaying others’ content and spend them to have their own articles shown elsewhere. It supports multiple languages, offers a dashboard for tracking impressions and clicks, and emphasizes that no monetary payment is required, only space on the site for exchanged content.

providers.name: IndieFlow
providers.description: IndieFlow is an all-in-one music management platform for independent artists and their managers, positioning itself as a "Shopify for musicians." Made by musicians, it centralizes the business side of an independent music career in one place: distributing releases to 30+ streaming services (Spotify, Apple Music, Tidal, Deezer, TikTok and more), collecting and registering royalties and songwriter/publisher credits with performing rights organizations, managing creative projects and release schedules, promoting music, booking gigs, and handling payments and collaborations. Founded in 2020, the company raised a $4M round led by State of Mind Ventures with participation from Techstars and other investors, and its artist-facing distribution is delivered through a Revelator-powered back end. IndieFlow does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile tracks the company's public web presence.

providers.name: Bonbrain
providers.description: Bonbrain LLC builds AI‑powered mobile applications that transform everyday tasks into seamless digital experiences. Their product suite includes BonPic, an AI photo generator; Pantry Buddy, an AI grocery‑list manager; Proof Buddy, a timestamped photo service for insurance and verification; Decora AI, an interior‑design assistant; and Fast Cleanup, an AI duplicate‑photo remover. The company emphasizes robust engineering, scalable architecture, and a focus on delivering magical, reliable user experiences across its AI‑driven apps.

providers.description: Books
