providers.name: NBC
providers.description: NBC (National Broadcasting Company) is a major American commercial broadcast television network and a subsidiary of Comcast through NBCUniversal. NBC produces news (NBC News, Today), entertainment, late-night, and sports programming (Sunday Night Football, Olympic Games). NBC and parent company NBCUniversal do not publish a public developer portal. Programmatic advertising APIs (NBCUniversal One Platform) and streaming partner integrations (Peacock) are offered only through direct sales relationships rather than self-serve developer signup.

providers.name: Ubiquitous Influence
providers.description: Ubiquitous Influence is a full‑service influencer marketing agency that partners brands with creators across platforms like TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, and X. They provide end‑to‑end campaign management, including strategy, logistics, performance tracking, and paid amplification, delivering transparent and profitable results for clients ranging from startups to large enterprises.

providers.name: Daily Studio
providers.description: Daily Studio is a SaaS platform that helps creators plan, record, and publish video content. It provides a web‑based studio and an iPhone teleprompter, integrates with TikTok, Reels, Shorts, and YouTube, and offers AI‑assisted script generation via connectors for Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini. Users can organize scripts into collections, schedule posts, and review content before publishing, all from a unified workflow.

providers.name: Jaxsta
providers.description: Jaxsta is a music industry data platform that aggregates official metadata from record labels, distributors, and rights owners. The service provides verified artist, release, and credit information to creators, partners, and industry members. As of 2024, Jaxsta entered hibernation under Vinyl Group, pausing commercial operations while preserving its underlying database and technology for future use. The platform remains a valuable source of authoritative music data for integration via APIs and data services.

providers.name: Bustle Digital Group
providers.description: Bustle Digital Group is a digital media company that operates a portfolio of online brands, including Bustle, Elite Daily, Mic, and others. It creates content across lifestyle, news, entertainment, and culture, reaching millions of readers worldwide. The company leverages data-driven storytelling and social media distribution to engage audiences and offers advertising solutions for brands.

providers.name: Curb
providers.description: Curb is a music entertainment company under Word Entertainment, operating record labels, artist management, and related media services. The public website provides information about its catalog, artists, and merchandise, but no public API documentation or developer portal is evident.

providers.name: scraptik-com
providers.description: ScrapTik provides an unofficial TikTok API that delivers creator analytics, video statistics, comments, and search capabilities. It offers data such as follower counts, video performance metrics, comment threads, hashtag trends, and sound usage, accessible via a REST API on RapidAPI, an Apify actor, or an MCP server for AI agents. The service supports pay‑per‑call pricing, custom volume plans, and integrates with platforms like Base for cryptocurrency payments. It is aimed at developers, marketers, and analysts needing public TikTok data without requiring an official TikTok account.

providers.name: Weibo
providers.description: Weibo is a Chinese microblogging platform, often described as the Chinese equivalent of Twitter. It provides a social networking service where users can post, share, and interact with short messages, images, and videos. Weibo offers a range of data APIs for developers to access public posts, user profiles, trends, and analytics, supporting commercial and research use cases. The platform is operated by Sina Corporation and serves hundreds of millions of active users worldwide, making it a significant source of social media data.

providers.name: Balthasar & Speyr
providers.description: Balthasar & Speyr is a dedicated portal offering a curated collection of publications by the renowned theologians Hans Urs von Balthasar and Adrienne von Speyr. The site provides access to books, articles, and scholarly works in both print and electronic formats, serving scholars, students, and anyone interested in contemporary Catholic theology and spirituality. It also features news, events, and resources related to the authors' legacy.

providers.name: Booktrack
providers.description: Booktrack provides immersive audiobook production services, creating original soundtracks, sound design, and synchronized audio for publishers, authors, and studios. Since 2011, they have delivered over 300 immersive titles, leveraging patented technology to enhance the listening experience with multi‑layered soundscapes and Dolby Atmos. Their services include full‑production, post‑production, narration, quality control, and studio facilities, partnering with global publishers such as Penguin Random House and Simon & Schuster.

providers.name: Lunar-X
providers.description: Lunar-X (Lunar X) is a global digital content studio that acquires, develops, and operates creator-driven entertainment brands into globally recognized franchises across animation, educational content, functional music, ecommerce, and live events. Its properties include Economics Explained, Theorist Inc, Music Labs, and Lunar Kids, collectively spanning tens of billions of views and over a hundred million subscribers. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Creandum and added to the API Evangelist network. As a media/content operator it publishes a marketing website and privacy policy but exposes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal.

providers.name: SFX
providers.description: SFX (SFX Entertainment, now operating as LiveStyle, Inc) is a Beverly Hills based global live-events and electronic dance music company. Originally founded by Robert F.X. Sillerman as a roll-up of EDM festival and event brands, the company reorganized as LiveStyle and continues to produce live music experiences, festivals, and fan events under the banner "For the Love of Music." It was surfaced as a portfolio-linked company and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. The company presents a corporate marketing web presence and publishes no public developer, API, or technical integration surface at this time.

providers.name: AI Arena
providers.description: AI Arena is an independent music discovery platform that hosts AI‑created and artist‑submitted tracks. Users can battle songs head‑to‑head, vote, and climb rankings in real‑time playlists. The service emphasizes exposure for emerging creators, offering blind battles, genre‑based playlists, and live events, while storing only links to externally hosted music.

providers.name: Cesure
providers.description: Cesure is a web‑based guitar tab editor that leverages AI transcription to convert audio into editable tablature, standard notation, and piano roll views. Users can collaborate in real time, tune, loop, and export scores as printable PDFs. The platform offers a rich editing experience directly in the browser, supporting audio import, AI‑driven transcription, and various playback features.

providers.name: Printique
providers.description: Printique (An Adorama Company, formerly AdoramaPix) is a professional online photo lab based in Brooklyn, NYC that produces photo prints, fine-art giclee prints, photo books, albums, wall decor (metal, acrylic, canvas, glass, framed, wood), cards, calendars, and photo gifts. Printique does NOT publish a documented public developer or fulfillment API. There is no developer portal, no published REST reference, no API keys, and no OpenAPI definition on the open web. Programmatic and automated ordering is instead delivered through prebuilt partner-platform integrations - a Squarespace integration that syncs products and automates order fulfillment, a PhotoShelter wholesale print-and-product integration for professional photographers, Fundy Designer album integration, and desktop plugins for Adobe Lightroom and Capture One that publish images directly to Printique. A Pro membership tier ($14.95/month or $159.95/year) unlocks tiered wholesale savings, white-label blind shipping, and dedicated support for photography businesses. The logical API surfaces below (catalog, orders, order status) are honestly modeled from Printique's public product, Pro, and integration pages to describe how ordering works conceptually; they are NOT transcribed from any released or documented Printique API. No public endpoints, paths, or request/response schemas are published, so endpointsModeled is true and no endpoint surface has been fabricated beyond these named, integration-delivered capabilities.

providers.name: Accusilicon
providers.description: Accusilicon (Guangzhou Ruixin Microelectronics Co., Ltd. / 广州睿芯微电子有限公司) is a fabless mixed-signal semiconductor company founded in July 2014 and headquartered in the Huangpu district of Guangzhou, China, with additional sites in Xi'an and Shanghai. It designs and sells ultra-low phase noise timing silicon and related analog ICs — XO/VCXO/TCXO and OCXO oscillator chips, clock ICs, crystal-oscillator modules, RF and analog switch ICs, mobile-interface protection ICs, ADC/DAC converters, digital audio processor (DSP) and audio ICs, and spectral image sensor chips — alongside clock stability analyzers and other test and measurement instruments, and ASIC/SoC, module, system and clock custom design services. Its parts are used in smartphones, digital communications and high-speed Ethernet, audio/video and professional audiophile equipment, medical, security, payment and measurement systems. The company is a hardware component supplier: it operates a corporate marketing site in Chinese only and publishes no developer program, developer portal, API documentation, SDK or machine-readable API description of any kind.

providers.name: Creator Stack
providers.description: CreatorStack is a consumer creator-economy platform that helps independent creators own their audience instead of renting it from social networks. Its core product, the "Superclub," lets a creator build a membership community of paying super-fans, capture first-party audience data, and deepen engagement and loyalty that translates into stronger brand sponsorships. A forthcoming Royalty product will let creators share and sell royalties in their future content directly to the top fans who invest early, in exchange for perks and exclusive benefits. Backed by Accel, CreatorStack positions a creator's brand and audience as a true, ownable asset on the internet rather than a rented one.

providers.name: Mozart AI
providers.description: Mozart AI is a generative audio workstation and AI music-creation platform (mozartai.com) that lets musicians compose, produce, and distribute songs using AI-assisted and agentic tools. Rather than generating finished tracks from a single prompt, it operates as a full digital audio workstation built around context-aware stem generation, real-time MIDI suggestions, synth and effects generation, and automated production tasks such as quantization and time-stretching, letting users work at the level of stems, instruments, or individual notes. Founded in 2025 and based in London, the company raised a $6M seed round led by Balderton Capital in February 2026 and reports more than 100,000 artists and over 1 million songs created. The product is delivered as a consumer web and mobile app (built on the ElevenLabs Eleven Music API) and does not currently publish a public developer API.

providers.name: Planetary
providers.description: Planetary is a decentralized, peer-to-peer social networking company built on the Secure Scuttlebutt (SSB) protocol, offering an iOS app for algorithm-free social media where users own and store their data locally with no advertising and no data selling. The team has since migrated its design, app, and philosophy to the Nostr protocol under a new app, nos.social. The project is fully open source, developed in the open on GitHub, and is a portfolio company of Bloomberg Beta. Planetary exposes no commercial REST/HTTP API; its developer surface is the underlying SSB/Nostr protocol documentation (RPC methods, replication, blobs) rather than a hosted web API.

providers.name: Aigist
providers.description: Aigist provides a service to publish HTML or Markdown generated by large language models (LLMs) as shareable links. Users can create live pages with optional passwords and expiry settings, enabling easy distribution of AI-generated content. The platform supports integration with Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini and other LLMs via its MCP client, offering endpoints for publishing, listing, retrieving, updating, and deleting pages.

providers.name: Drop
providers.description: Drop (formerly Massdrop) is a consumer e-commerce brand operated by Corsair that sells limited-edition, community-driven products across mechanical keyboards, audiophile gear, and licensed gaming collaborations (Fallout, Cyberpunk 2077, The Witcher, Call of Duty and others). Founded in San Francisco and backed by Cowboy Ventures and other investors before its acquisition by Corsair, Drop runs a direct-to-consumer storefront at drop.com with a Zendesk-based support helpdesk. It is a retail brand with no public developer API program; this API Evangelist profile tracks it as a company in the network.

The service offers flexible scheduling, Zoom-based instruction, and a range of pricing options. The company’s website presents detailed information about teachers, lesson formats, pricing, and regional availability, positioning itself as a global provider of personalized vocal training.

providers.name: Epic! Creations
providers.description: Epic! Creations, Inc. operates Epic, an award-winning digital reading and learning platform for children twelve and under. The service gives families and educators unlimited access to a library of more than 40,000 books, audiobooks, and learning videos, with reading-level personalization, quizzes, and progress tracking. Epic offers a consumer family subscription and Epic School, a version that is free for teachers and students during the school day via class codes. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Battery Ventures and added to the API Evangelist network. Epic is a business-to-consumer application and does not publish a public developer program, API, or SDK surface.

providers.name: Boots & Bassline
providers.description: Boots & Bassline is a music collective and brand that creates and shares original songs and albums. Their flagship album "All of It Was Ours" features seventeen tracks about friendship, family, love and the open road, available on Spotify and Apple Music. The site offers a listening room, back room, artwork, wallpapers, and a press page, plus contact via hello@bootsandbassline.com.

providers.name: Dom Kozak
providers.description: Dom Kozak is a Director of Programmatic at JCDecaux Middle East in Dubai, leading programmatic out‑of‑home advertising, applied AI initiatives, and hosting the Built for MENA podcast. He is recognized as an Ad Tech Hero 2022 and serves as a judge for the pDOOH Live Awards. His work spans digital out‑of‑home, media buying, and AI‑driven attention measurement, with a strong presence in the MENA advertising ecosystem.

providers.name: Bridgeco
providers.description: BridgeCo Inc. was a fabless semiconductor company founded in 2000 that built networked-audio silicon and software for consumer electronics. Its JukeBlox platform — a system-on-a-chip paired with a software development kit — let wireless speakers, A/V receivers, home-theater systems and docking stations stream music from tablets, smartphones and PCs, and was designed into products from Pioneer, Philips, Denon, Marantz, JBL and Harman/Kardon. Earlybird Venture Capital was the company's first institutional investor in 2000. BridgeCo was acquired by Standard Microsystems Corporation (SMSC) on 19 May 2011 in a deal worth up to $67.5 million, and SMSC was in turn acquired by Microchip Technology on 2 August 2012, where the JukeBlox wireless-audio line was folded into Microchip's portfolio. BridgeCo no longer operates as an independent company and publishes no developer portal, documentation or public API; the bridgeco.com domain today is an unrelated domain-for-sale parking page.

providers.name: Fortunes
providers.description: ForTunes was a Vienna-based mobile music data analytics application for self-publishing and DIY artists, managers, and small labels. The app collected and visualized performance data across Spotify, Apple Music, SoundCloud, YouTube, Instagram, Facebook, and other platforms into a single intelligent feed, with notifications for playlist adds and follower growth, a Spotify playlist recommendation engine, public artist profiles, and team collaboration. Backed by Speedinvest (2018), the company was acquired by Utopia Music in 2023. As of this profile the primary web domain (fortunes.io) no longer resolves and no public developer API, API documentation, or developer portal is published; the product surface is the consumer iOS and Android apps.

providers.name: Frame
providers.description: Frame Technology Corp. was a software company that developed FrameMaker, a structured desktop-publishing and technical-documentation authoring application widely used for long, complex documents. Founded in the 1980s and taken public, Frame Technology was acquired by Adobe Systems in 1995; FrameMaker continues today as an Adobe product. This is a historical/acquired portfolio company of Canaan Partners with no independent developer or API surface of its own.

providers.name: Group Nine Media
providers.description: Group Nine Media was a New York-based digital-media holding company formed in 2016 through the merger of Discovery Digital with the original Group Nine, uniting the news brand NowThis, the animal brand The Dodo, the lifestyle brand Thrillist, and the science brand Seeker under one roof (it later added PopSugar). Backed by Discovery Inc. and venture investor IVP, it built large social-video and branded-content audiences before it was acquired by Vox Media in February 2022 and folded into that portfolio. Group Nine operated as a consumer media publisher, not an API provider: it did not publish a public developer portal, API documentation, SDKs, or any machine-readable API surface, and its groupnine.com domain now resolves to a third-party domain-sale landing page. This profile is retained as a VC-portfolio identity record with no scorable API artifacts.

providers.name: Joyride
providers.description: Joyride was a mobile audio service that made driving more fun and more interesting, offering an in-car audio/entertainment experience for drivers and passengers. Founded by Jeff Chen (co-founder & CEO) and James Zhang (co-founder & CTO), the company raised a seed round from Cowboy Ventures and was subsequently acquired by Google, marking a successful exit. As a consumer mobile application it exposed no public developer API surface, and the product is no longer independently operated following the acquisition. This profile is retained in the API Evangelist network for portfolio-graph completeness rather than as an active API provider.

providers.name: Locker Room *
providers.description: Locker Room was a live-audio social app for sports fans built by Betty Labs, a seed-stage startup backed by GV, Lightspeed Venture Partners, and Precursor Ventures. Launched in October 2020, it let insiders and fans hold real-time voice conversations about sports. Betty Labs and Locker Room were acquired by Spotify in March 2021 and folded into Spotify Greenroom / Spotify Live, which Spotify has since discontinued. Locker Room no longer operates as an independent product and exposes no public developer API or portal; this profile is retained as a GV portfolio lead in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Simply Measured
providers.description: Simply Measured was a Seattle-based social media analytics and reporting platform, founded in 2010 and backed by Trinity Ventures, that measured brand performance across Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, LinkedIn and other social channels. It was acquired by Sprout Social in December 2017 and its product, brand, and developer surface were sunset and folded into Sprout Social. The simplymeasured.com domain now 301-redirects to sproutsocial.com and no independent Simply Measured API, developer portal, or documentation remains online. This record is retained as a defunct/acquired portfolio-lead marker; there is no live API surface to enrich.

providers.name: Spext Labs
providers.description: Spext (Spext Labs) is an AI-powered audio and video editing platform that lets users edit recordings by trimming an auto-generated transcript rather than a waveform — a text-first "recording management system" for podcasts, interviews and other spoken-word media. Backed by 500 Global, the company operates from a Framer-hosted marketing site (spext.co) and a web application (app.spext.co). As of this enrichment pass Spext exposes no public developer surface — no documented API, developer portal, SDKs, OpenAPI, or well-known discovery endpoints were found; the profile is retained as a network company record.

providers.name: Wiley
providers.description: A global publishing and education company providing research, professional development, and learning solutions. Publishes peer-reviewed journals, textbooks, and digital content across science, technology, medicine, social science, and business.

providers.name: contentbox
providers.description: ContentBox is a blockchain infrastructure company for the digital content industry, built by the team behind Castbox, a global podcast platform serving millions of users across 135 countries. ContentBox aims to give the industry three things: a shared content pool, a shared user pool, and a unified, token-based payout system. Its products include BOX Payout (a blockchain multi-party payment system), BOX Passport (blockchain identity and attribution across applications), and BOX Unpack (a turn-key platform for content creators). The foundation publishes open-source blockchain infrastructure (boxd) and first-party developer SDKs in JavaScript, Python, and Java through its BOXFoundation GitHub organization. Backed by Qiming Venture Partners.

providers.name: Storytree
providers.description: Storytree Inc. is a Palo Alto consumer photo company, backed by 500 Global, that operates SimplePrints (simpleprints.com, formerly getsimpleprints.com) — a mobile-first service that turns the photos on your phone into physical products: layflat and mini photo books, canvas prints, metal prints and metal desk prints, photo cards, and wall calendars. The app pulls images directly from the phone with no exporting or reformatting, and the business adds a referral program, promotional discounts, and a schools program. SimplePrints is a business-to-consumer mobile app and does NOT publish a developer API, SDKs, OpenAPI, or a developer portal. The one machine-consumable surface it exposes is a Wix-hosted llms.txt and a generic Wix Site MCP endpoint for agentic access to public site content (business details, site search, and a bridge to Wix business-solution APIs).

providers.name: Artiphon
providers.description: Artiphon is a Nashville-based music technology company that designs smart, portable musical instruments for everyday creativity. Its products, including the Instrument 1, Orba, Orba 2, Orba 3, and Chorda, combine strumming, tapping, sliding, and looping into palm-sized MIDI controllers and synthesizers, paired with companion apps that let anyone make beats, loop sounds, and explore music anywhere. Artiphon sells direct and through retailers such as Guitar Center and Sweetwater. It does not currently publish a public developer API; this profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network as a consumer-hardware company reference.

providers.name: Lily Camera
providers.description: The domain lily.camera currently serves "Lily Camera", a consumer-facing marketplace that connects clients with certified drone pilots for aerial photography and videography across real estate, events, agriculture, construction, and media production. It is a client-rendered single-page application: every requested path returns the same HTML shell, and the routes defined in its JavaScript bundle cover browsing pilots and drones, comparisons, bookings, messaging, a pilot dashboard, and a drone raffle. There is no public API, no developer portal, no documentation, no OpenAPI or other machine-readable specification, no SDKs, and no /.well-known discovery surface. The site is built on Lovable (GPT Engineer), monetized with Google AdSense, and backed by a hosted Supabase project. No API artifacts could be harvested because the provider publishes none.

providers.name: BandLab
providers.description: BandLab is a cloud-based music creation and social platform where musicians and fans make, collaborate on, publish, and discover music. It pairs a free browser- and mobile-based digital audio workstation (Mix Editor) with a social network for creators, plus sample packs, mastering, distribution, and community features. Part of BandLab Technologies (which also owns Cakewalk/SONAR and other music brands), it is backed by Prosus Ventures. No public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or official client SDK was found during enrichment; the GitHub organization publishes only internal engineering tooling (eslint/stylelint configs, audio libraries). This profile is a company identity record awaiting a documented API surface.

providers.name: Bjstudios
providers.description: Bjstudios is a Belgian eventsupport and live‑streaming technology partner offering LED wall rentals, live streaming services, and event production solutions. The company operates a Wix‑based website (bjstudios.be) showcasing its services, contact information, and portfolio. It appears to focus on corporate events, concerts, and media productions, providing technical expertise and equipment for visual displays and streaming.

providers.name: Callisto Media
providers.description: Callisto Media Inc. was a data-driven nonfiction book publisher founded in 2011 by chief executive Benjamin Wayne, operating from 1955 Broadway in Oakland, California (earlier Emeryville) and 220 West 19th Street in New York. It built a publishing model around demand signals rather than editorial instinct — mining point-of-sale data, search volume and category gaps to decide which instructional titles to commission, then matching each topic to a subject-matter author. Its primary imprint was Rockridge Press, best known for diet-, appliance- and condition-specific cookbooks and health titles, alongside the Callisto Kids line of pre-K through grade 12 workbooks, STEM, history and biography titles; the company said it had reached more than 50 million customers and ranked among the top fifteen US publishers by unit sales. It raised venture funding from 137 Ventures in 2017, then contracted sharply — cutting 35 percent of staff in July 2022 and a further 200 roles that October — and on 9 May 2023 its publishing assets were acquired by the independent publisher Sourcebooks in a deal funded by Penguin Random House, with Simon & Schuster Distribution Services continuing to distribute the titles. The brand now trades as Callisto Publishing, a Sourcebooks imprint: callistomedia.com 301-redirects to callistopublishing.com, which 301-redirects again to sourcebooks.com/callisto (chain verified 2026-08-02). Callisto Media is a consumer publishing business, not a software vendor, and has no public API surface. Probes on 2026-08-02 against callistomedia.com, www.callistopublishing.com and www.sourcebooks.com returned no machine-readable contract: /openapi.json, /swagger.json and /.well-known/ai-plugin.json all 404, /.well-known/agent-card.json and /.well-known/agent.json both 404 (no A2A agent card), and every other probed path answered with the Sourcebooks single-page Magento storefront shell rather than a document. There is no developer portal, no GitHub organization (callistomedia, callisto-media and rockridgepress all 404 on the GitHub API), no published SDK on npm or PyPI, and no llms.txt.

providers.name: Playback
providers.description: Playback (playback.tv) is a mobile-first live streaming platform backed by Khosla Ventures, where creators broadcast live streams, audiences watch and interact in real time, and streamers earn through the platform's monetization program. The consumer product is organized around streaming, watching, earning, and community guidelines. As of this enrichment pass Playback publishes a consumer web/app experience and a Notaku-powered help center but exposes no public developer API, OpenAPI specification, SDK, or documented developer surface; this profile therefore carries identity and domain-security signal only.

providers.name: Viacom
providers.description: Viacom was an American mass media conglomerate that merged with CBS Corporation in December 2019 to form ViacomCBS (later rebranded as Paramount Global). The combined entity, which included brands such as CBS, MTV, Nickelodeon, Comedy Central, BET, Paramount Pictures, Showtime, and Paramount+, was subsequently acquired by Skydance Media and ceased to exist as an independent public company in August 2025. Viacom maintained open source software through its GitHub organization (ViacomInc), including tools for Roku channel development, tvOS UI components, and broadcast calendar utilities. No public external developer API program was offered.

providers.name: DIVE studios
providers.description: DIVE Studios is a global K-entertainment media platform that produces original shows, podcasts, and short-form social content, reaching over 135M Gen Z and Millennial fans and 5B+ lifetime views. The company operates two commercial arms: DIVE Media, which sells advertising and branded content across its podcast, video, and social network, and DIVE Agency (DIVE X), which builds creator, influencer, and celebrity marketing campaigns for global brands connecting with K-culture audiences. It publishes an llms.txt describing its pages but exposes no public developer API, SDK, or portal. Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company and profiled in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: USA TODAY
providers.description: A major American daily national newspaper and digital news platform owned by Gannett. One of the most widely circulated newspapers in the United States covering news, sports, entertainment, and lifestyle topics.

providers.name: Veritiv
providers.description: Veritiv is a North American business-to-business distributor of packaging, facility solutions, print, and publishing products. Formed in July 2014 through the merger of International Paper's xpedx division with Unisource Worldwide, Veritiv operated as a publicly traded company on the New York Stock Exchange until it was acquired and taken private by Clayton, Dubilier & Rice (CD&R) in November 2023 in a transaction valued at approximately $2.3 billion. The company is headquartered in Sandy Springs, Georgia, and operates roughly 125 distribution centers across the United States and Mexico. Veritiv does not publish any public developer APIs, OpenAPI specifications, SDKs, or a developer portal — its commercial surface is built around sales reps, account managers, and large-account customer portals rather than a programmable API.

providers.name: Changba
providers.description: Changba (唱吧) is a Chinese mobile karaoke platform offering a large community for singing, sharing performances, and discovering music. The service provides a mobile app across iOS, Android, and Windows Phone, featuring millions of high‑quality backing tracks, user‑generated recordings, live streaming, and social interaction. It operates under Beijing CoolTech Technology Co., Ltd., with a focus on music entertainment and user‑generated content, and maintains a comprehensive website changba.com that showcases its features, licensing, and corporate information.

providers.name: Aiva
providers.description: AIVA (Artificial Intelligence Virtual Artist) is an AI music generation platform that composes original music across more than 250 styles in seconds. Musicians, content creators, and studios generate tracks from prompts or from uploaded audio and MIDI influences, build custom style models, edit the resulting compositions, and export to MP3, MIDI, and WAV. Paid plans add higher download limits, longer tracks, social monetization rights, and full copyright ownership. AIVA is a consumer- and creator-facing product; as of this enrichment pass it publishes no public developer API, SDKs, or /.well-known discovery documents.

providers.name: Arcturusstudio
providers.description: Arcturusstudio, operating as Arcturus Studio, delivers real‑time 3D volumetric video of sports events using computer vision and AI. Their platform enables broadcasters, teams, leagues, and venues to provide immersive, interactive experiences across 2D broadcast, social media, and AR/VR devices. The company also offers data products derived from player and game analytics, supporting coaches and analysts with actionable insights.

providers.name: Cassie Hour
providers.description: cassiehour-com is a company surfaced via the API Evangelist harvest backlog (source: mcp-registry) and added to the network as a stub for full-pipeline profiling.

providers.name: CreatorDAO
providers.description: CreatorDAO supports content creators through funding, bespoke tooling, and training, backing a roster of YouTube and social channels ranging from tens of thousands to millions of subscribers. It operates a decentralized autonomous organization model with an on-chain creator token, promoting its creator app (district.xyz) and community channels rather than a developer platform. Surfaced as a portfolio company of a16z and Initialized Capital, CreatorDAO publishes no public API, developer documentation, or API specifications as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Audio Up Media
providers.description: Audio Up Media is a Los Angeles based podcast studio, music company and audio entertainment network founded in 2020 by Jared Gutstadt, the founder of Jingle Punks. The company develops and produces scripted and unscripted audio series, original music IP and branded audio campaigns, and adapts that intellectual property into television, film and live formats. Its catalog includes scripted titles such as Strawberry Spring, Make It Up As We Go, Where the Bodies Are Buried and Maejor Frequency, alongside branded case-study work for consumer brands. Audio Up is a content studio rather than a software platform: it publishes a marketing site and distributes its shows through third-party podcast platforms, and does not operate a developer program, public API, SDK or machine-readable specification of its own.

providers.name: DataSift (MediaSift Inc.)
providers.description: DataSift (MediaSift Inc.) was a pioneering social data platform that provided real-time and historical access to social media firehoses (Twitter, Facebook Topic Data, and more) through its CSDL filtering language and its Push, Historics, and Managed Sources REST APIs. Founded in 2007 and backed by Insight Partners and others, the company was acquired by Meltwater in 2019; the datasift.com domain now redirects to meltwater.com and the standalone DataSift developer platform and APIs have been discontinued. Official first-party client SDKs for Python, Ruby, PHP, Java, and Node.js remain published on public package registries under the datasift GitHub organization as historical artifacts.

providers.name: ESPN
providers.description: ESPN, the worldwide leader in sports broadcasting, provides comprehensive coverage of live events, news, scores, and analysis across a multitude of sports. Through its digital platforms, ESPN delivers real-time updates, video highlights, and in-depth articles to fans globally. The company also offers a suite of APIs that enable developers to integrate sports data, media content, and interactive features into applications, enhancing user engagement with timely and accurate sports information.

providers.name: Headgum
providers.description: Headgum is an American comedy podcast network founded in 2015 by Marty Michael, Amir Blumenfeld, and Jake Hurwitz, with studios in Los Angeles and New York. It produces and distributes premium comedy and entertainment podcasts including Doughboys, Not Another D&D Podcast, Dead Eyes, Hey Riddle Riddle, and Why Won't You Date Me?, and operates Gumball, a host-read podcast and YouTube advertising marketplace that lets brands buy ads directly from creators. Headgum is a portfolio company of Union Square Ventures. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; as of this pass Headgum publishes no public developer API, SDK, or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Openwhyd
providers.description: Download curated playlists of streaming tracks (YouTube, SoundCloud, etc...)

providers.name: Twenty-First Century Fox
providers.description: Twenty-First Century Fox was an American multinational mass media corporation that operated film, television, and cable assets before being largely acquired by The Walt Disney Company in 2019. Its remaining broadcasting and news assets continued under Fox Corporation. The company no longer exists as an independent entity and did not expose public developer APIs.

providers.name: ByteDance
providers.description: ByteDance is a global technology company founded in 2012 and headquartered in Beijing, operating across roughly 120 cities with more than 150,000 employees. It builds content, creativity, and productivity platforms powered by machine learning, including TikTok and Douyin (short-form video), Toutiao (news aggregation), CapCut (video editing), Lark/Feishu (enterprise collaboration), Pico (virtual reality), and the Volcano Engine cloud and AI platform. ByteDance maintains an active open source presence on GitHub with 400+ public repositories spanning AI agent frameworks, infrastructure, and media tooling. It was surfaced in the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of altimeter-capital, coatue, ggv-capital, hongshan, idg-capital, softbank-vision-fund, and tiger-global.

providers.name: Hungama
providers.description: Hungama (Hungama Digital Media Entertainment Pvt. Ltd.) is an Indian digital entertainment company operating a video-on-demand and audio OTT platform. Hungama.com offers trending web series, popular movies, Hungama Originals, music, podcasts, audiobooks, and audio stories across Hindi, Bollywood, Punjabi, and regional Indian content. The company was surfaced as a portfolio company of Bessemer Venture Partners and added to the API Evangelist network. Hungama publishes a public LLM Access Policy (llms.txt) governing how AI systems may crawl, summarize, and reference its content, but exposes no public developer API or documentation.
